# Songwriting S1, the Sheet: Implementation Plan

> **For Claude:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task.

**Goal:** Build milestone S1 of [2026-10-01-songwriting-design.md](2026-10-01-songwriting-design.md): a Songs library
and a song sheet - lyrics in sections, chord names over their words as scale degrees, key and Transpose, a Chords tab,
hearing a chord, autosave, and Open in Progression both ways.

**Architecture:** A song is one ProseMirror document. Its chord atoms carry the progression page's own `ChordSlot`, so a
section's progression is derived from the words rather than stored beside them, and a key change re-spells every chord
from its degree. Pure modules hold every rule - naming, parsing, the schema, the commands, the palette, the merge back
from the progression page - and are named for what they return; the components host the editor, and the stores keep
songs in IndexedDB and the hand-off in the session.

**Tech Stack:** Angular 21 standalone, TypeScript 5.9 strict, RxJS 7.8, ProseMirror (model 1.25, state 1.4, view 1.42,
history, keymap, commands, transform, inputrules), Tone.js 15 through the progression page's audio seam, IndexedDB,
Jasmine/Karma.

## Before you start

**Worktree.** Everything happens in `.worktrees/songwriting` on `feature/songwriting-s1`, from `590a09e`: `main` at
`dfc5feb` - the GP milestone merged - plus the songwriting design. Baseline there: **3,777 specs, 0 failures**.

**Read first:** the design's Parts 1, 2, 6 and 8; `CLAUDE.md`; and, for any name this plan uses from the progression
page, `models/progression.model.ts`, `services/progression-edit.ts` (`createDegreeSlot`, `regenerateSlot`),
`services/progression-chord-names.ts`, `services/progression-recognise.ts` and `services/progression-vocabulary.ts`.

**Running specs** (from `client/`). One file, or several with one `--include` each:

```bash
npx ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless --include=src/app/services/song-chord-parse.spec.ts
```

Everything:

```bash
npx ng test --watch=false --browsers=ChromeHeadless 2>&1 | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[mAK]//g' | grep -E "FAILED$|TOTAL" | grep -v Executed
```

Karma pins the debugging port, so run one Karma at a time.

**Type-checking** (from `client/`): `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit`, then `npx tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json --noEmit`.
Run both: the app config excludes specs, and the spec config leaves out any file no spec imports. A template error only
shows in a build: `npx ng build --configuration development`.

**Commits.** `<type>: <description>`, and every message ends with a blank line and
`Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Never commit `client/yarn.lock`: npm rewrites it, a checkout
rewrites its line endings, and nothing in this plan changes it - put it back with `git checkout -- client/yarn.lock`.

**House style.** Read `CLAUDE.md`: pure derivations are named for what they return; comments explain why, generously; 1000
lines per file at most; standalone OnPush components; `takeUntil` for subscriptions; CSS custom properties, in
component-scoped styles - and ProseMirror's own DOM, which component styles do not reach, styled under `:host ::ng-deep`
and a class the component owns; no `!` assertion in application code without a reason given.

**How the code blocks are marked.** Every block that changes a file is preceded by an HTML comment the rendered plan
hides: `<!-- apply: create PATH -->` (write the whole file), `<!-- apply: find PATH -->` followed by
`<!-- apply: replace PATH -->` (exact text, which occurs exactly once in the file as the earlier blocks of the task have
left it; line endings are the file's own, compared as LF), and `<!-- apply: delete PATH -->`. Read them as
instructions; they are also what the proof below applied, mechanically and in order.

## Corrections to the design, found while building it

The design was written before any of this code. Building it disproved or refined these readings; each task below is
written to the corrected version, and Task J.1 records them in the design doc.

1. **The progression types live in `models/progression.model.ts`**, not `composer.model.ts`; only `TimeSignature` is
   the composer's.
2. **Nothing auditioned a single chord.** Part 3 says the sheet plays a chord "the voicing the palette auditions today";
   the progression page plays only whole progressions, through `Tone.Transport`. `ToneApi` gains `now()` and
   `ProgressionPlayerService` gains `audition(notes, seconds, tempo)`: a stab of the slot's own notes on the existing
   chain, released before the next, never touching the transport. Tempo is an argument because a note's length is in
   beats. A chord placed from the Chords tab sounds as it lands, behind a "Play chords as I place them" preference
   (Task F.1).
3. **`chordVocabulary` has no diatonic row.** The palette built its seven triads itself, and nothing built sevenths.
   That code moves into `progression-vocabulary.ts` as `diatonicChordsOf(key, scale, extent)`, the palette maps over it
   unchanged, and the Chords tab asks it for extent 3 and 7 (Task E.1).
4. **`chordName` writes `A min` and `C Maj`.** Lead-sheet names (`Am`, `Cmaj7`, `Bø7`, `F/A`) come from a fourth suffix
   table beside the other three, filled in the same pass, so a lead-sheet name and the progression page's name can
   never disagree about which chord a degree is (Task A.1).
5. **Nothing read a chord typed by name.** The recogniser reads notes. The new parser reads a root and a figure, writes
   it on the degree its *letter* names (`F#` in C is ♯IV, `Gb` is ♭V, each printed back as typed), and refuses with a
   reason anything the model cannot hold - a slash bass that is not a chord tone above all, which `expressInKey` would
   have silently dropped (Task A.1).
6. **The progression page has no key picker**; its key comes from the circle of fifths. The song has its own - tonic
   and a scale that can build chords - and, unlike the progression page, refuses a key that cannot build chords, since
   the song owns its key and no degree can be written in a pentatonic one (Tasks B.2, D.2).
7. **`rekey` was a method needing a store.** Its body is extracted as the pure `rekeyedSlot`; the method delegates, and
   the song re-keys every chord through it in one transaction - so a chord hand-voiced on the progression page keeps
   its pitches and is re-numbered, as there (Task B.2).
8. **ProseMirror needs every attribute of a required node to have a default.** A section's id defaults to null; the
   id plugin gives every null or repeated id a fresh one in the same dispatch, and stored songs with one are refused.
   That plugin, not `transformPasted`, renews pasted ids - prosemirror-view runs `transformPasted` before it knows a
   drag is a move (Task B.1).
9. **`[` cannot both open the chord field and start `[Chorus]`.** On a line with anything on it, `[` opens the field
   and is never typed, and the field takes a closing `]` as Enter - so `[Am]Wondering [F]where` typed straight through
   works. On an empty line `[` is typed; the bracket rule then reads its contents as a chord when they are one (`[G]`,
   `[IV]`) and as a section otherwise (`[Chorus]`, `[Amen]`) (Tasks B.2, D.3).
10. **ProseMirror selects an atom on a modified arrow key.** Beside a chord, Ctrl/Alt/Shift arrows selected the chord
    instead of moving, and a second Alt+arrow then *moved* it. A key handler now steps past the chords and lets the
    browser make its own word jump or extension (Task H.1).
11. **A chord name keeps zero width, but lines are taller.** The design pictured names above each line. A wrapped line
    needs room above every row, and padding that resolves a collision can itself move a chord to the next row - so the
    lyric line-height reserves the room, and spacing is measured from no padding each time, so measuring twice gives
    the same layout (Task E.2).
12. **Open in Progression keeps the link in the session.** The progression page holds its document in memory only, so
    a reload during a hand-off would have lost both the section's edits and the user's own progression. The link, the
    section's latest progression and any returns not yet taken survive a reload in `sessionStorage`. The return is a
    three-way merge against the progression that was sent, so chords placed on the sheet meanwhile survive; `adopt` on
    the progression page is guarded so the circle's key never re-keys the section; and a section deleted meanwhile
    offers its chords as a new section rather than dropping them (Task G.1).
13. **Display choices are the viewer's**, not the song's: names or numerals, lyric size, the panel, playing on place
    live in `localStorage` through `SongSheetPreferencesService`, out of the document, its history and its save
    (Tasks D.2, E.1, F.1).
14. **Autosave is compare-and-swap.** A save is refused when the stored revision is not the one this page loaded - two
    tabs never silently overwrite each other - and there is no timed retry, since IndexedDB's failures do not clear by
    themselves. Changes wait 800 ms after the last one, and never more than 5 s while typing continues (Task C.1).
15. **A key is shown as the progression page shows it**, "C Ionian (Major)", not "C major": a song's key may be any scale
    that builds chords (Task D.1).
16. **A secondary dominant is numbered as the sheet prints it** (A7 in C is `VI7`), since a chord atom stores no target
    to write a slash against; the vocabulary's `V/ii` is kept as a caption under the cell (Task E.1).

## Phase A: Chord names, both ways

The words a sheet uses for a chord, and reading one back.

### Task A.1: Lead-sheet chord names, and reading a chord typed by name or numeral

Two pure modules the rest of S1 stands on. `leadSheetNameOf` names a degree the way a chord sheet does
(`Am`, `Bb7`, `F/A`, `Bø7`) from the same identity `chordName` reads, so the two names can never describe different
chords; `numeralOf` re-exports the progression page's numeral. `chordFromText` reads a name or a numeral in a key and
returns the degree, or a refusal a user can act on.

The parser writes a name on the degree its letter names, through the recogniser's `atDegree`, now exported; it falls
back to `expressInKey` only past a double accidental. Its figure grammar reads everything the namer prints and the
catalogue's symbols, and its specs sweep every chord the model can build, by name and by numeral, pinning the few
classes that read back under another name.

**Files** (under `client/src/app/` unless given in full):
- Create: `services/song-chord-names.spec.ts`, `services/song-chord-names.ts`, `services/song-chord-parse.spec.ts`, `services/song-chord-parse.ts`
- Modify: `services/progression-chord-names.ts`, `services/progression-recognise.ts`

**Step 1: The failing specs.**

`client/src/app/services/song-chord-names.spec.ts`, new:

<!-- apply: create client/src/app/services/song-chord-names.spec.ts -->
```ts
import { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey, createDegreeSlot } from '../models/progression.model';
import { MusicTheoryService } from './music-theory.service';
import { chordName, romanNumeral } from './progression-chord-names';
import { ChordExtent, effectiveChord, isHeptatonic } from './progression-harmony';
import { chordRootName } from './progression-spelling';
import { leadSheetNameOf, numeralOf } from './song-chord-names';

/**
 * The sheet's chord names, checked against how a lead sheet prints them.
 *
 * Every expected name here was worked out by hand before it was written down:
 * the module's whole claim is that it prints what a chart prints, so a fixture
 * read off its own output would be testing nothing. The intervals are written
 * out rather than looked up, on the `progression-spelling.spec.ts` precedent;
 * the one sweep at the bottom asks the service for its scales because its
 * question is about all of them.
 */
const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];
const AEOLIAN = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10];
const HARMONIC_MINOR = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11];

const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const G_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 7, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const F_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 5, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: false };
const E_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 4, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const E_FLAT_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 3, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: false };
const B_FLAT_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 10, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: false };
const A_MINOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 9, scaleId: 'aeolian', preferSharps: false };

/**
 * A degree as a slot really holds one, with the given fields over it.
 *
 * Built through `createDegreeSlot` so the fixture carries whatever a fresh slot
 * carries, as `progression-spelling.spec.ts` does.
 */
function chord(shape: Partial<ChordDegree> & { degree: number }): ChordDegree {
  const slot = createDegreeSlot(shape.degree, 0);
  if (slot.harmony.kind !== 'degree') throw new Error('unreachable');
  return { ...slot.harmony.degree, ...shape };
}

describe('leadSheetNameOf', () => {
  describe('in C major', () => {
    const named = (shape: Partial<ChordDegree> & { degree: number }): string =>
      leadSheetNameOf(chord(shape), C_MAJOR, IONIAN);

    it('writes a major triad as its root alone', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 0 })).toBe('C');
      expect(named({ degree: 4 })).toBe('G');
    });

    it('writes a minor triad with a lower-case m', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 5 })).toBe('Am');
      expect(named({ degree: 1 })).toBe('Dm');
    });

    it('writes the diminished and augmented triads with the signs the progression page uses', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 6 })).toBe('B°');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, quality: 'augmented' })).toBe('C+');
    });

    it('writes the four diatonic sevenths as a chart does', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 7 })).toBe('Cmaj7');
      expect(named({ degree: 4, extent: 7 })).toBe('G7');
      expect(named({ degree: 5, extent: 7 })).toBe('Am7');
    });

    it('writes the half-diminished seventh with ø, which is what chordName writes', () => {
      const half = chord({ degree: 6, extent: 7 });

      expect(leadSheetNameOf(half, C_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('Bø7');
      expect(chordName('B', effectiveChord(IONIAN, half))).toBe('Bø7');
    });

    it('writes the other seventh shapes', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 6, extent: 7, quality: 'diminished7' })).toBe('B°7');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 7, quality: 'minorMajor7' })).toBe('CmMaj7');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 7, quality: 'augmented7' })).toBe('C+7');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 7, quality: 'augmentedMajor7' })).toBe('C+maj7');
    });

    it('writes a borrowed chord on the letter its numeral names', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 6, alter: -1, quality: 'major' })).toBe('Bb');
      expect(named({ degree: 6, alter: -1, quality: 'dominant7', extent: 7 })).toBe('Bb7');
      expect(named({ degree: 5, alter: -1, quality: 'major' })).toBe('Ab');
      expect(named({ degree: 3, alter: 1, quality: 'minor' })).toBe('F#m');
    });

    it('writes a secondary dominant by its own root', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 1, quality: 'dominant7', extent: 7 })).toBe('D7');
    });

    it('writes the suspensions last', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 4, suspension: 'sus4' })).toBe('Gsus4');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, suspension: 'sus2' })).toBe('Csus2');
      expect(named({ degree: 4, extent: 7, suspension: 'sus4' })).toBe('G7sus4');
      expect(named({ degree: 4, extent: 9, suspension: 'sus4' })).toBe('G9sus4');
    });

    it('writes the added-tone chords', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 7, quality: 'major6' })).toBe('C6');
      expect(named({ degree: 5, extent: 7, quality: 'minor6' })).toBe('Am6');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 7, quality: 'add9' })).toBe('Cadd9');
      expect(named({ degree: 5, extent: 7, quality: 'minorAdd9' })).toBe('Amadd9');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 9, quality: 'major6' })).toBe('C6/9');
    });

    it('writes ninths, elevenths and thirteenths at the height they reach', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 9, quality: 'dominant7' })).toBe('C9');
      expect(named({ degree: 4, extent: 9 })).toBe('G9');
      expect(named({ degree: 1, extent: 11 })).toBe('Dm11');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 13 })).toBe('Cmaj13');
      expect(named({ degree: 4, extent: 13 })).toBe('G13');
    });

    it('writes the alterations the model can pin, ascending after the height', () => {
      const flatNine = { ninth: -1 as const, eleventh: null, thirteenth: null };
      const sharpEleven = { ninth: null, eleventh: 1 as const, thirteenth: null };

      expect(named({ degree: 4, extent: 9, extensions: flatNine })).toBe('G7b9');
      expect(named({ degree: 0, extent: 11, extensions: sharpEleven })).toBe('Cmaj9#11');
      expect(named({ degree: 4, extent: 9, extensions: { ...flatNine, ninth: 1 } })).toBe('G7#9');
    });

    it('writes an inversion as a slash over the note in the bass', () => {
      expect(named({ degree: 3, inversion: 1 })).toBe('F/A');
      expect(named({ degree: 3, inversion: 2 })).toBe('F/C');
      expect(named({ degree: 4, extent: 7, inversion: 3 })).toBe('G7/F');
    });

    it('marks a chord with no name the way chordName does, rather than guessing', () => {
      // A diminished triad has no suspended symbol: see `SUSPENDED_FIGURES`.
      const suspended = chord({ degree: 6, suspension: 'sus4' });

      expect(leadSheetNameOf(suspended, C_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('B?');
      expect(chordName('B', effectiveChord(IONIAN, suspended))).toBe('B?');
    });
  });

  describe('spelling', () => {
    it('follows the key: sharps in G, flats in F', () => {
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 6 }), G_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('F#°');
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 2 }), G_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('Bm');
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 3 }), F_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('Bb');
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 4, extent: 7 }), E_FLAT_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('Bb7');
    });

    it("spells a displaced root by its degree's letter, not by preference", () => {
      // B flat major's ♭II is a C flat: the second letter above B.
      const neapolitan = chord({ degree: 1, alter: -1, quality: 'major' });
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(neapolitan, B_FLAT_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('Cb');
    });

    it('spells the slash bass on the letter its place in the chord names', () => {
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 0, inversion: 1 }), E_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('E/G#');
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 4, extent: 7, inversion: 1 }), E_FLAT_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('Bb7/D');
      const flatSix = chord({ degree: 5, alter: -1, quality: 'major', inversion: 1 });
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(flatSix, C_MAJOR, IONIAN)).toBe('Ab/C');
    });

    it("names a mode's degrees as that mode builds them", () => {
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 6 }), A_MINOR, AEOLIAN)).toBe('G');
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 1, extent: 7 }), A_MINOR, AEOLIAN)).toBe('Bø7');
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 4, extent: 7 }), A_MINOR, HARMONIC_MINOR)).toBe('E7');
      expect(leadSheetNameOf(chord({ degree: 2 }), A_MINOR, HARMONIC_MINOR)).toBe('C+');
    });
  });

  /**
   * The name's identity comes from where `chordName`'s does, so the two can
   * never disagree about which chord a degree is: the same root, and the same
   * refusal. Only the suffix differs, and that is the one table this module adds.
   */
  it("agrees with chordName on every chord's root and on which chords have no name", () => {
    const scales = new MusicTheoryService()
      .getScaleCategories()
      .flatMap(category => category.scales)
      .filter(scale => isHeptatonic(scale.intervals));
    const extents: readonly ChordExtent[] = [3, 7, 9, 11, 13];
    let checked = 0;

    for (const scale of scales) {
      for (let tonic = 0; tonic < 12; tonic++) {
        const key: ProgressionKey = { tonic, scaleId: scale.id, preferSharps: scale.preferSharps };
        for (let degree = 0; degree < 7; degree++) {
          for (const extent of extents) {
            const shape = chord({ degree, extent });
            const root = chordRootName(key, scale.intervals, shape);
            const name = leadSheetNameOf(shape, key, scale.intervals);
            const printed = chordName(root, effectiveChord(scale.intervals, shape));

            expect(name.startsWith(root)).withContext(`${printed} in ${scale.id}`).toBeTrue();
            expect(name.endsWith('?')).withContext(`${printed} in ${scale.id}`).toBe(printed.endsWith('?'));
            checked++;
          }
        }
      }
    }

    expect(checked).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});

describe('numeralOf', () => {
  it("is the progression page's numeral for the same degree", () => {
    const shapes: ChordDegree[] = [
      chord({ degree: 0 }),
      chord({ degree: 5 }),
      chord({ degree: 6 }),
      chord({ degree: 6, extent: 7 }),
      chord({ degree: 4, extent: 9 }),
      chord({ degree: 6, alter: -1, quality: 'major' })
    ];

    for (const shape of shapes) {
      expect(numeralOf(shape, IONIAN)).toBe(
        romanNumeral(shape.degree, shape.alter, effectiveChord(IONIAN, shape))
      );
    }
  });

  it('prints the numerals the sheet toggles to', () => {
    expect(numeralOf(chord({ degree: 0 }), IONIAN)).toBe('I');
    expect(numeralOf(chord({ degree: 5 }), IONIAN)).toBe('vi');
    expect(numeralOf(chord({ degree: 6 }), IONIAN)).toBe('vii°');
    expect(numeralOf(chord({ degree: 4, extent: 7 }), IONIAN)).toBe('V7');
    expect(numeralOf(chord({ degree: 6, alter: -1, quality: 'major' }), IONIAN)).toBe('♭VII');
  });

  it("is relative to the key's own mode", () => {
    // A aeolian's seventh is a G, so its G major triad is VII and not ♭VII.
    expect(numeralOf(chord({ degree: 6 }), AEOLIAN)).toBe('VII');
    expect(numeralOf(chord({ degree: 0 }), AEOLIAN)).toBe('i');
  });
});
```

```ts
import { SUSPENSIONS } from '../models/progression-normalize';
import { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey, createDegreeSlot } from '../models/progression.model';
import { CHORD_CATEGORIES } from './chord-catalog';
import { MusicTheoryService } from './music-theory.service';
import { ChordExtent, effectiveChord, isHeptatonic } from './progression-harmony';
import { TypedChord, chordFromText } from './song-chord-parse';
import { leadSheetNameOf, numeralOf } from './song-chord-names';

/**
 * Reading a chord typed into the sheet's `[` field, by name or by numeral.
 *
 * Fixtures first, each worked out by hand; then the round trips the parser is
 * held to - what the sheet prints, the field reads back as the same chord - over
 * a table of names and then over every chord the app's scales build.
 */
const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];
const DORIAN = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10];
const AEOLIAN = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10];
const HARMONIC_MINOR = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11];
const MAJOR_PENTATONIC = [0, 2, 4, 7, 9];

const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const G_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 7, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const D_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 2, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const F_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 5, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: false };
const E_FLAT_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 3, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: false };
const G_FLAT_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 6, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: false };
const C_SHARP_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 1, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const A_MINOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 9, scaleId: 'aeolian', preferSharps: false };
const A_HARMONIC_MINOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 9, scaleId: 'harmonicMinor', preferSharps: false };
const D_DORIAN: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 2, scaleId: 'dorian', preferSharps: false };
const C_PENTATONIC: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'majorPentatonic', preferSharps: true };

/** The degree a reading produced, or a failed expectation naming the refusal. */
function degreeOf(reading: TypedChord): ChordDegree {
  if (reading.kind !== 'chord') throw new Error(`refused: ${reading.reason}`);
  return reading.degree;
}

/** The refusal's reason, or a failed expectation naming the chord it read. */
function reasonOf(reading: TypedChord): string {
  if (reading.kind !== 'refused') throw new Error(`read a chord: ${JSON.stringify(reading.degree)}`);
  return reading.reason;
}

/** What the sheet prints for a typed name, read in a key. */
function reprinted(text: string, key: ProgressionKey, scale: readonly number[]): string {
  return leadSheetNameOf(degreeOf(chordFromText(text, key, scale)), key, scale);
}

/** A degree as a slot really holds one, with the given fields over it. */
function chord(shape: Partial<ChordDegree> & { degree: number }): ChordDegree {
  const slot = createDegreeSlot(shape.degree, 0);
  if (slot.harmony.kind !== 'degree') throw new Error('unreachable');
  return { ...slot.harmony.degree, ...shape };
}

  describe('reading a name', () => {
    it('reads a diatonic chord as the degree the palette would store', () => {
      const am = degreeOf(chordFromText('Am', C_MAJOR, IONIAN));

    it('reads suspensions, heights and alterations into the fields that hold them', () => {

      expect(numeralOf(minorMajor, HARMONIC_MINOR)).toBe('i(maj7)');
    });

    /**
     * Every chord the app's heptatonic scales build on their own degrees, in all
     * twelve keys, at every height and suspension: printed as a name and as a
     * numeral, and each read back.
     *
     * Three kinds of chord are held to a weaker promise, and all are counted so
     * the exemptions stay visible:
     *
     *  - **No name** (`?`). There is nothing to read back.
     *  - **One pitch class twice.** A suspension at a height doubles an
     *    extension's pitch class (a sus2 is the ninth an octave down), and so
     *    does a diminished seventh's thirteenth. The parse reads pitch classes,
     *    so it reads the shorter chord: the same notes, and the name may differ.
     *  - **A sus2 carrying a ♯9.** The ♯9 is the minor third's pitch class, and
     *    `parseChord` tries a third before a suspension (`OPENINGS`), so
     *    `Cmaj7#9sus2` reads as `CmMaj9`: the same notes, named the other way.
     *    Reachable only in the exotic scales whose own ninth sits a minor third
     *    up (ultra locrian's seventh degree, for one).
     *
     * Both of the last two are promised the same pitch classes, by name and by
     * numeral.
     */
    it('reads back every chord the app builds, by name and by numeral', () => {
      const scales = new MusicTheoryService()
        .getScaleCategories()
        .flatMap(category => category.scales)
        .filter(scale => isHeptatonic(scale.intervals));
      const extents: readonly ChordExtent[] = [3, 7, 9, 11, 13];
      const counts = { exact: 0, unnamed: 0, doubled: 0, sus2SharpNine: 0 };

      for (const scale of scales) {
        for (let tonic = 0; tonic < 12; tonic++) {
          const key: ProgressionKey = { tonic, scaleId: scale.id, preferSharps: scale.preferSharps };
          for (let degree = 0; degree < 7; degree++) {
            for (const extent of extents) {
              for (const suspension of SUSPENSIONS) {
                const shape = chord({ degree, extent, suspension });
                const built = effectiveChord(scale.intervals, shape);
                const name = leadSheetNameOf(shape, key, scale.intervals);
                const context = `${name} (${scale.id} on ${tonic})`;

                if (name.endsWith('?')) {
                  counts.unnamed++;
                  continue;
                }

                const byName = degreeOf(chordFromText(name, key, scale.intervals));
                const byNumeral = degreeOf(
                  chordFromText(numeralOf(shape, scale.intervals), key, scale.intervals)
                );
                const pitchClasses = new Set(built.intervals.map(interval => interval % 12));

                const doubled = pitchClasses.size < built.intervals.length;
                const sus2SharpNine = built.suspension === 'sus2' && built.ninth === 1;
                if (doubled || sus2SharpNine) {
                  if (doubled) counts.doubled++;
                  else counts.sus2SharpNine++;

                  const sounding = soundingOf(shape, key, scale.intervals);
                  expect(soundingOf(byName, key, scale.intervals)).withContext(context).toEqual(sounding);
                  expect(soundingOf(byNumeral, key, scale.intervals)).withContext(context).toEqual(sounding);
                  continue;
                }

                counts.exact++;
                expect(leadSheetNameOf(byName, key, scale.intervals)).withContext(context).toBe(name);
                expect(numeralOf(byNumeral, scale.intervals))
                  .withContext(context)
                  .toBe(numeralOf(shape, scale.intervals));
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }

      // Pinned rather than bounded, so a scale added to the app or a change to
      // the parse moves a number here and says which exemption it moved.
      // 41,580 chords: 33 scales, 12 keys, 7 degrees, 5 heights, 3 suspensions.
      expect(counts).toEqual({ exact: 22176, unnamed: 13656, doubled: 5280, sus2SharpNine: 468 });
    });
  });
});

/** The pitch classes a degree sounds in a key, sorted, for comparing two readings. */
function soundingOf(degree: ChordDegree, key: ProgressionKey, scale: readonly number[]): number[] {
  const built = effectiveChord(scale, degree);
  const classes = new Set(built.intervals.map(interval => (key.tonic + built.root + interval) % 12));
  return [...classes].sort((left, right) => left - right);
}
```

```ts
/**
 * How a quality is written, in the three places a chord is written at all.
 *
```

<!-- apply: create client/src/app/services/song-chord-names.ts -->
```ts
import type { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../models/progression.model';
import { SpelledNote, formatNote, reduceToOctave, spellAt } from './note-spelling';
import { leadSheetChordName, romanNumeral } from './progression-chord-names';
import { ChordIdentity, effectiveChord } from './progression-harmony';
import { chordRootSpelling, scaleNoteSpelling } from './progression-spelling';

/**
 * How the song sheet writes a chord: a lead-sheet name over the lyric, or a
 * Roman numeral when the sheet's I-IV toggle is on.
 *
 * Pure, with no Angular, on the `progression-harmony.ts` precedent. Everything
 * that decides *which chord* a degree is comes from where the progression page
 * gets it - `chordRootSpelling` for the root's letter, `effectiveChord` for the
 * chord the slot actually builds, and `composeFigure` (through
 * `leadSheetChordName`) for its height, alterations and suspension - so the
 * sheet and the progression page can differ only in typography and never about
 * the chord. The one table the sheet adds, `LEAD_SHEET_SUFFIXES`, lives beside
 * the other three in `progression-chord-names.ts`, keyed on the same exhaustive
 * union.
 *
 * ## The conventions, and where each came from
 *
 * - **Accidentals in names are ASCII**, `Bb7` and `F#m`, because that is what
 *   `chordName` and the root spelling (`formatNote`) already print. Numerals
 *   keep `♭` and `♯`, which is `romanNumeral`'s own convention; the field that
 *   reads both (`song-chord-parse.ts`) takes either glyph.
 * - **Half-diminished is `ø7`**, because the app's names already write it so
 *   (`CHORD_SUFFIXES.halfDiminished7`). The catalogue's `m7b5` is read as an
 *   alias and printed back as `ø7`.
 * - **Diminished and augmented are `°` and `+`**, for the same reason.
 * - **The slash bass is spelled by its place in the chord**, as the roll spells
 *   chord tones: the third of E is `G#`, never `Ab`.
 */

/**
 * A degree's lead-sheet name in a key: `C`, `Am`, `B°`, `Bb7`, `Bø7`, `G7b9`,
 * `Gsus4`, `C6/9`, `F/A`.
 *
 * `scaleIntervals` must be heptatonic - the song's key control offers only
 * scales that can build chords - and a scale that is not throws exactly as
 * `effectiveChord` does, rather than printing a name the key cannot hold. A
 * chord with no name at all prints `?` after its root, as `chordName` does:
 * unlabelled rather than mislabelled.
 */
export function leadSheetNameOf(
  degree: ChordDegree,
  key: ProgressionKey,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[]
): string {
  const root = chordRootSpelling(key, scaleIntervals, degree);
  const chord = effectiveChord(scaleIntervals, degree);
  const name = leadSheetChordName(formatNote(root), chord);

  const bass = bassSpelling(key, scaleIntervals, root, chord, degree.inversion);
  return bass === null ? name : `${name}/${formatNote(bass)}`;
}

/**
 * The note an inversion puts in the bass, spelled on the letter its place in
 * the chord names, or null in root position.
 *
 * `inversion` indexes the built stack, which is what `voiceChord` rotates and
 * what `inversionOf` writes back, so the note named here is the note the slot
 * sounds lowest. The letter comes from `ChordIdentity.steps` as it does for the
 * roll's chord tones (`slotSpeller`), and past a double accidental falls back to
 * the key's own spelling of that pitch class, as a root does.
 *
 * Null as well for a chord with no intervals to index - `'other'` as a stored
 * quality builds none - since there is then no note to name.
 */
function bassSpelling(
  key: ProgressionKey,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[],
  root: SpelledNote,
  chord: ChordIdentity,
  inversion: number
): SpelledNote | null {
  if (inversion === 0) return null;

  const interval = chord.intervals.at(inversion);
  const steps = chord.steps.at(inversion);
  if (interval === undefined || steps === undefined) return null;

  const pitchClass = reduceToOctave(key.tonic + chord.root + interval);
  return spellAt(pitchClass, root, steps) ?? scaleNoteSpelling(key, scaleIntervals, pitchClass);
}

/**
 * A degree's Roman numeral, exactly as the progression page prints it: `I`,
 * `vi`, `vii°`, `V7`, `♭VII`.
 *
 * A wrapper rather than a second numeral, so the sheet's I-IV toggle has one
 * import beside `leadSheetNameOf` and cannot drift from the strip's card -
 * which builds its numeral from the same two calls (`describeSlot`). Relative
 * to the key's own mode, as those are: A aeolian's G major triad is `VII`.
 * No key is taken because a numeral needs none; the scale is the whole frame.
 */
export function numeralOf(degree: ChordDegree, scaleIntervals: readonly number[]): string {
  return romanNumeral(degree.degree, degree.alter, effectiveChord(scaleIntervals, degree));
}
```

<!-- apply: create client/src/app/services/song-chord-parse.ts -->
```ts
import { ALTER_MAX, ALTER_MIN } from '../models/progression-normalize';
import type { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../models/progression.model';
import { SpelledNote, parseNoteName, pitchClassOf } from './note-spelling';
import { isNameable } from './progression-chord-names';
import { ChordIdentity, effectiveChord, isHeptatonic } from './progression-harmony';
import { nearest, parseChord, reduce } from './progression-parse';
import { atDegree, expressInKey } from './progression-recognise';
import { tonicSpelling } from './progression-spelling';

/**
 * Reading a chord typed into the song sheet's `[` field: a name (`Am`, `Bb7`,
 * `F/A`) or a numeral (`vi`, `♭VII`, `V7`), into the `ChordDegree` a chord atom
 * stores.
 *
 * Pure, with no Angular. The app reads chords from *notes* already
 * (`parseChord`) and writes a reading into a key already (`expressInKey`), and
 * this module is the small piece in front of them that neither had: it turns the
 * text into the chord's intervals above a root, and hands those to the same two
 * doors recognition uses. So a typed chord is decided - base shape, suspension,
 * extensions, which fields the key is left to answer - by exactly the rules a
 * chord played into the roll is, and `leadSheetNameOf` prints it back through
 * the same identity. `song-chord-parse.spec.ts` holds the two to a round trip
 * over every chord the app's scales build.
 *
 * ## What the field reads
 *
 * **A name** is a root (`A`-`G`, then up to two of `b`/`#`/`♭`/`♯`), a suffix,
 * and an optional `/Bass`. The suffix is a small grammar rather than a list, so
 * that everything `leadSheetNameOf` can print is something this can read:
 *
 *     [m|min|-] [dim|°|o|ø|aug|+] [maj|Maj|M|Δ] [6|6/9|add9|add2] [7|9|11|13]
 *     [b5|#5|b9|#9|#11|b13 ...] [sus2|sus4|sus]
 *
 * which covers every symbol in the chord catalogue (`CHORD_CATEGORIES`) except
 * `7b5`, plus the progression page's own spaced names (`C Maj7`, `A min`) and
 * the usual aliases (`M7`, `Δ`, `-7`, `m7b5`, `ø`, `m(maj7)`, `69`). Brackets
 * and commas around alterations are ignored, so `C7(b9)` is `C7b9`. An
 * alteration above the height fills the extensions under it, which is what a
 * chord of stacked thirds is: `C7#11` is read as `C9#11`, and printed so.
 *
 * **A numeral** is up to two of `b`/`#`/`♭`/`♯`, `I`-`VII` in one case, and the
 * same figure grammar without the `m` - the case is the third, as it is in
 * `romanNumeral`. Numerals are the key's own mode's, as the progression page's
 * are: `VII` in A aeolian is a G major triad.
 *
 * ## The letter typed is the numeral meant
 *
 * A name is written on the degree its **letter** names, and only falls back to
 * `expressInKey`'s ranking when that letter is too far from the root for the
 * model to store (more than a double accidental). `F#` in C is therefore `♯IV`
 * and `Gb` is `♭V`: one pitch class, two chords on the sheet, each printed back
 * as typed. That is the ruling `keptNumeral` records for recognition - a root
 * outside the key has two numerals, and what the user wrote is the evidence of
 * which they meant - and it is also what makes the round trip exact: the sheet
 * spells a root by its degree's letter, so a chord written on the typed letter
 * comes back spelled as typed. `Cb`, `E#` and `B#` follow from the same rule and
 * need nothing of their own.
 *
 * ## What it refuses, and why it never guesses
 *
 * An empty field; a key whose scale cannot build chords; a root that is not a
 * note; a suffix or alteration it does not read, named in the reason; a power
 * chord; a shape the model has no quality for (`7b5`); a numeral in mixed case,
 * past `VII`, or with a sign its case contradicts; a secondary numeral (`V/V`),
 * which names a function rather than a root; and **a slash bass that is not a
 * note of the chord**. The model stores a bass only as an inversion - an index
 * into the chord's own notes - and `expressInKey` reads any other bass as root
 * position, so `C/D` would be stored as a plain C with the D silently gone. The
 * field refuses it and says why instead.
 *
 * ## Two kinds of chord it reads back under another name
 *
 * The parse works on pitch classes, so where two readings sound the same pitch
 * classes it takes the one `parseChord` prefers, and the sheet then prints that
 * one. The notes are the same either way; the spec counts both and holds them
 * to exactly that.
 *
 *  - **A chord that sounds one pitch class twice** - a suspension tall enough to
 *    reach the extension it doubles (`Cmaj9sus2`, whose sus2 is its ninth), or a
 *    diminished seventh's thirteenth - is read at the shorter height. The voicing
 *    loses the doubled octave.
 *  - **A sus2 carrying a ♯9** is read as the minor chord with a ninth
 *    (`Cmaj7#9sus2` as `CmMaj9`), because the ♯9 is the minor third's pitch class
 *    and `parseChord` tries a third before a suspension. Only exotic scales build
 *    one unasked.
 */

/** What the field makes of a typed chord. */
export type TypedChord =
  | { kind: 'chord'; degree: ChordDegree }
  | { kind: 'refused'; reason: string };

const EMPTY_REASON = 'Type a chord name, such as Am, or a numeral, such as vi.';

const NO_CHORDS_REASON =
  "This key's scale can't build chords; choose a seven-note scale for the song.";

const MIXED_CASE_REASON =
  'Write a numeral in one case: VI for a major chord, vi for a minor one.';

const SECONDARY_REASON =
  'Secondary numerals like V/V are not read here; type the chord name instead.';

const POWER_CHORD_REASON =
  'A power chord has no third, and a chord here needs one (or a sus2 or sus4 in its place).';

const ROMAN_NUMERALS: readonly string[] = ['I', 'II', 'III', 'IV', 'V', 'VI', 'VII'];

/** An accidental prefix, a run of numeral letters, and whatever follows. */
const NUMERAL = /^([b#]*)([IViv]+)(.*)$/;

/** A slash naming a numeral rather than a note: `V/V`, `V7/vi`. */
const SECONDARY = /\/[b#]*[IViv]/;

/** A root: one capital letter and up to two of one accidental. */
const ROOT = /^[A-G](?:#{1,2}|b{1,2})?/;

/**
 * The suffix grammar in the header, one optional group per slot, in the order a
 * chart writes them. `m(?!aj)` keeps `maj` from being read as a minor `m`.
 */
const FIGURE =
  /^(min|m(?!aj)|-)?(dim|°|o|ø|aug|\+)?(maj|Maj|M|Δ)?(6\/9|6|add9|add2)?(7|9|11|13)?((?:[b#](?:5|9|11|13))*)(sus2|sus4|sus)?$/;

/** One alteration out of the run the grammar's sixth group matched. */
const ALTERATION = /([b#])(5|9|11|13)/g;

/** The natural ninth, eleventh and thirteenth, as `EXTENSION_NATURALS` has them. */
const EXTENSION_NATURALS: readonly number[] = [14, 17, 21];

/** Which extension a height reaches, as an index into the naturals above. */
const TOP_EXTENSION: Readonly<Record<number, number>> = { 7: -1, 9: 0, 11: 1, 13: 2 };

/** The altered extensions a chord can carry, and the interval each puts there. */
const EXTENSION_ALTERATIONS: Readonly<Record<string, { index: number; interval: number }>> = {
  b9: { index: 0, interval: 13 },
  '#9': { index: 0, interval: 15 },
  '#11': { index: 1, interval: 18 },
  b13: { index: 2, interval: 20 }
};

/** Whether the figure's third comes from its own `m`, or from a numeral's case. */
type ThirdFrom = { kind: 'name' } | { kind: 'numeral'; minor: boolean };

/** A figure read into intervals above the root, or the reason it was not. */
type Figure = { intervals: readonly number[] } | { reason: string };

/**
 * A typed chord, read in a key: the degree a chord atom would store, or the
 * reason it was refused - a short sentence the user can act on.
 *
 * `scaleIntervals` is the key's scale, nullable so a caller can hand over
 * `ProgressionKeyContext.chordScaleFor(key)` directly; null or not heptatonic
 * is refused, as the progression palette refuses in a pentatonic key.
 */
export function chordFromText(
  text: string,
  key: ProgressionKey,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[] | null
): TypedChord {
  const written = normalized(text);
  if (written === '') return refused(EMPTY_REASON);
  if (scaleIntervals === null || !isHeptatonic(scaleIntervals)) return refused(NO_CHORDS_REASON);

  const numeral = NUMERAL.exec(written);
  return numeral === null
    ? namedChord(written, key, scaleIntervals)
    : numeralChord(numeral, written, scaleIntervals);
}

/**
 * The text with its spaces taken out and the musical signs made ASCII.
 *
 * Spaces go everywhere, not only at the ends, because the progression page
 * prints `C Maj7` and `A min` and a user copying one should not be refused for
 * the space. Nothing the grammar reads contains one.
 */
function normalized(text: string): string {
  return text.replace(/\s+/g, '').replace(/♭/g, 'b').replace(/♯/g, '#');
}

function refused(reason: string): TypedChord {
  return { kind: 'refused', reason };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Names
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function namedChord(
  written: string,
  key: ProgressionKey,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[]
): TypedChord {
  const { chordText, bassText } = splitBass(written);
  if (chordText === '') return refused('Type the chord before the slash, such as C/E.');

  const rootText = ROOT.exec(chordText)?.[0];
  // `ROOT` matches only what `parseNoteName` reads, so a match always parses;
  // the second test is the type checker's, not a second rule.
  const root = rootText === undefined ? null : parseNoteName(rootText);
  if (rootText === undefined || root === null) return refused(rootReason(chordText));

  const figure = figureOf(chordText.slice(rootText.length), { kind: 'name' });
  if ('reason' in figure) return refused(figure.reason);

  let bass: number | null = null;
  if (bassText !== null) {
    const spelled = parseNoteName(bassText);
    if (spelled === null) {
      return refused(`"${bassText}" after the slash is not a note; write the bass as A to G.`);
    }
    bass = reduce(pitchClassOf(spelled) - key.tonic);
  }

  const identity = identityOf(figure.intervals, reduce(pitchClassOf(root) - key.tonic));
  if (identity === null) return refused(unbuildableReason(chordText));

  if (bass !== null && !soundsPitchClass(identity, bass)) {
    return refused(
      `${bassText} is not a note of ${chordText}, and only a note of the chord can go under the slash.`
    );
  }

  const from = bass ?? identity.root;
  const degree =
    onLetter(identity, root, key, scaleIntervals, from) ??
    expressInKey(identity, scaleIntervals, 0, from);

  return chordOrRefusal(degree, scaleIntervals, chordText);
}

/**
 * The chord and its bass, split at the last slash that is followed by a letter.
 *
 * A slash followed by anything else belongs to the suffix: `C6/9` is a sixth
 * chord with a ninth, and `C6/9/E` is that chord over its third.
 */
function splitBass(written: string): { chordText: string; bassText: string | null } {
  const slash = written.lastIndexOf('/');
  const after = written.slice(slash + 1);

  return slash >= 0 && /^[A-Za-z]/.test(after)
    ? { chordText: written.slice(0, slash), bassText: after }
    : { chordText: written, bassText: null };
}

/**
 * Why the start of the text is not a root, said in the user's terms.
 *
 * A lower-case root is asked to be a capital rather than read, because a
 * lower-case `b` is also the flat that opens a numeral (`bVII`), and reading
 * `bb` as B flat would make the case of one letter decide which of two
 * grammars a chord is in.
 */
function rootReason(chordText: string): string {
  if (/^[a-g]/.test(chordText)) {
    return `Write the root as a capital letter: ${chordText[0].toUpperCase()}${chordText.slice(1)}.`;
  }

  const token = /^[A-Za-z]+/.exec(chordText)?.[0] ?? chordText[0];
  return `"${token}" is not a note: a chord name starts with a letter from A to G, and a numeral with I to VII.`;
}

/**
 * The chord written on the degree its root's letter names, or null when that
 * letter is too far from the root to be a numeral the model can store.
 *
 * See the header for why the letter decides. `atDegree` is handed a degree
 * whose root is the identity's by construction - `alter` is measured from that
 * degree to this root - which is the one check it leaves to its caller.
 */
function onLetter(
  identity: ChordIdentity,
  root: SpelledNote,
  key: ProgressionKey,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[],
  bass: number
): ChordDegree | null {
  const degree = (root.letter - tonicSpelling(key).letter + 7) % 7;
  const alter = nearest(identity.root - scaleIntervals[degree]);
  if (alter < ALTER_MIN || alter > ALTER_MAX) return null;

  return atDegree(identity, scaleIntervals, { degree, alter }, 0, bass);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Numerals
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function numeralChord(
  match: RegExpExecArray,
  written: string,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[]
): TypedChord {
  const [, signs, roman, rest] = match;

  if (!/^(?:b{0,2}|#{0,2})$/.test(signs)) {
    return refused(`"${signs}" is not an accidental; put up to two b or # signs before the numeral.`);
  }

  const upper = roman.toUpperCase();
  if (roman !== upper && roman !== roman.toLowerCase()) return refused(MIXED_CASE_REASON);

  const degree = ROMAN_NUMERALS.indexOf(upper);
  if (degree < 0) return refused(`"${roman}" is not a scale degree; numerals run from I to VII.`);

  if (SECONDARY.test(rest)) return refused(SECONDARY_REASON);

  const figure = figureOf(rest, { kind: 'numeral', minor: roman !== upper });
  if ('reason' in figure) return refused(figure.reason);

  const alter = signs.startsWith('b') ? -signs.length : signs.length;
  const root = reduce(scaleIntervals[degree] + alter);

  const identity = identityOf(figure.intervals, root);
  if (identity === null) return refused(unbuildableReason(written));

  return chordOrRefusal(
    atDegree(identity, scaleIntervals, { degree, alter }, 0, root),
    scaleIntervals,
    written
  );
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The figure, and the two doors it goes through
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A suffix or a numeral's figure, read into the intervals of the chord it
 * names above its root - or the reason it cannot be.
 *
 * The intervals need not be in any order and may sit past the octave: they are
 * reduced into a set of pitch classes for `parseChord`, which decides from that
 * set what each note is. That is the point of handing over notes rather than a
 * shape: the field cannot disagree with recognition about what a chord is.
 */
function figureOf(raw: string, third: ThirdFrom): Figure {
  const subject = third.kind === 'name' ? 'chord type' : 'numeral figure';
  // Brackets and commas group alterations on a chart - `C7(b9,#11)` - and mean
  // nothing the grammar needs; `m(maj7)` is the one place they wrap a word.
  const figure = raw.replace(/[(),]/g, '');
  if (figure === '5') return { reason: POWER_CHORD_REASON };

  const parts = FIGURE.exec(figure);
  if (parts === null) return { reason: `"${raw}" is not a ${subject} this app reads.` };

  const [, minorMark, sign, majorMark, added, heightText, alterationText, suspension] = parts;
  const diminished = sign === 'dim' || sign === '°' || sign === 'o';
  const halfDiminished = sign === 'ø';
  const augmented = sign === 'aug' || sign === '+';

  // The third: the name's own `m`, or the numeral's case.
  let minor: boolean;
  if (third.kind === 'name') {
    if (minorMark !== undefined && sign !== undefined) {
      return { reason: `"${raw}" is not a ${subject} this app reads.` };
    }
    minor = minorMark !== undefined || diminished || halfDiminished;
  } else {
    if (minorMark !== undefined) return { reason: `"${raw}" is not a ${subject} this app reads.` };
    if ((diminished || halfDiminished) && !third.minor) {
      return { reason: 'A diminished numeral is written in lower case, such as vii°.' };
    }
    if (augmented && third.minor) {
      return { reason: 'An augmented numeral is written in upper case, such as III+.' };
    }
    minor = third.minor;
  }

  if (suspension !== undefined && (sign !== undefined || (third.kind === 'name' && minor))) {
    return {
      reason: `A sus chord has no third, so it can't also be minor, diminished or augmented: drop the "${minorMark ?? sign}".`
    };
  }

  let fifth = diminished || halfDiminished ? 6 : augmented ? 8 : 7;
  const height = heightText === undefined ? null : Number(heightText);

  // The seventh: a major one wherever the figure says so, a diminished one under
  // `°` with a height, a minor one under any other height and under a bare `ø`.
  let seventh: number | null = null;
  if (majorMark !== undefined) {
    if (majorMark === 'Δ' || height !== null) seventh = 11;
  } else if (height !== null) {
    seventh = diminished ? 9 : 10;
  } else if (halfDiminished) {
    seventh = 10;
  }

  // An added tone, which stands where a seventh would and takes no height - but
  // `69` is how `6/9` is often typed, and is read as it.
  let addedTones: number[] = [];
  let top = height === null ? -1 : TOP_EXTENSION[height];
  if (added !== undefined) {
    const sixNine = added === '6' && height === 9 && majorMark === undefined;
    if ((height !== null && !sixNine) || majorMark !== undefined) {
      return { reason: `"${raw}" is not a ${subject} this app reads.` };
    }
    addedTones = added === '6' ? (sixNine ? [9, 14] : [9]) : added === '6/9' ? [9, 14] : [14];
    seventh = null;
    top = -1;
  }

  // The alterations, each to the one note it moves.
  const extensions: (number | null)[] = [null, null, null];
  let fifthAltered = false;
  for (const [alteration, accidental, number] of alterationText.matchAll(ALTERATION)) {
    if (number === '5') {
      if (fifth !== 7 || fifthAltered) {
        return { reason: `"${alteration}" contradicts the rest of "${raw}".` };
      }
      fifth = accidental === 'b' ? 6 : 8;
      fifthAltered = true;
      continue;
    }

    const extension = EXTENSION_ALTERATIONS[alteration];
    if (extension === undefined) {
      return {
        reason: `"${alteration}" is not an alteration this app can build; it reads b5, #5, b9, #9, #11 and b13.`
      };
    }
    if (seventh === null) {
      return { reason: `"${alteration}" needs a seventh chord under it, such as 7${alteration}.` };
    }
    if (extensions[extension.index] !== null) {
      return { reason: `"${alteration}" contradicts the rest of "${raw}".` };
    }
    extensions[extension.index] = extension.interval;
    top = Math.max(top, extension.index);
  }

  // Every extension up to the highest one named, natural unless altered: a
  // stack of thirds has no gaps, so `7#11` carries its ninth.
  const stacked: number[] = [];
  for (let index = 0; index <= top; index++) {
    stacked.push(extensions[index] ?? EXTENSION_NATURALS[index]);
  }

  const position1 = suspension === 'sus2' ? 2 : suspension !== undefined ? 5 : minor ? 3 : 4;
  return {
    intervals: [0, position1, fifth, ...(seventh === null ? [] : [seventh]), ...addedTones, ...stacked]
  };
}

/**
 * The chord these intervals make over this root, through `parseChord` - or null
 * when it reads none, or reads one the model has no quality for.
 *
 * `root` is relative to the key's tonic, which is the frame `expressInKey`
 * works in. A base of `'other'` is refused here rather than handed on, because
 * `writeAt` would try every quality, build none of them, and return nothing
 * anyway - the reason is the shape, and saying so is more useful than saying
 * the key could not write it.
 */
function identityOf(intervals: readonly number[], root: number): ChordIdentity | null {
  const pitchClasses = new Set(intervals.map(interval => reduce(root + interval)));
  const identity = parseChord(pitchClasses, root);
  return identity === null || identity.base === 'other' ? null : identity;
}

/** Whether a chord sounds this pitch class, in the tonic-relative frame. */
function soundsPitchClass(identity: ChordIdentity, pitchClass: number): boolean {
  return identity.intervals.some(interval => reduce(identity.root + interval) === pitchClass);
}

/**
 * The degree as a reading, or the refusal for a chord the key could not write
 * or the sheet could not name.
 *
 * The second test is the round trip's guarantee rather than a rule of its own:
 * a chord accepted here is printed by `leadSheetNameOf`, and a chord it would
 * print as `?` is one the user could not read back off the sheet.
 */
function chordOrRefusal(
  degree: ChordDegree | null,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[],
  subject: string
): TypedChord {
  if (degree === null) return refused(`${subject} can't be written as a chord of this key.`);
  if (!isNameable(effectiveChord(scaleIntervals, degree))) return refused(unbuildableReason(subject));
  return { kind: 'chord', degree };
}

function unbuildableReason(subject: string): string {
  return `This app has no chord shape for ${subject}, so it can't go on the sheet.`;
}
```

## Phase B: The song model

A song as a ProseMirror document, and every edit as a command.

### Task B.1: The song's ProseMirror model

The schema of Part 1 - `doc` with the song's meta, `section+`, lyric lines of text and chord atoms, and
the `tabBlock` and `memo` atoms S3 and S4 will fill, declared now so they need no migration - and the pure derivations
over it: a new song, validating a stored one without ever throwing, a section's derived progression, a summary for the
library, a voiced chord atom. Every attribute is validated by the schema; a chord atom is a `ChordSlot` without its
`startBeat`, which a section's progression sums back.

The ProseMirror packages arrive here, at exact versions.

**Files** (under `client/src/app/` unless given in full):
- Create: `models/song.model.ts`, `services/song-document.spec.ts`, `services/song-document.ts`, `services/song-schema.spec.ts`, `services/song-schema.ts`
- Modify: `client/package-lock.json`, `client/package.json`

**Step 1: The failing specs.**

`client/src/app/services/song-document.spec.ts`, new:

```ts
import { DOMParser, DOMSerializer, Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { EditorState, TextSelection } from 'prosemirror-state';
import {
  ChordDegree,
  ChordSlot,
  ProgressionKey,
  createDefaultProgression,
  createDegreeSlot
} from '../models/progression.model';
import { ChordAtomAttrs, SongDoc, SongMeta } from '../models/song.model';
import { DeriveState, ProgressionStore } from './progression-history';
import { regenerateSlot, requireUniqueSlotIds, settle } from './progression-edit';
import {
  chordSlotOf,
  chordsOf,
  createSectionNode,
  createSongContent,
  createSongIdsPlugin,
  idRepairsOf,
  sectionProgressionOf,
  sectionsOf,
  songMetaOf,
  songNodeOf,
  songSummaryOf
} from './song-document';
import { songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * The song document's derivations and constructors, headless.
 *
 * Every spec builds its document through the schema, or as stored JSON for the
 * validation specs, and runs transactions on a bare `EditorState`: nothing here
 * needs a view.
 */
const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const A_MINOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 9, scaleId: 'aeolian', preferSharps: false };
const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];
const FOUR_FOUR = { numerator: 4, denominator: 4, isCommon: true };
const THREE_FOUR = { numerator: 3, denominator: 4, isCommon: false };

const META: SongMeta = { title: 'Last Dance', artist: 'The Band', key: C_MAJOR, tempo: 100, timeSignature: FOUR_FOUR };

/** A chord atom for a C major degree, `lengthBeats` long and voiced. */
function chordNode(degree: number, lengthBeats = 4): Node {
  const slot: ChordSlot = regenerateSlot({ ...createDegreeSlot(degree, 0), lengthBeats }, C_MAJOR, IONIAN);
  const attrs: ChordAtomAttrs = {
    id: slot.id,
    harmony: slot.harmony,
    lengthBeats: slot.lengthBeats,
    notes: slot.notes,
    owned: slot.owned
  };
  return songSchema.node('chord', attrs);
}

function line(...content: (string | Node)[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node(
    'lyricLine',
    null,
    content.map(part => (typeof part === 'string' ? songSchema.text(part) : part))
  );
}

function section(id: string, label: string, ...lines: Node[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node('section', { id, label, kind: 'verse' }, lines);
}

function song(meta: SongMeta, ...sections: Node[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node('doc', meta, sections);
}

function degreeOf(slot: { harmony: ChordSlot['harmony'] }): ChordDegree {
  if (slot.harmony.kind !== 'degree') throw new Error('expected a degree slot');
  return slot.harmony.degree;
}

function storedSong(content: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>): SongDoc {
  return { id: 'song-1', revision: 3, createdAt: 1000, updatedAt: 2000, content };
}

describe('createSongContent', () => {
  it('starts a song on one "Verse 1" with one empty line, in C major at 100 BPM in 4/4', () => {
    const doc = createSongContent();

    expect(songMetaOf(doc)).toEqual({ title: '', artist: '', key: C_MAJOR, tempo: 100, timeSignature: FOUR_FOUR });
    expect(sectionsOf(doc).map(({ label, kind }) => ({ label, kind }))).toEqual([{ label: 'Verse 1', kind: 'verse' }]);
    expect(doc.child(0).childCount).toBe(1);
    expect(doc.child(0).child(0).type.name).toBe('lyricLine');
    expect(doc.child(0).child(0).content.size).toBe(0);
  });

  it('takes what the meta says over the defaults', () => {
    const doc = createSongContent({ title: 'Waltz', key: A_MINOR, timeSignature: THREE_FOUR });

    expect(songMetaOf(doc)).toEqual({ title: 'Waltz', artist: '', key: A_MINOR, tempo: 100, timeSignature: THREE_FOUR });
  });

  it('gives each new song its own section id, and a song that reads back', () => {
    const first = createSongContent();
    const second = createSongContent();

    expect(sectionsOf(first)[0].id).not.toEqual(sectionsOf(second)[0].id);
    expect(songNodeOf(first.toJSON()).kind).toBe('song');
  });
});

describe('createSectionNode', () => {
  it('builds a section with a fresh id, its label and kind, and one empty line', () => {
    const chorus = createSectionNode('Chorus', 'chorus');

    expect(chorus.attrs['id']).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
    expect(chorus.attrs['label']).toBe('Chorus');
    expect(chorus.attrs['kind']).toBe('chorus');
    expect(chorus.childCount).toBe(1);
    expect(createSectionNode('Chorus', 'chorus').attrs['id']).not.toBe(chorus.attrs['id']);
  });
});

describe('songNodeOf', () => {
  const good = (): Record<string, unknown> =>
    song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(chordNode(0), 'one ', chordNode(4), 'two')), section('s2', 'Chorus', line())).toJSON();

  /** The stored JSON with one part replaced, built as a corrupt record would be. */
  function corrupted(edit: (json: Record<string, any>) => void): Record<string, unknown> {
    const json = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(good()));
    edit(json);
    return json;
  }

  function reasonFor(json: unknown): string {
    const reading = songNodeOf(json);
    if (reading.kind !== 'refused') throw new Error('expected a refusal');
    return reading.reason;
  }

  it('reads a stored song back into the document it was', () => {
    const original = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(chordNode(0), 'one')));

    const reading = songNodeOf(JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(original.toJSON())));

    expect(reading.kind).toBe('song');
    expect(reading.kind === 'song' && reading.doc.eq(original)).toBeTrue();
  });

  it('refuses something that is not a document at all', () => {
    expect(reasonFor(null)).toMatch(/Invalid input/);
    expect(reasonFor('a song')).toMatch(/node type/);
    expect(reasonFor({ type: 'chorus' })).toMatch(/chorus/);
  });

  it('refuses a part of a song stored as if it were a whole one', () => {
    const lone = section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one')).toJSON();

    expect(reasonFor(lone)).toMatch(/not a song/);
  });

  it('refuses a song with no sections, or a section with nothing in it', () => {
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['content'] = [])))).toMatch(/doc/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['content'][1]['content'] = [])))).toMatch(/section/);
  });

  it('refuses text with marks the schema does not have', () => {
    const reason = reasonFor(
      corrupted(json => (json['content'][0]['content'][0]['content'][1]['marks'] = [{ type: 'strong' }]))
    );

    expect(reason).toMatch(/strong/);
  });

  it('refuses song facts that are missing or unplayable', () => {
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => delete json['attrs']['key']))).toMatch(/key/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['attrs']['key']['tonic'] = 1.5)))).toMatch(/key/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['attrs']['tempo'] = '100')))).toMatch(/tempo/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['attrs']['timeSignature'] = { numerator: 0 })))).toMatch(/time signature/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['attrs']['title'] = 7)))).toMatch(/title/);
  });

  it('refuses a section with no id, or a kind it does not know', () => {
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['content'][0]['attrs']['id'] = null)))).toMatch(/no id/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['content'][0]['attrs']['kind'] = 'refrain')))).toMatch(/kind/);
  });

  it('refuses a chord the progression model would refuse', () => {
    const chordAt = (json: Record<string, any>): Record<string, any> => json['content'][0]['content'][0]['content'][0];

    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (chordAt(json)['attrs']['harmony']['degree']['degree'] = 7)))).toMatch(/harmony/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (chordAt(json)['attrs']['notes'] = 'C E G')))).toMatch(/notes/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (chordAt(json)['attrs']['owned'] = { pitches: 'yes' })))).toMatch(/owned/);
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => delete chordAt(json)['attrs']['lengthBeats']))).toMatch(/lengthBeats/);
  });

  it('refuses two sections that share an id', () => {
    expect(reasonFor(corrupted(json => (json['content'][1]['attrs']['id'] = 's1')))).toMatch(/s1.*more than once/);
  });

  it('refuses two chords that share an id, even in different sections', () => {
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(chordNode(0))), section('s2', 'Chorus', line(chordNode(4))));
    const json = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(doc.toJSON()));
    const firstId: string = json['content'][0]['content'][0]['content'][0]['attrs']['id'];
    json['content'][1]['content'][0]['content'][0]['attrs']['id'] = firstId;

    expect(reasonFor(json)).toMatch(new RegExp(`${firstId}.*more than once`));
  });

  it('never throws, whatever it is handed', () => {
    for (const json of [undefined, 0, [], { type: 'doc' }, { type: 'doc', attrs: META, content: 'x' }]) {
      expect(() => songNodeOf(json)).not.toThrow();
      expect(songNodeOf(json).kind).toBe('refused');
    }
  });
});

describe('sectionsOf and chordsOf', () => {
  const am = chordNode(5);
  const f = chordNode(3);
  const c = chordNode(0);
  const doc = song(
    META,
    section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(am, 'Wondering ', f, 'where the'), line('second line')),
    songSchema.node('section', { id: 's2', label: 'Chorus', kind: 'chorus' }, [line(c, 'Got me')])
  );

  it('lists each section with its id, label, kind and position', () => {
    const sections = sectionsOf(doc);

    expect(sections.map(({ id, label, kind }) => ({ id, label, kind }))).toEqual([
      { id: 's1', label: 'Verse 1', kind: 'verse' },
      { id: 's2', label: 'Chorus', kind: 'chorus' }
    ]);
    for (const entry of sections) expect(doc.nodeAt(entry.pos)).toBe(entry.node);
  });

  it('lists a section\'s chords in document order, at their positions in the document', () => {
    const [verse, chorus] = sectionsOf(doc);

    const verseChords = chordsOf(verse.node, verse.pos);
    const chorusChords = chordsOf(chorus.node, chorus.pos);

    expect(verseChords.map(entry => entry.attrs.id)).toEqual([am.attrs['id'], f.attrs['id']]);
    expect(chorusChords.map(entry => entry.attrs.id)).toEqual([c.attrs['id']]);
    for (const entry of [...verseChords, ...chorusChords]) {
      expect(doc.nodeAt(entry.pos)?.attrs['id']).toBe(entry.attrs.id);
    }
  });
});

describe('sectionProgressionOf', () => {
  const am = chordNode(5, 4);
  const f = chordNode(3, 2);
  const g = chordNode(4, 6);
  const doc = song(
    META,
    section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(am, 'Wondering ', f, 'where the'), line(g, 'lights go')),
    section('s2', 'Chorus', line(chordNode(0), 'Got me'))
  );

  it('is the section\'s chords in order, with their start beats summed', () => {
    const progression = sectionProgressionOf(doc, 's1');

    expect(progression?.slots.map(slot => slot.id)).toEqual([am.attrs['id'], f.attrs['id'], g.attrs['id']]);
    expect(progression?.slots.map(slot => slot.startBeat)).toEqual([0, 4, 6]);
    expect(progression?.slots.map(slot => slot.lengthBeats)).toEqual([4, 2, 6]);
    expect(progression?.slots[0].notes).toEqual(am.attrs['notes']);
  });

  it('carries the song\'s key, tempo and time signature, and a name from both titles', () => {
    const waltz = song({ ...META, key: A_MINOR, tempo: 84, timeSignature: THREE_FOUR }, section('s1', 'Bridge', line()));

    const progression = sectionProgressionOf(waltz, 's1');

    expect(progression?.key).toEqual(A_MINOR);
    expect(progression?.tempo).toBe(84);
    expect(progression?.timeSignature).toEqual(THREE_FOUR);
    expect(progression?.name).toBe('Last Dance — Bridge');
    expect(progression?.slots).toEqual([]);
  });

  it('names an untitled song\'s section so it still reads as a song\'s', () => {
    const untitled = song({ ...META, title: '  ' }, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line()));

    expect(sectionProgressionOf(untitled, 's1')?.name).toBe('Untitled song — Verse 1');
  });

  it('is identified by the section, the same every time, at revision 0', () => {
    expect(sectionProgressionOf(doc, 's1')?.id).toBe('s1');
    expect(sectionProgressionOf(doc, 's1')).toEqual(sectionProgressionOf(doc, 's1'));
    expect(sectionProgressionOf(doc, 's1')?.revision).toBe(0);
  });

  it('is null for a section the song does not have', () => {
    expect(sectionProgressionOf(doc, 'nope')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('reorders when a chord is moved to another word, and keeps the moved chord\'s length', () => {
    const verse = sectionsOf(doc)[0];
    const [amAt, , gAt] = chordsOf(verse.node, verse.pos);
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc });

    // Am to the start of the second line, after G: delete it, then insert it
    // where G's position has been mapped to, one past G.
    const tr = state.tr.delete(amAt.pos, amAt.pos + 1);
    const target = tr.mapping.map(gAt.pos) + 1;
    tr.insert(target, am);

    const progression = sectionProgressionOf(tr.doc, 's1');

    expect(progression?.slots.map(slot => slot.id)).toEqual([f.attrs['id'], g.attrs['id'], am.attrs['id']]);
    expect(progression?.slots.map(slot => slot.startBeat)).toEqual([0, 2, 8]);
  });

  it('is already what the progression store would settle it to, so it can be handed over as is', () => {
    const progression = sectionProgressionOf(doc, 's1');
    if (progression === null) throw new Error('expected a progression');

    expect(settle(progression)).toEqual(progression);
    expect(() => requireUniqueSlotIds(progression)).not.toThrow();

    const derive: DeriveState = (current, selectedSlotId, isDirty, history, relabel) => ({
      doc: current,
      selectedSlotId,
      relabel,
      canBuildChords: true,
      keyScale: null,
      isDirty,
      canUndo: history.canUndo,
      canRedo: history.canRedo
    });
    const store = new ProgressionStore(createDefaultProgression(), derive);
    store.replaceDocument(progression, true);
    expect(store.doc.slots).toEqual(progression.slots);
  });

  it('shares nothing with the document it was read from', () => {
    const progression = sectionProgressionOf(doc, 's1');
    if (progression === null) throw new Error('expected a progression');

    expect(progression.timeSignature).not.toBe(doc.attrs['timeSignature']);
    expect(progression.key).not.toBe(doc.attrs['key']);
    expect(progression.slots[0].harmony).not.toBe(am.attrs['harmony']);
    expect(progression.slots[0].notes).not.toBe(am.attrs['notes']);
  });
});

describe('songSummaryOf', () => {
  it('lists a song\'s title, artist, key, section count and when it was last written', () => {
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line()), section('s2', 'Chorus', line()));

    expect(songSummaryOf(storedSong(doc.toJSON()))).toEqual({

describe('chordSlotOf', () => {
  const vi: ChordDegree = degreeOf(createDegreeSlot(5, 0));

  it('makes a chord one bar long in the song\'s time signature', () => {
    expect(chordSlotOf(vi, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, FOUR_FOUR).lengthBeats).toBe(4);
    expect(chordSlotOf(vi, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, THREE_FOUR).lengthBeats).toBe(3);
    // A bar of 6/8 is three quarter notes: the progression's beat is a quarter.
    expect(chordSlotOf(vi, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, { numerator: 6, denominator: 8, isCommon: false }).lengthBeats).toBe(3);
  });

  it('voices the chord, so it sounds before anything else touches it', () => {
    const slot = chordSlotOf(vi, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, THREE_FOUR);

    // A minor from middle C: A, C, E in root position above A3... as the
    // generator voices vi in C: its root's pitch class first, then up.
    expect(slot.notes.map(note => note.midi % 12)).toEqual([9, 0, 4]);
    expect(slot.notes.every(note => note.lengthBeats === 3 && note.startBeat === 0)).toBeTrue();
  });

  it('keeps the whole degree it was given, suspension and extensions included', () => {
    const sus: ChordDegree = { ...degreeOf(createDegreeSlot(4, 0)), extent: 7, suspension: 'sus4' };

    const slot = chordSlotOf(sus, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, FOUR_FOUR);

    expect(degreeOf(slot)).toEqual(sus);
    expect(slot.notes.map(note => note.midi % 12)).toEqual([7, 0, 2, 5]);
  });

  it('gives every chord a fresh id, owns nothing, and stores no startBeat', () => {
    const first = chordSlotOf(vi, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, FOUR_FOUR);
    const second = chordSlotOf(vi, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, FOUR_FOUR);

    expect(first.id).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
    expect(first.id).not.toBe(second.id);
    expect(first.owned).toEqual({ pitches: false, timing: false, velocity: false });
    expect('startBeat' in first).toBeFalse();
    expect(() => songSchema.node('chord', first)).not.toThrow();
  });
});

describe('ids', () => {
  const plugins = [createSongIdsPlugin()];

  function idsIn(doc: Node): (string | null)[] {
    const ids: (string | null)[] = [];
    doc.descendants(node => {
      if ('id' in node.attrs) ids.push(node.attrs['id']);
    });
    return ids;
  }

  it('gives a pasted copy of a chord a fresh id, and leaves the original its own', () => {
    const am = chordNode(5);
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(am, 'Wondering where')));
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc, plugins });
    const copied = doc.slice(2, 3);

    const end = 2 + 1 + 'Wondering where'.length;
    const after = state.apply(state.tr.setSelection(TextSelection.create(doc, end)).replaceSelection(copied)).doc;

    const [original, copy] = chordsOf(after.child(0), 0);
    expect(original.attrs.id).toBe(am.attrs['id']);
    expect(copy.attrs.id).not.toBe(am.attrs['id']);
    expect({ ...copy.attrs, id: '' }).toEqual({ ...original.attrs, id: '' });
  });

  it('gives a chord copied and pasted through the clipboard a fresh id, its slot otherwise whole', () => {
    const am = chordNode(5);
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(am, 'Wondering')));
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc, plugins });
    const container = document.createElement('div');
    container.appendChild(DOMSerializer.fromSchema(songSchema).serializeFragment(doc.slice(2, 3).content));
    const pasted = DOMParser.fromSchema(songSchema).parseSlice(container);

    const end = 2 + 1 + 'Wondering'.length;
    const after = state.apply(state.tr.setSelection(TextSelection.create(doc, end)).replaceSelection(pasted)).doc;

    const [original, copy] = chordsOf(after.child(0), 0);
    expect(original.attrs.id).toBe(am.attrs['id']);
    expect(copy.attrs.id).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
    expect(copy.attrs.id).not.toBe(am.attrs['id']);
    expect({ ...copy.attrs, id: '' }).toEqual({ ...original.attrs, id: '' });
  });

  it('keeps the original\'s id when the copy is pasted in front of it', () => {
    const am = chordNode(5);
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(am, 'Wondering')));
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc, plugins });

    const after = state.apply(state.tr.insert(2, doc.slice(2, 3).content)).doc;

    const [copy, original] = chordsOf(after.child(0), 0);
    expect(original.attrs.id).toBe(am.attrs['id']);
    expect(copy.attrs.id).not.toBe(am.attrs['id']);
  });

  it('keeps a moved chord\'s id: a move leaves one of it', () => {
    const am = chordNode(5);
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(am, 'Wondering where')));
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc, plugins });

    const tr = state.tr.delete(2, 3);
    tr.insert(tr.mapping.map(2) + 5, am);
    const after = state.apply(tr).doc;

    expect(chordsOf(after.child(0), 0).map(entry => entry.attrs.id)).toEqual([am.attrs['id']]);
  });

  it('gives the second half of a split section its own id', () => {
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one'), line('two')));
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc, plugins });
    const between = 1 + doc.child(0).child(0).nodeSize;

    const after = state.apply(state.tr.split(between)).doc;

    expect(after.childCount).toBe(2);
    expect(after.child(0).attrs['id']).toBe('s1');
    expect(after.child(1).attrs['id']).toMatch(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/);
  });

  it('gives a section ProseMirror generated an id', () => {
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one')));
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc, plugins });

    const after = state.apply(state.tr.delete(0, doc.content.size)).doc;

    expect(idsIn(after)).toEqual([jasmine.stringMatching(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/)]);
    expect(songNodeOf(after.toJSON()).kind).toBe('song');
  });

  it('names exactly the positions that need a fresh id', () => {
    const am = chordNode(5);
    const doc = song(META, section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(am, 'one')));
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc });
    const tr = state.tr.insert(6, doc.slice(2, 3).content);

    expect(idRepairsOf(doc, tr.doc, tr.mapping)).toEqual([6]);
    expect(idRepairsOf(doc, doc, state.tr.mapping)).toEqual([]);
  });
});
```
