```ts
import { DOMParser, DOMSerializer, Fragment, Node, Slice } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { AllSelection, EditorState } from 'prosemirror-state';
import { ChordSlot, ProgressionKey, createDegreeSlot } from '../models/progression.model';
import { ChordAtomAttrs, SongMeta } from '../models/song.model';
import { regenerateSlot } from './progression-edit';
import { NEW_SECTION, songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * The song's schema: what a song document can hold, how it goes to JSON and
 * back, and how its nodes survive the clipboard.
 *
 * Headless: ProseMirror's model needs no view. The clipboard specs use the
 * schema's own `DOMSerializer` and `DOMParser`, which are the two halves the
 * editor's copy and paste run through - Karma's Chrome supplies the document.
 */
const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];

const META: SongMeta = {
  title: 'Last Dance',
  artist: 'The Band',
  key: C_MAJOR,
  tempo: 100,
  timeSignature: { numerator: 4, denominator: 4, isCommon: true }
};

/** A chord atom's attributes, as a slot in C major really carries them: voiced, one bar long. */
function chordAttrs(degree: number): ChordAtomAttrs {
  const slot: ChordSlot = regenerateSlot(createDegreeSlot(degree, 0), C_MAJOR, IONIAN);
  return { id: slot.id, harmony: slot.harmony, lengthBeats: slot.lengthBeats, notes: slot.notes, owned: slot.owned };
}

function chordNode(degree: number): Node {
  return songSchema.node('chord', chordAttrs(degree));
}

function line(...content: (string | Node)[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node(
    'lyricLine',
    null,
    content.map(part => (typeof part === 'string' ? songSchema.text(part) : part))
  );
}

function section(id: string, label: string, ...children: Node[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node('section', { id, label, kind: 'verse' }, children);
}

function song(...sections: Node[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node('doc', META, sections);
}

/** Every chord atom in a node or a slice's content, in document order. */
function chordsIn(node: Node | Fragment): Node[] {
  const found: Node[] = [];
  node.descendants(child => {
    if (child.type.name === 'chord') found.push(child);
  });
  return found;
}

/** A slice through the schema's clipboard serializer and parser, as copy then paste moves it. */
function throughClipboard(slice: Slice): Slice {
  const container = document.createElement('div');
  container.appendChild(DOMSerializer.fromSchema(songSchema).serializeFragment(slice.content));
  return DOMParser.fromSchema(songSchema).parseSlice(container);
}

describe('songSchema', () => {
  describe('JSON', () => {
    it('round-trips a song with sections, words, chords, a tab block and a memo', () => {
      const original = song(
        section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(chordNode(5), 'Wondering ', chordNode(3), 'where the'), line()),
        section(
          's2',
          'Chorus',
          songSchema.node('tabBlock', {
            id: 't1',
            name: 'Riff',
            score: { title: '', subTitle: '', artist: '', album: '', tempo: 100, masterBars: [], tracks: [] }
          }),
          songSchema.node('memo', { id: 'm1', name: 'Hum', durationSec: 12.5 })
        )
      );

      const json = original.toJSON();
      const restored = Node.fromJSON(songSchema, JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(json)));

      expect(restored.eq(original)).toBeTrue();
      expect(restored.toJSON()).toEqual(json);
      expect(() => restored.check()).not.toThrow();
    });

    it('keeps the song facts on the doc node, so they share the words\' undo history', () => {
      const json = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line())).toJSON();

      expect(json.attrs).toEqual(META);
    });

    it('stores a chord without a startBeat: it is derived, and one handed in is dropped', () => {
      const withStart = { ...chordAttrs(0), startBeat: 8 };
      const chord = songSchema.node('chord', withStart);

      expect('startBeat' in chord.attrs).toBeFalse();
      expect(chord.toJSON().attrs).toEqual(withoutStartBeat(withStart));
    });
  });

  describe('content', () => {
    it('refuses a song with no section', () => {
      expect(() => songSchema.node('doc', META, []).check()).toThrowError(/doc/);
    });

    it('fills an empty section with one empty lyric line, which is where its caret goes', () => {
      const filled = songSchema.nodes['section'].createAndFill({ id: 's1', label: 'Chorus', kind: 'chorus' });

      expect(filled?.childCount).toBe(1);
      expect(filled?.firstChild?.type.name).toBe('lyricLine');
      expect(filled?.firstChild?.content.size).toBe(0);
    });

    it('leaves one empty lyric line when everything in a section is deleted', () => {

      expect(after.child(0).firstChild?.content.size).toBe(0);
      expect(after.child(1).textContent).toBe('three');
    });

    it('generates a new song\'s first section, without an id, when everything is deleted', () => {
      const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one')), section('s2', 'Chorus', line('two')));
      const state = EditorState.create({ doc });

      const after = state.apply(state.tr.setSelection(new AllSelection(state.doc)).deleteSelection()).doc;

      expect(after.childCount).toBe(1);
      expect(after.child(0).attrs).toEqual({ id: null, label: NEW_SECTION.label, kind: NEW_SECTION.kind });
    });

    it('holds text and chords in a lyric line, and no marks', () => {
      const lyric = line(chordNode(0), 'Got me ', chordNode(3), 'thinking');

      expect(() => lyric.check()).not.toThrow();
      expect(songSchema.nodes['lyricLine'].spec.marks).toBe('');
    });

    it('refuses text directly in a section', () => {
      const attrs = { id: 's1', label: 'Verse 1', kind: 'verse' };

      expect(() => songSchema.node('section', attrs, [songSchema.text('loose')])).toThrowError(/section/);
    });
  });

  describe('attributes', () => {
    it('refuses a chord whose degree is outside the scale', () => {
      const attrs = chordAttrs(0);
      const harmony = { kind: 'degree', degree: { ...degreeOf(attrs), degree: 9 } };

      expect(() => songSchema.node('chord', { ...attrs, harmony })).toThrowError(/harmony/);
    });

    it('refuses a chord whose harmony is not one of the two kinds', () => {
      expect(() => songSchema.node('chord', { ...chordAttrs(0), harmony: { kind: 'guess' } })).toThrowError(/harmony/);
      expect(() => songSchema.node('chord', { ...chordAttrs(0), harmony: 'C' })).toThrowError(/harmony/);
    });

    it('refuses a chord with a note that is not a MIDI number, or with no id', () => {
      const notes = [{ midi: 60.5, startBeat: 0, lengthBeats: 4, velocity: 80 }];

      expect(() => songSchema.node('chord', { ...chordAttrs(0), notes })).toThrowError(/notes/);
      expect(() => songSchema.node('chord', { ...chordAttrs(0), id: '' })).toThrowError(/id/);
    });

    it('refuses a section kind it does not know', () => {
      const attrs = { id: 's1', label: 'Verse', kind: 'refrain' };

      expect(() => songSchema.node('section', attrs, [line()])).toThrowError(/kind/);
    });

    it('refuses a song key, tempo or time signature that could not be played', () => {
      const sections = [section('s1', 'Verse 1', line())];
      const songWith = (meta: Partial<SongMeta>): Node => songSchema.node('doc', { ...META, ...meta }, sections);

      expect(() => songWith({ key: { ...C_MAJOR, tonic: 12 } })).toThrowError(/key/);
      expect(() => songWith({ tempo: 1000 })).toThrowError(/tempo/);
      expect(() => songWith({ timeSignature: { numerator: 4, denominator: 3, isCommon: false } })).toThrowError(
        /time signature/
      );
    });

    it('checks an attribute set by a step, not only one given at creation', () => {
      const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(chordNode(0))));
      const tr = EditorState.create({ doc }).tr;

      expect(() => tr.setNodeAttribute(2, 'lengthBeats', Number.NaN)).toThrowError(/lengthBeats/);
    });
  });

  describe('the clipboard', () => {
    it('carries a chord\'s whole slot through copy and paste', () => {
      const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('Wondering ', chordNode(5), 'where')));
      const copied = doc.slice(2, 2 + 'Wondering '.length + 1 + 'where'.length);

      const pasted = throughClipboard(copied);
      const [chord] = chordsIn(pasted.content);

      expect(chord.attrs).toEqual(chordsIn(doc)[0].attrs);
      expect(pasted.content.textBetween(0, pasted.content.size)).toBe('Wondering where');
    });

    it('carries a whole section, its label and kind included', () => {
      const doc = song(
        section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one')),
        songSchema.node('section', { id: 's2', label: 'Chorus 2', kind: 'chorus' }, [line(chordNode(0), 'two')])
      );
      const second = doc.child(0).nodeSize;

      const pasted = throughClipboard(doc.slice(second, doc.content.size));

      expect(pasted.content.firstChild?.attrs).toEqual({ id: 's2', label: 'Chorus 2', kind: 'chorus' });
      expect(chordsIn(pasted.content).length).toBe(1);
    });

    it('drops a chord whose data cannot be read, rather than inventing one', () => {
      const container = document.createElement('div');
      container.innerHTML =
        '<p>one <span data-chord="{not json">x</span>two <span data-chord=\'{"id":"c"}\'></span>three</p>';

      const pasted = DOMParser.fromSchema(songSchema).parseSlice(container);

      expect(chordsIn(pasted.content).length).toBe(0);
      expect(pasted.content.textBetween(0, pasted.content.size)).toBe('one xtwo three');
    });

    it('reads a plain paragraph from elsewhere as a lyric line', () => {
      const container = document.createElement('div');
      container.innerHTML = '<p>Got me thinking</p>';

      const pasted = DOMParser.fromSchema(songSchema).parseSlice(container);

      expect(pasted.content.firstChild?.type.name).toBe('lyricLine');
      expect(pasted.content.firstChild?.textContent).toBe('Got me thinking');
    });
  });
});

function degreeOf(attrs: ChordAtomAttrs): object {
  if (attrs.harmony.kind !== 'degree') throw new Error('expected a degree slot');
  return attrs.harmony.degree;
}

/** The attributes the schema keeps from a set that also carried a `startBeat`. */
function withoutStartBeat(attrs: ChordAtomAttrs & { startBeat: number }): ChordAtomAttrs {
  return { id: attrs.id, harmony: attrs.harmony, lengthBeats: attrs.lengthBeats, notes: attrs.notes, owned: attrs.owned };
}

```ts
import type { ScoreDoc, TimeSignature } from './composer.model';
import type { ChordSlot, ProgressionKey } from './progression.model';

/**
 * A song: one ProseMirror document, and the few facts the library keeps beside
 * it.
 *
 * Everything that defines the song lives in `content` - its key, tempo,
 * sections, words and chords - so one undo history covers all of it and a later
 * sync provider (design Part 8) syncs one thing. The fields around `content`
 * are the record's, not the song's: which record it is, how many times it has
 * been written, and when.
 *
 * The schema that `content` follows is `services/song-schema.ts`; the
 * derivations that read it are `services/song-document.ts`. This file holds
 * only the shapes, so a module that stores or lists songs need not import
 * ProseMirror to name them.
 */
export interface SongDoc {
  id: string;
  /**
   * How many times the record has been written, counting from 0 for one never
   * saved. The library bumps it on each save, so two copies of a song can be
   * told apart without comparing their content.
   */
  revision: number;
  /**
   * Epoch milliseconds rather than `Date`, unlike `CompositionEntry`: a number
   * survives `JSON.stringify` - which an export or a sync message goes through -
   * where a `Date` comes back as a string nobody re-parses.
   */
  createdAt: number;
  updatedAt: number;
  /**
   * The ProseMirror document as `Node.toJSON()` writes it.
   *
   * Typed loosely on purpose: a record read back from IndexedDB is whatever was
   * stored, which after a bug or a hand-edited import may not be a song at all.
   * `songNodeOf` is the one door from this to a document, and it refuses with a
   * reason rather than trusting the type.
   */
  content: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;
}

/**
 * What the library's list shows for one song, without the content.
 *
 * Derived from the record by `songSummaryOf` rather than stored beside it, so
 * the card can never disagree with the sheet it opens.
 */
export interface SongSummary {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  artist: string;
  /** Null exactly when `unreadable` is set: a song that cannot be read has no key to show. */
  key: ProgressionKey | null;
  sectionCount: number;
  updatedAt: number;
  /**
   * Why the song's content cannot be opened, or null when it can.
   *
   * A corrupt record still gets a card - with its title if the title is still
   * readable - so the user can see it is there and delete it. Leaving it off the
   * list would be dropping it silently, which the design rules out (Part 6).
   */
  unreadable: string | null;
}

/**
 * The song's own facts: the `doc` node's attributes.
 *
 * On the document rather than beside it so a key change or a tempo change is a
 * step in the same undo history as the words (design Part 1). Every section
 * shares them; a section's progression borrows them (`sectionProgressionOf`).
 */
export interface SongMeta {
  title: string;
  artist: string;
  /** Reused from the progression page as it is, `preferSharps` included. */
  key: ProgressionKey;
  /** BPM. */
  tempo: number;
  timeSignature: TimeSignature;
}

/**
 * What a section is for.
 *
 * `pre` is a pre-chorus. The kind is what the section *is*; the label is what
 * it is *called* ("Chorus 2", "Middle eight"), and the two are kept apart so a
 * renamed section still plays, prints and exports as what it is.
 */
export type SectionKind = 'intro' | 'verse' | 'pre' | 'chorus' | 'bridge' | 'outro' | 'other';

/** Every kind, in the order a song usually meets them; the "+ Section" menu's order. */
export const SECTION_KINDS: readonly SectionKind[] = Object.freeze([
  'intro',
  'verse',
  'pre',
  'chorus',
  'bridge',
  'outro',
  'other'
]);

/** A section node's attributes. */
export interface SectionAttrs {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  kind: SectionKind;
}

/**
 * A chord atom's attributes: a whole `ChordSlot`, less its `startBeat`.
 *
 * **`startBeat` is left out on purpose.** It is derived - the beats of the
 * chords before this one in its section, summed - so a stored copy could only
 * ever agree with that sum or be wrong, and every move, insert and delete would
 * have to rewrite every later atom to keep it agreeing. Omitting it makes the
 * wrong state unrepresentable; `sectionProgressionOf` puts it back.
 *
 * Built from `ChordSlot` rather than listed again, so a field the progression
 * model gains is a field the atom must carry: the schema's per-attribute
 * checks (`CHORD_CHECKS` in `song-schema.ts`) and `atomAttrsOf` stop compiling
 * until it does.
 */
export type ChordAtomAttrs = Omit<ChordSlot, 'startBeat'>;

/**
 * A tab block's attributes (milestone S3). Declared in S1 so a song saved now
 * opens unchanged when tab blocks arrive: no schema migration.
 */
export interface TabBlockAttrs {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  /** One track, in the composer's model, kept to the song's tempo and time signature. */
  score: ScoreDoc;
}

/**
 * A voice memo's attributes (milestone S4), declared now for the same reason as
 * `TabBlockAttrs`.
 *
 * The audio is not here. It lives in its own store, keyed by `id`, so binary
 * data stays out of the undo history and out of a future sync (design Part 1).
 */
export interface MemoAttrs {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  durationSec: number;
}
```

<!-- apply: create client/src/app/services/song-document.ts -->
```ts
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { Plugin } from 'prosemirror-state';
import { Mappable, Mapping } from 'prosemirror-transform';
import type { TimeSignature } from '../models/composer.model';
import {
  ChordDegree,
  ChordSlot,
  ProgressionDoc,
  ProgressionKey,
  createDegreeSlot
} from '../models/progression.model';
import {
  ChordAtomAttrs,
  SectionKind,
  SongDoc,
  SongMeta,
  SongSummary
} from '../models/song.model';
import { messageOf } from './error-message';
import { regenerateSlot, settle } from './progression-edit';
import { barBeats } from './progression-score';
import { NEW_SECTION, songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * Reading and building song documents: the derivations over `songSchema`, and
 * the few constructors that make new nodes.
 *
 * Pure but for ids. Every function here reads a document and returns a value,
 * except the constructors, which also draw fresh UUIDs - `createSongContent`,
 * `createSectionNode`, `chordSlotOf` - and the id plugin, which writes them.
 * Nothing here holds state: the document is the state (design Part 1), and
 * everything a page shows about a song - its sections, a section's
 * progression, its library card - is derived from it on demand and never
 * stored (design Part 8).
 */

/** What a document read from storage turned out to be. */
export type SongReading = { kind: 'song'; doc: Node } | { kind: 'refused'; reason: string };

/** A section, where it is, and the facts a header or a menu needs. */
export interface SongSection {
  id: string;
  label: string;
  kind: SectionKind;
  /** The document position just before the section, so `doc.nodeAt(pos)` is `node`. */
  pos: number;
  node: Node;
}

/** A chord atom and its document position (`doc.nodeAt(pos)` is the atom). */
export interface ChordAt {
  attrs: ChordAtomAttrs;
  pos: number;
}

/** What a progression is called when the song it came from has no title yet. */
const UNTITLED_SONG = 'Untitled song';

/** The node types that carry an `id`, and so must carry a unique one. */
const IDENTIFIED: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['section', 'chord', 'tabBlock', 'memo']);

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Constructors
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The facts a new song starts with: untitled, C major, 100 BPM, 4/4.
 *
 * 100 rather than the progression page's 120 because a song starts at a
 * singing tempo, and the design's mock-up (Part 2) shows it. C ionian with
 * `preferSharps: true` is `createDefaultProgression`'s key and the reason is
 * the same - it is what `MusicTheoryService` starts on and what `setKey` would
 * derive for an empty signature. The title is empty rather than a placeholder
 * word, so "not named yet" is blankness and the page can show a hint for it.
 */
function newSongMeta(): SongMeta {
  return {
    title: '',
    artist: '',
    key: { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true },
    tempo: 100,
    timeSignature: { numerator: 4, denominator: 4, isCommon: true }
  };
}

/**
 * A new song: the defaults above under whatever `meta` says, and one "Verse 1"
 * holding one empty lyric line for the caret.
 *
 * Returns the node, not JSON: the editor needs the node, and the one caller
 * that stores it calls `toJSON()` once.
 */
export function createSongContent(meta: Partial<SongMeta> = {}): Node {
  return songSchema.node('doc', { ...newSongMeta(), ...meta }, [
    createSectionNode(NEW_SECTION.label, NEW_SECTION.kind)
  ]);
}

/** A section with a fresh id, holding one empty lyric line. */
export function createSectionNode(label: string, kind: SectionKind): Node {
  return songSchema.node('section', { id: crypto.randomUUID(), label, kind }, [
    songSchema.node('lyricLine')
  ]);
}

/**
 * A new chord atom's attributes: `degree` in `key`, one bar of the song's time
 * signature long, voiced, owning nothing, with a fresh id.
 *
 * Built through `createDegreeSlot` and `regenerateSlot` - the progression
 * page's own road to a slot - so a chord placed on the sheet is the same object
 * the palette would have made, and its notes are there before anything plays
 * it. Two things differ from the factory's defaults, on purpose:
 *
 * - **The whole `degree` is written**, not only its index: a typed `Gsus4` or
 *   `G7b9` keeps its suspension and extensions, which `chosen` would clear.
 * - **The length is one bar of the song's meter** (`barBeats`), not
 *   `createDegreeSlot`'s fixed 4, which is one bar only in 4/4. Beats are
 *   quarter notes, as everywhere in the progression model, so 3/4 gives 3 and
 *   6/8 gives 3 too.
 *
 * The id is `createDegreeSlot`'s, which is `crypto.randomUUID()`: fresh per
 * call. `scaleIntervals` null - a key whose scale cannot build chords - leaves
 * the notes empty, as `regenerateSlot` does; the sheet refuses chord entry in
 * such a key before it gets here.
 */
export function chordSlotOf(
  degree: ChordDegree,
  key: ProgressionKey,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[] | null,
  timeSignature: TimeSignature
): ChordAtomAttrs {
  const fresh = createDegreeSlot(degree.degree, 0);
  const slot = regenerateSlot(
    { ...fresh, harmony: { kind: 'degree', degree }, lengthBeats: barBeats(timeSignature) },
    key,
    scaleIntervals
  );
  return atomAttrsOf(slot);
}

/**
 * A slot's atom attributes. Listed rather than spread, so a field `ChordSlot`
 * gains is a compile error here rather than a field the atom silently drops.
 */
function atomAttrsOf(slot: ChordSlot): ChordAtomAttrs {
  return { id: slot.id, harmony: slot.harmony, lengthBeats: slot.lengthBeats, notes: slot.notes, owned: slot.owned };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Reading
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A stored song's content as a document, or the reason it cannot be one.
 *
 * Never throws: a corrupt record is a fact to report, not a crash. Everything
 * the schema checks (see `song-schema.ts`) runs here through
 * `Node.fromJSON` and `Node.check()`, and this adds the two rules a schema
 * cannot state: the top node must be a song, and every id must be present and
 * used once. A repeated id would break everything that finds a node by it -
 * Open in Progression's write-back, `requireUniqueSlotIds` - so a record with
 * one is refused rather than repaired by guessing which twin is the real one.
 */
export function songNodeOf(json: unknown): SongReading {
  let doc: Node;
  try {
    doc = Node.fromJSON(songSchema, json);
    doc.check();
  } catch (error) {
    return { kind: 'refused', reason: messageOf(error) };
  }

  if (doc.type !== songSchema.topNodeType) {
    return { kind: 'refused', reason: `This is a ${doc.type.name}, not a song.` };
  }

  const problem = idProblemOf(doc);
  return problem === null ? { kind: 'song', doc } : { kind: 'refused', reason: problem };
}

/** The first missing or repeated id in a document, said as a reason, or null. */
function idProblemOf(doc: Node): string | null {
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const { id, type } of identifiedNodesOf(doc)) {
    if (id === null) return `A ${type} has no id.`;
    if (seen.has(id)) return `The id ${id} is used more than once.`;
    seen.add(id);
  }
  return null;
}

/** Every node that carries an id, in document order. */
function identifiedNodesOf(doc: Node): { id: string | null; type: string; pos: number }[] {
  const found: { id: string | null; type: string; pos: number }[] = [];
  doc.descendants((node, pos) => {
    if (IDENTIFIED.has(node.type.name)) found.push({ id: node.attrs['id'], type: node.type.name, pos });
  });
  return found;
}

/** The song's facts, off the doc node. */
export function songMetaOf(doc: Node): SongMeta {
  const { title, artist, key, tempo, timeSignature } = doc.attrs;
  return { title, artist, key, tempo, timeSignature };
}

/**
 * Every section, in order.
 *
 * Read from a document the editor has published or `songNodeOf` has accepted,
 * where every section has an id. (One ProseMirror has just generated has `null`
 * until `createSongIdsPlugin` runs, which it does before any such document is
 * published.)
 */
export function sectionsOf(doc: Node): SongSection[] {
  const sections: SongSection[] = [];
  doc.forEach((node, offset) => {
    sections.push({ id: node.attrs['id'], label: node.attrs['label'], kind: node.attrs['kind'], pos: offset, node });
  });
  return sections;
}

/**
 * A section's chord atoms in document order, which is the order they play in.
 *
 * `sectionPos` is the section's own position (`SongSection.pos`), so the
 * positions returned are document positions, ready for a transaction.
 */
export function chordsOf(section: Node, sectionPos: number): ChordAt[] {
  const chords: ChordAt[] = [];
  section.descendants((node, offset) => {
    if (node.type.name !== 'chord') return true;
    // The section's content starts one past its own position.
    chords.push({ attrs: node.attrs as ChordAtomAttrs, pos: sectionPos + 1 + offset });
    return false;
  });
  return chords;
}

/**
 * A section's progression, derived: its chord atoms in document order, start
 * beats summed, in the song's key, tempo and time signature. Null when the
 * song has no such section.
 *
 * Derived on every call and never stored, so it cannot fall out of step with
 * the sheet: moving a chord to another word reorders it by construction
 * (design Part 1).
 *
 * - **`id` is the section's id.** The same section gives the same id every
 *   time, which is what lets the hand-off (S1 task 10) recognise "the
 *   progression open on that page is this section's" by comparing one string,
 *   and lets a generated track's `GeneratedOrigin.progressionId` (S2) point at
 *   the section it came from. Section ids are UUIDs, so this cannot collide
 *   with a progression the user made. A song duplicated in the library shares
 *   its section ids with the original until the library re-ids it; the
 *   hand-off keys on the song id as well, so the two are still told apart.
 * - **`revision` is 0**, a progression's "never committed" value, as in
 *   `createDefaultProgression`. A derived progression has no history of its
 *   own, and `ProgressionStore.replaceDocument` re-issues the revision anyway;
 *   the hand-off records the one the store gives it.
 * - **It goes through `settle`**, the store's own normalise-then-reflow, so the
 *   result is already the fixed point the store would make of it: handed to
 *   `replaceDocument`, no `startBeat` moves and no length is clamped behind the
 *   sheet's back. `settle` also rebuilds every slot, key and note, so nothing
 *   in the result is shared with the document's attributes - an edit to it can
 *   never reach back into an immutable ProseMirror node.
 */
export function sectionProgressionOf(doc: Node, sectionId: string): ProgressionDoc | null {
  const section = sectionsOf(doc).find(entry => entry.id === sectionId);
  if (section === undefined) return null;

  const meta = songMetaOf(doc);
  const title = meta.title.trim() === '' ? UNTITLED_SONG : meta.title.trim();

  return settle({
    id: section.id,
    revision: 0,
    name: `${title} — ${section.label}`,
    key: meta.key,
    tempo: meta.tempo,
    timeSignature: { ...meta.timeSignature },
    // Each atom's start is a placeholder that `settle` replaces with the sum
    // of the lengths before it - the only place a start beat is ever made.
    slots: chordsOf(section.node, section.pos).map(({ attrs }) => ({ ...attrs, startBeat: 0 }))
  });
}

/**
 * A song's library card, from its stored record.
 *
 * Never throws, for the reason `songNodeOf` does not. A record whose content
 * cannot be read still gets a card, carrying the reason and whatever title and
 * artist can still be found on it, so the library can show it and offer to
 * delete it.
 */
export function songSummaryOf(song: SongDoc): SongSummary {
  const reading = songNodeOf(song.content);
  if (reading.kind === 'refused') {
    const attrs = song.content['attrs'];
    const text = (name: string): string => {
      const value = typeof attrs === 'object' && attrs !== null ? (attrs as Record<string, unknown>)[name] : undefined;
      return typeof value === 'string' ? value : '';
    };
    return {
      id: song.id,
      title: text('title'),
      artist: text('artist'),
      key: null,
      sectionCount: 0,
      updatedAt: song.updatedAt,
      unreadable: reading.reason
    };
  }

  const meta = songMetaOf(reading.doc);
  return {
    id: song.id,
    title: meta.title,
    artist: meta.artist,
    key: { ...meta.key },
    sectionCount: reading.doc.childCount,
    updatedAt: song.updatedAt,
    unreadable: null
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Ids
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * The positions, in `after`, of nodes that need a fresh id: every id-bearing
 * node with no id, and every copy of an id that now appears more than once.
 *
 * **Which twin is the copy** is decided by where the original went. For each
 * repeated id, the node that `before` held under it is followed through
 * `mapping` to its place in `after`; the one found there keeps the id, and every
 * other is renewed. So a chord pasted in front of itself, the second half of a
 * split section, and a chord dropped with Ctrl held are all renewed while the
 * original keeps the id the hand-off and any open link know it by. A chord
 * *moved* - deleted and reinserted in one transaction - appears once, and keeps
 * its id. Where no original can be followed (it was deleted and pasted back
 * twice), the first in document order keeps it.
 *
 * This is the one mechanism for unique ids, rather than a rule in the clipboard
 * parser, because ProseMirror runs `transformPasted` on an internal drag before
 * it knows whether the drop moves or copies: renewing there would re-id every
 * chord a user drags to another word.
 */
export function idRepairsOf(before: Node, after: Node, mapping: Mappable): number[] {
  const byId = new Map<string, number[]>();
  const repairs: number[] = [];
  for (const { id, pos } of identifiedNodesOf(after)) {
    if (id === null) repairs.push(pos);
    else byId.set(id, [...(byId.get(id) ?? []), pos]);
  }

  const repeated = [...byId].filter(([, positions]) => positions.length > 1);
  if (repeated.length > 0) {
    const originals = new Map<string, number>();
    for (const { id, pos } of identifiedNodesOf(before)) {
      // Associated forward, so a copy inserted exactly where the original
      // started maps the original past the copy, to where it now is.
      const mapped = mapping.mapResult(pos, 1);
      if (id !== null && !mapped.deletedAfter) originals.set(id, mapped.pos);
    }
    for (const [id, positions] of repeated) {
      const original = originals.get(id);
      const keeper = original !== undefined && positions.includes(original) ? original : positions[0];
      repairs.push(...positions.filter(pos => pos !== keeper));
    }
  }

  return repairs.sort((a, b) => a - b);
}

/**
 * The plugin that keeps every id in a song present and unique, whatever the
 * edit: it gives each position `idRepairsOf` names a fresh UUID, in a
 * transaction appended to the one that made the need.
 *
 * Appended rather than separate, so the history plugin folds it into the same
 * undo step - undoing a paste undoes its new ids with it - and no state with a
 * missing or repeated id is ever published to the view. It walks the whole
 * document on each change; a song is a few hundred nodes, which costs less than
 * the render the change triggers.
 */
export function createSongIdsPlugin(): Plugin {
  return new Plugin({
    appendTransaction: (transactions, oldState, newState) => {
      if (!transactions.some(tr => tr.docChanged)) return null;

      const mapping = new Mapping();
      for (const tr of transactions) mapping.appendMapping(tr.mapping);

      const repairs = idRepairsOf(oldState.doc, newState.doc, mapping);
      if (repairs.length === 0) return null;

      // `setNodeAttribute` replaces no content, so the positions stay valid
      // from one repair to the next.
      const tr = newState.tr;
      for (const pos of repairs) tr.setNodeAttribute(pos, 'id', crypto.randomUUID());
      return tr;
    }
  });
}

```ts
import { DOMOutputSpec, Node, Schema } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { TEMPO_MAX, TEMPO_MIN, createOwnership, normalizeChordSlot } from '../models/progression-normalize';
import type { ChordSlot, LiteralReason, RollNote, SlotHarmony, SlotOwnership } from '../models/progression.model';
import { ChordAtomAttrs, SECTION_KINDS, SectionKind } from '../models/song.model';
import { messageOf } from './error-message';

/**
 * The song's ProseMirror schema: what a song document can hold.
 *
 * ```
 * doc         attrs: title, artist, key, tempo, timeSignature      (SongMeta)
 *  └ section+         attrs: id, label, kind                       (SectionAttrs)
 *     └ (lyricLine | tabBlock | memo)+
 *        lyricLine    inline content: (text | chord)*, no marks
 *        chord        inline atom, attrs: a ChordSlot less startBeat (ChordAtomAttrs)
 *        tabBlock     block atom, attrs: id, name, score            (S3)
 *        memo         block atom, attrs: id, name, durationSec      (S4)
 * ```
 *
 * Design Part 1 has the reasoning; what follows is what the schema itself
 * decides.
 *
 * ## Every attribute is checked, at every door
 *
 * Each attribute carries a `validate`, which ProseMirror runs when a node is
 * created - from JSON, from a parse of pasted HTML, or by a step such as
 * `setNodeAttribute` - and again in `Node.check()`. So a chord the progression
 * model would refuse cannot get into a song by any road, and `songNodeOf` can
 * read a stored record by trusting nothing but this schema. The chord's checks
 * are the progression model's own (`normalizeChordSlot`), run on the one part
 * being checked: the song and the progression page cannot disagree about what a
 * valid chord is.
 *
 * A check *refuses*; it never repairs. `normalizeChordSlot` clamps some values
 * (a length under one beat) rather than throwing, and those pass here and are
 * clamped where they are played, by `sectionProgressionOf`'s `settle`. What it
 * throws on - a fractional MIDI note, a degree outside the scale - is refused.
 *
 * ## A section is never empty
 *
 * Its content is `+`, not `*`: an "empty" section is one holding a single empty
 * lyric line, which is where its caret goes. ProseMirror keeps that true by
 * itself - deleting everything in a section leaves the line, because `lyricLine`
 * is the first type the content expression can generate.
 *
 * The same rule at the top (`section+`) means ProseMirror must be able to
 * *generate* a section - after select-all and delete, say - and it refuses a
 * schema whose required child has a required attribute. So a section's
 * attributes have defaults: `NEW_SECTION`'s label and kind, and an `id` of
 * `null`, meaning "generated, not yet given one". Null is never stored and never
 * seen: `createSongIdsPlugin` gives such a section an id in the same dispatch,
 * and `songNodeOf` refuses a record with one. Every other node's attributes are
 * required, so a stored record missing one is refused rather than filled with a
 * guess.
 *
 * ## The clipboard
 *
 * Copy and paste go through `toDOM` and `parseDOM`. A chord, tab block or memo
 * carries its whole attribute set as JSON in a `data-` attribute, so a copy is
 * exact; a paste re-runs every check above and drops what fails rather than
 * inventing a chord. A pasted copy keeps the ids it was copied with - deciding
 * which of two equal ids is the copy needs the document before and after, so it
 * is `createSongIdsPlugin`'s job, not the parser's.
 */

/** What a section ProseMirror generates is called, and what a new song's first section is. */
export const NEW_SECTION: Readonly<{ label: string; kind: SectionKind }> = Object.freeze({
  label: 'Verse 1',
  kind: 'verse'
});

const LITERAL_REASONS: readonly LiteralReason[] = ['unrecognised', 'user-detached'];

/** A denominator a bar can have: a whole note divided by a power of two. */
const DENOMINATORS: readonly number[] = [1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64];

type Validate = (value: unknown) => void;

function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Readonly<Record<string, unknown>> {
  return typeof value === 'object' && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
}

/** A value, briefly, for a message: enough to recognise, never a whole document. */
function shown(value: unknown): string {
  const text = value === undefined ? 'undefined' : JSON.stringify(value) ?? String(value);
  return text.length > 60 ? `${text.slice(0, 57)}...` : text;
}

function refuse(subject: string, rule: string, value: unknown): never {
  throw new RangeError(`${subject} must be ${rule}; got ${shown(value)}`);
}

function aString(subject: string): Validate {
  return value => {
    if (typeof value !== 'string') refuse(subject, 'text', value);
  };
}

function anId(subject: string): Validate {
  return value => {
    if (typeof value !== 'string' || value === '') refuse(subject, 'a non-empty id', value);
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The song's facts
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A key as `ProgressionKey` has it. The tonic must already be 0-11:
 * `normalizeProgressionKey` would wrap a 12 into a 0, but a stored 12 is a
 * record something wrote wrongly, and a song key every writer bounds has no
 * business arriving out of range.
 */
const validKey: Validate = value => {
  const rule = 'a key: a whole tonic from 0 to 11, a scale id and preferSharps';
  if (!isRecord(value)) refuse('The song key', rule, value);
  const { tonic, scaleId, preferSharps } = value;
  if (typeof tonic !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(tonic) || tonic < 0 || tonic > 11) {
    refuse('The song key', rule, value);
  }
  if (typeof scaleId !== 'string' || scaleId === '' || typeof preferSharps !== 'boolean') {
    refuse('The song key', rule, value);
  }
};

/** Bounded as the progression page bounds it, so a section hands over a tempo it will play. */
const validTempo: Validate = value => {
  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !(value >= TEMPO_MIN && value <= TEMPO_MAX)) {
    refuse('The song tempo', `a BPM from ${TEMPO_MIN} to ${TEMPO_MAX}`, value);
  }
};

const validTimeSignature: Validate = value => {
  const rule = 'a time signature: a whole number of beats over a power of two';
  if (!isRecord(value)) refuse('The song time signature', rule, value);
  const { numerator, denominator, isCommon } = value;
  if (typeof numerator !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(numerator) || numerator < 1) {
    refuse('The song time signature', rule, value);
  }
  if (typeof denominator !== 'number' || !DENOMINATORS.includes(denominator) || typeof isCommon !== 'boolean') {
    refuse('The song time signature', rule, value);
  }
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sections
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** A string id, or null for a section ProseMirror generated (see the header). */
const validSectionId: Validate = value => {
  if (value !== null && (typeof value !== 'string' || value === '')) {
    refuse('A section id', 'a non-empty id', value);
  }
};

const validSectionKind: Validate = value => {
  if (!SECTION_KINDS.includes(value as SectionKind)) {
    refuse('A section kind', `one of ${SECTION_KINDS.join(', ')}`, value);
  }
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Chords
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Runs the progression model's own check on one part of a slot.
 *
 * The other parts come from a slot `normalizeChordSlot` accepts as it is, so
 * whatever it throws is about `part`. A literal harmony stands in for the
 * harmony because it has no degree of its own to check.
 */
function slotPartChecked(name: keyof ChordAtomAttrs, part: Partial<ChordSlot>): void {
  const probe: ChordSlot = {
    id: 'probe',
    harmony: { kind: 'literal', reason: 'unrecognised', from: null },
    startBeat: 0,
    lengthBeats: 1,
    notes: [],
    owned: createOwnership(),
    ...part
  };
  try {
    normalizeChordSlot(probe);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new RangeError(`A chord's ${name} is not one the progression model accepts: ${messageOf(error)}`);
  }
}

/**
 * One check per attribute, and the mapped type makes it every attribute: a
 * field `ChordSlot` gains is a compile error here until it has a check.
 *
 * The shape tests in front of `slotPartChecked` are the ones
 * `normalizeChordSlot` does not make, because the progression page only ever
 * hands it slots it built: that `harmony` is one of the two kinds, that
 * `owned` is an object. Without them a corrupt record would fail with a
 * `TypeError` from inside the model, or not at all.
 */
const CHORD_CHECKS: { readonly [K in keyof ChordAtomAttrs]: Validate } = {
  id: anId("A chord's id"),
  harmony: value => {
    const rule = 'a degree, or a literal chord with its reason';
    if (!isRecord(value)) refuse("A chord's harmony", rule, value);
    if (value['kind'] === 'degree') {
      if (!isRecord(value['degree'])) refuse("A chord's harmony", rule, value);
    } else if (value['kind'] !== 'literal' || !LITERAL_REASONS.includes(value['reason'] as LiteralReason)) {
      refuse("A chord's harmony", rule, value);
    }
    slotPartChecked('harmony', { harmony: value as unknown as SlotHarmony });
  },
  lengthBeats: value => {
    if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value)) refuse("A chord's lengthBeats", 'a number of beats', value);
  },
  notes: value => slotPartChecked('notes', { notes: value as RollNote[] }),
  owned: value => {
    if (!isRecord(value)) refuse("A chord's owned", 'three ownership flags', value);
    slotPartChecked('owned', { owned: value as unknown as SlotOwnership });
  }
};

/** Whether a value is a whole set of chord attributes, by the checks above. */
function isChordAtomAttrs(value: unknown): value is ChordAtomAttrs {
  if (!isRecord(value)) return false;
  try {
    for (const [name, check] of Object.entries(CHORD_CHECKS)) check(value[name]);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

/**
 * The attributes a chord atom keeps, from a set that may carry more.
 *
 * Listed rather than spread, so a stray `startBeat` - or anything else a pasted
 * or foreign object brings - is not carried into the document. (ProseMirror
 * would drop an attribute the schema does not declare anyway; this keeps the
 * parse rule from depending on that.)
 */
function chordAtomAttrsOf(attrs: ChordAtomAttrs): ChordAtomAttrs {
  return { id: attrs.id, harmony: attrs.harmony, lengthBeats: attrs.lengthBeats, notes: attrs.notes, owned: attrs.owned };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tab blocks and memos
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * A tab block's score is checked only for being an object here. Its shape is
 * the composer's model, which S3 opens with the composer's own reader; this
 * schema would otherwise hold a second, weaker copy of those rules.
 */
const validScore: Validate = value => {
  if (!isRecord(value)) refuse("A tab block's score", 'a score document', value);
};

const validDuration: Validate = value => {
  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
    refuse("A memo's durationSec", 'a length in seconds', value);
  }
};

/** A block atom's attributes from its `data-` attribute, or false so the parser skips it. */
function blockAttrsFrom(json: string | null, checks: Readonly<Record<string, Validate>>): Record<string, unknown> | false {
  try {
    const value: unknown = JSON.parse(json ?? '');
    if (!isRecord(value)) return false;
    const attrs: Record<string, unknown> = {};
    for (const [name, check] of Object.entries(checks)) {
      check(value[name]);
      attrs[name] = value[name];
    }
    return attrs;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

const TAB_BLOCK_CHECKS: Readonly<Record<string, Validate>> = {
  id: anId("A tab block's id"),
  name: aString("A tab block's name"),
  score: validScore
};

const MEMO_CHECKS: Readonly<Record<string, Validate>> = {
  id: anId("A memo's id"),
  name: aString("A memo's name"),
  durationSec: validDuration
};

/** Required attributes, each with its check: the form every non-section node uses. */
function required(checks: Readonly<Record<string, Validate>>): Record<string, { validate: Validate }> {
  return Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(checks).map(([name, validate]) => [name, { validate }]));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The schema
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const songSchema = new Schema({
  nodes: {
    doc: {
      content: 'section+',
      attrs: required({
        title: aString('The song title'),
        artist: aString('The song artist'),
        key: validKey,
        tempo: validTempo,
        timeSignature: validTimeSignature
      })
    },

    section: {
      content: '(lyricLine | tabBlock | memo)+',
      attrs: {
        id: { default: null, validate: validSectionId },
        label: { default: NEW_SECTION.label, validate: aString('A section label') },
        kind: { default: NEW_SECTION.kind, validate: validSectionKind }
      },
      // A section boundary is structure, changed from the section's menu: a
      // backspace at the start of a chorus should not pull its first line up
      // into the verse above.
      isolating: true,
      parseDOM: [
        {
          tag: 'section[data-section-id]',
          getAttrs: (dom: HTMLElement) => {
            const kind = dom.getAttribute('data-kind');
            if (!SECTION_KINDS.includes(kind as SectionKind)) return false;
            return {
              id: dom.getAttribute('data-section-id') || null,
              label: dom.getAttribute('data-label') ?? NEW_SECTION.label,
              kind
            };
          }
        }
      ],
      toDOM: (node: Node): DOMOutputSpec => [
        'section',
        {
          class: 'song-section',
          'data-section-id': node.attrs['id'] ?? '',
          'data-label': node.attrs['label'],
          'data-kind': node.attrs['kind']
        },
        0
      ]
    },

    lyricLine: {
      content: 'inline*',
      // Lyrics are words, not formatting: no bold, no links. A paste from a web
      // page comes in as plain words, as a chord sheet's would.
      marks: '',
      parseDOM: [{ tag: 'p' }],
      toDOM: (): DOMOutputSpec => ['p', { class: 'song-lyric-line' }, 0]
    },

    chord: {
      inline: true,
      group: 'inline',
      atom: true,
      // Dragging a chord's name to another letter is how it moves (design Part 2).
      draggable: true,
      attrs: required(CHORD_CHECKS),
      parseDOM: [
        {
          tag: 'span[data-chord]',
          getAttrs: (dom: HTMLElement) => {
            try {
              const value: unknown = JSON.parse(dom.getAttribute('data-chord') ?? '');
              return isChordAtomAttrs(value) ? chordAtomAttrsOf(value) : false;
            } catch {
              return false;
            }
          }
        }
      ],
      toDOM: (node: Node): DOMOutputSpec => [
        'span',
        { class: 'song-chord', 'data-chord': JSON.stringify(node.attrs) }
      ]
    },

    tabBlock: {
      group: 'block',
      atom: true,
      draggable: true,
      attrs: required(TAB_BLOCK_CHECKS),
      parseDOM: [
        {
          tag: 'div[data-tab-block]',
          getAttrs: (dom: HTMLElement) => blockAttrsFrom(dom.getAttribute('data-tab-block'), TAB_BLOCK_CHECKS)
        }
      ],
      toDOM: (node: Node): DOMOutputSpec => [
        'div',
        { class: 'song-tab-block', 'data-tab-block': JSON.stringify(node.attrs) }
      ]
    },

    memo: {
      group: 'block',
      atom: true,
      draggable: true,
      attrs: required(MEMO_CHECKS),
      parseDOM: [
        {
          tag: 'div[data-memo]',
          getAttrs: (dom: HTMLElement) => blockAttrsFrom(dom.getAttribute('data-memo'), MEMO_CHECKS)
        }
      ],
      toDOM: (node: Node): DOMOutputSpec => ['div', { class: 'song-memo', 'data-memo': JSON.stringify(node.attrs) }]
    },

    text: { group: 'inline' }
  },
  marks: {}
});

### Task B.2: Editing a song: commands and the editor plugins

Every edit the sheet makes, as a pure command over a headless state: chords placed, changed, lengthened,
moved and removed; sections added, renamed, moved, duplicated and deleted; the key, Transpose, tempo, time signature,
title and artist. Each returns an edit, a refusal with its reason, or "unchanged", and each is one undo step.
`rekeyedSlot` comes out of `ProgressionDegreeEditor` for the key commands.

`songEditorPlugins` is the sheet's whole plugin list: history, the id plugin, the keymap - Enter splits a line and never
a section, arrows step over chords - the `[Section]` rule, and the hook through which `[` asks for the chord field.

import { ChordSlot, ProgressionKey, createDegreeSlot } from '../models/progression.model';
import { rekeyedSlot } from './progression-degree-editor';
import { regenerateSlot } from './progression-edit';

/**
 * `rekeyedSlot`, the pure half of `ProgressionDegreeEditor.rekey`.
 *
 * Its behaviour is pinned through the service in `progression.service.rekey.spec.ts`
 * and `progression.service.regenerate.spec.ts`; these two specs hold the function
 * itself to the rule the song sheet re-keys its chord atoms by, without a store.
 */
describe('rekeyedSlot', () => {
  const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];
  const AEOLIAN = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10];
  const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
  const A_MINOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 9, scaleId: 'aeolian', preferSharps: false };
  const C_MINOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'aeolian', preferSharps: false };

  function voiced(degree: number): ChordSlot {
    return regenerateSlot(createDegreeSlot(degree, 0), C_MAJOR, IONIAN);
  }

  function pitchClassesOf(slot: ChordSlot): number[] {
    return [...new Set(slot.notes.map(note => note.midi % 12))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  }

  it('keeps a slot that does not own its pitches on its degree, and voices it in the new key', () => {
    const fifth = voiced(4);

    const moved = rekeyedSlot(fifth, IONIAN, AEOLIAN, A_MINOR, -3);

    expect(moved.harmony).toEqual(fifth.harmony);
    // v in A minor: E, G, B.
    expect(pitchClassesOf(moved)).toEqual([4, 7, 11]);
  });

  it('keeps the pitches of a slot that owns them, and numbers them again in the new key', () => {
    const tonic = voiced(0);
    const owned: ChordSlot = { ...tonic, owned: { ...tonic.owned, pitches: true } };

    // Same tonic, new mode: nothing transposes, so the pitches stay exactly put.
    const moved = rekeyedSlot(owned, IONIAN, AEOLIAN, C_MINOR, 0);

    expect(moved.notes).toEqual(owned.notes);
    // C, E, G is still a major chord on the tonic, so it is written I with its
    // major third pinned: the bare degree would now read i, over notes it is not.
    expect(moved.harmony).toEqual({
      kind: 'degree',
      degree: jasmine.objectContaining({ degree: 0, alter: 0, quality: 'major', inversion: 0, octave: 0 })
    });
    expect(tonic.harmony).toEqual({ kind: 'degree', degree: jasmine.objectContaining({ quality: null }) });
  });
});

```ts
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { history, undo, undoDepth } from 'prosemirror-history';
import {
  AllSelection,
  EditorState,
  NodeSelection,
  Selection,
  TextSelection,
  Transaction
} from 'prosemirror-state';
import { createExtensions } from '../models/progression-normalize';
import { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../models/progression.model';
import { ChordAtomAttrs, SongMeta } from '../models/song.model';
import { MusicTheoryService } from './music-theory.service';
import { ProgressionKeyContext } from './progression-key-context';
import {
  SongEdit,
  SongEditOutcome,
  addSection,
  chordWithId,
  commandOf,
  copyLabelOf,
  deleteChord,
  deleteSection,
  duplicateSection,
  insertChord,
  isSongCommand,
  moveChordBy,
  moveChordTo,
  moveSection,
  renameSection,
  replaceChord,
  selectedChordOf,
  setArtist,
  setChordLength,
  setSongKey,
  setTempo,
  setTimeSignature,
  setTitle,
  transposeSong
} from './song-commands';
import { chordSlotOf, chordsOf, createSongIdsPlugin, sectionsOf, songMetaOf, songNodeOf } from './song-document';
import { songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * The song sheet's commands, on a headless `EditorState`.
 *
 * Each edit is run twice over in spirit: as a `SongEdit`, whose outcome says
 * what it would do or why it will not, and - in the `commandOf` specs - as the
 * ProseMirror `Command` the page and the keymap call. Every state carries the
 * history and id plugins the editor runs with, so "one undo step" is asked of
 * the real history.
 */
const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];
const FOUR_FOUR = { numerator: 4, denominator: 4, isCommon: true };
const META: SongMeta = { title: 'Last Dance', artist: 'The Band', key: C_MAJOR, tempo: 100, timeSignature: FOUR_FOUR };

const keys = new ProgressionKeyContext(new MusicTheoryService());

function degreeAt(degree: number): ChordDegree {
  return {
    degree,
    alter: 0,
    extent: 3,
    quality: null,
    inversion: 0,
    suspension: 'none',
    extensions: createExtensions(),
    octave: 0
  };
}

/** A voiced C major chord atom's attributes on `degree`, one bar long. */
function chordAttrs(degree: number): ChordAtomAttrs {
  return chordSlotOf(degreeAt(degree), C_MAJOR, IONIAN, FOUR_FOUR);
}

function chord(degree: number): Node {
  return songSchema.node('chord', chordAttrs(degree));
}

function line(...content: (string | Node)[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node(
    'lyricLine',
    null,
    content.map(part => (typeof part === 'string' ? songSchema.text(part) : part))
  );
}

function section(id: string, label: string, ...lines: Node[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node('section', { id, label, kind: label === 'Chorus' ? 'chorus' : 'verse' }, lines);
}

function song(...sections: Node[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node('doc', META, sections);
}

function stateOf(doc: Node, selection?: (doc: Node) => Selection): EditorState {
  return EditorState.create({
    doc,
    selection: selection?.(doc),
    plugins: [history(), createSongIdsPlugin()]
  });
}

/** The position just before the first `text` in the document. */
function before(doc: Node, text: string): number {
  let found = -1;
  doc.descendants((node, pos) => {
    if (found >= 0) return false;
    const at = node.isText ? (node.text ?? '').indexOf(text) : -1;
    if (at >= 0) found = pos + at;
    return true;
  });
  if (found < 0) throw new Error(`no "${text}" in the document`);
  return found;
}

function caret(pos: number): (doc: Node) => Selection {
  return doc => TextSelection.create(doc, pos);
}

/** Each line as its words with each chord written `[degree]` where it sits. */
function sheetOf(doc: Node): string[] {
  const lines: string[] = [];
  doc.descendants(node => {
    if (node.type.name !== 'lyricLine') return true;
    let text = '';
    node.forEach(child => {
      if (child.isText) text += child.text;
      else if (child.type.name === 'chord') {
        const harmony = child.attrs['harmony'];
        text += `[${harmony.kind === 'degree' ? harmony.degree.degree : '?'}]`;
      }
    });
    lines.push(text);
    return false;
  });
  return lines;
}

function labelsOf(doc: Node): string[] {
  return sectionsOf(doc).map(entry => entry.label);
}

function edited(outcome: SongEditOutcome): Transaction {
  if (outcome.kind !== 'edit') throw new Error(`expected an edit, got ${JSON.stringify(outcome)}`);
  return outcome.tr;
}

/** `edit` applied, through the plugins, as the editor would apply it. */
function run(state: EditorState, edit: SongEdit): EditorState {
  return state.apply(edited(edit(state)));
}

function reasonOf(state: EditorState, edit: SongEdit): string {
  const outcome = edit(state);
  if (outcome.kind !== 'refused') throw new Error(`expected a refusal, got ${outcome.kind}`);
  return outcome.reason;
}

/** The state after one undo. */
function undone(state: EditorState): EditorState {
  let after = state;
  expect(undo(state, tr => (after = state.apply(tr)))).toBeTrue();
  return after;
}

/** That `edit` is one undo step: one more on the stack, and one undo puts the document back. */
function expectOneUndoStep(state: EditorState, edit: SongEdit): void {
  const after = run(state, edit);
  expect(undoDepth(after)).toBe(undoDepth(state) + 1);
  expect(undone(after).doc.eq(state.doc)).toBeTrue();
}

function pitchClassesOf(attrs: ChordAtomAttrs): number[] {
  return [...new Set(attrs.notes.map(note => note.midi % 12))].sort((a, b) => a - b);
}

function onlyChord(doc: Node): ChordAtomAttrs {
  const all = sectionsOf(doc).flatMap(entry => chordsOf(entry.node, entry.pos));
  expect(all.length).toBe(1);
  return all[0].attrs;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

describe('commandOf', () => {
  const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('Wondering')));

  it('dispatches the edit and answers true', () => {
    const state = stateOf(doc, caret(2));
    let dispatched: Transaction | null = null;

    expect(commandOf(insertChord(chordAttrs(5)))(state, tr => (dispatched = tr))).toBeTrue();
    expect(dispatched).not.toBeNull();
  });

  it('answers false, dispatches nothing and says why when the edit is refused', () => {
    const state = stateOf(doc, () => new AllSelection(doc));
    const reasons: string[] = [];
    const dispatch = jasmine.createSpy('dispatch');

    expect(commandOf(insertChord(chordAttrs(5)), reason => reasons.push(reason))(state, dispatch)).toBeFalse();
    expect(dispatch).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(reasons).toEqual([reasonOf(state, insertChord(chordAttrs(5)))]);
  });

  it('only answers when asked without a dispatch, and reports no refusal', () => {
    const refuse = jasmine.createSpy('refuse');
    const command = commandOf(insertChord(chordAttrs(5)), refuse);

    expect(command(stateOf(doc, caret(2)))).toBeTrue();
    expect(command(stateOf(doc, () => new AllSelection(doc)))).toBeFalse();
    expect(refuse).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('answers false and reports nothing when there is nothing to change', () => {
    const refuse = jasmine.createSpy('refuse');
    const dispatch = jasmine.createSpy('dispatch');

    expect(commandOf(setTitle('Last Dance'), refuse)(stateOf(doc), dispatch)).toBeFalse();
    expect(refuse).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(dispatch).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('marks each edit as a command, so the editor can close its undo step', () => {
    const state = stateOf(doc, caret(2));

    expect(isSongCommand(edited(insertChord(chordAttrs(5))(state)))).toBeTrue();
    expect(isSongCommand(state.tr.insertText('x'))).toBeFalse();
  });
});

      expect(copied.attrs.id).not.toBe(am.attrs['id']);

      expect(songNodeOf(after.toJSON()).kind).toBe('song');
    });

    it('numbers the copy of a numbered section on, and keeps an unnumbered name', () => {
      expect(labelsOf(run(stateOf(withChords), duplicateSection('s1')).doc)).toEqual(['Verse 1', 'Verse 2', 'Chorus']);
      expect(labelsOf(run(stateOf(withChords), duplicateSection('s2')).doc)).toEqual(['Verse 1', 'Chorus', 'Chorus']);
    });

    it('leaves a voice memo out of the copy, since its recording belongs to the original', () => {
      const memo = songSchema.node('memo', { id: 'memo-1', name: 'Take 1', durationSec: 12 });
      const withMemo = song(songSchema.node('section', { id: 's1', label: 'Verse 1', kind: 'verse' }, [memo]));

    });

      expectOneUndoStep(stateOf(withChords), duplicateSection('s1'));
    });
  });

  describe('copyLabelOf', () => {
    it('numbers past the highest number its name already has in the song', () => {
      expect(copyLabelOf('Verse 1', ['Verse 1', 'Chorus'])).toBe('Verse 2');
      expect(copyLabelOf('Verse 1', ['Verse 1', 'Verse 2', 'verse 3'])).toBe('Verse 4');
      expect(copyLabelOf('Chorus', ['Chorus'])).toBe('Chorus');
      expect(copyLabelOf('Take 5', ['Take 5'])).toBe('Take 6');

    it('takes the section and everything in it out', () => {
      expect(labelsOf(run(stateOf(doc), deleteSection('s1')).doc)).toEqual(['Chorus']);
    });

    it('refuses to delete the last section, or one that is not in the song', () => {
      const one = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one')));

      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), deleteSection('gone'))).toMatch(/no longer in the song/);
    });

    it('leaves the caret in a line', () => {
      const after = run(stateOf(doc, caret(before(doc, 'two'))), deleteSection('s1'));

      expect(after.selection.$head.parent.type.name).toBe('lyricLine');
    });

    it('is one undo step', () => {
      expectOneUndoStep(stateOf(doc), deleteSection('s1'));
    });
  });
});

describe('song commands', () => {

    function withOwnedTonic(): Node {

      const owned = songSchema.node('chord', { ...attrs, owned: { ...attrs.owned, pitches: true } });
      return song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(owned, 'Wondering')));
    }

    }

      const after = run(stateOf(doc), setSongKey(keys, 7, 'ionian')).doc;
      const [tonic, dominant] = chordsIn(after);

      expect(songMetaOf(after).key).toEqual({ tonic: 7, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true });
      expect(tonic.harmony).toEqual(one.attrs['harmony']);
      expect(dominant.harmony).toEqual(five.attrs['harmony']);
      // I and V in G: G B D and D F# A.
      expect(pitchClassesOf(tonic)).toEqual([2, 7, 11]);
      expect(pitchClassesOf(dominant)).toEqual([2, 6, 9]);
    });

    it('carries a chord whose pitches are owned with the tonic', () => {
      const [tonic] = chordsIn(run(stateOf(withOwnedTonic()), setSongKey(keys, 2, 'ionian')).doc);

      expect(tonic.owned.pitches).toBeTrue();
    });

      const before = chordsIn(withOwnedTonic())[0];

      const [tonic] = chordsIn(run(stateOf(withOwnedTonic()), setSongKey(keys, 0, 'aeolian')).doc);

      expect(tonic.harmony).toEqual({ kind: 'degree', degree: jasmine.objectContaining({ degree: 0, quality: 'major' }) });
    });

      const attrs = five.attrs as ChordAtomAttrs;
      const literal = songSchema.node('chord', {
        ...attrs,
        harmony: { kind: 'literal', reason: 'user-detached', from: null }
      });
      const literalSong = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(literal, 'Wondering')));

      const [after] = chordsIn(run(stateOf(literalSong), setSongKey(keys, 7, 'ionian')).doc);

      expect(after.notes).toEqual(attrs.notes);
    });

    it('spells the key from its signature, unless told which spelling', () => {
      const keyAfter = (tonic: number, preferSharps?: boolean): ProgressionKey =>
        songMetaOf(run(stateOf(doc), setSongKey(keys, tonic, 'ionian', preferSharps)).doc).key;

      expect(keyAfter(5).preferSharps).toBeFalse();
      expect(keyAfter(2).preferSharps).toBeTrue();
      expect(keyAfter(6).preferSharps).toBeTrue();
      expect(keyAfter(6, false).preferSharps).toBeFalse();
    });

    it('is one undo step that puts back the key and every chord', () => {
      expectOneUndoStep(stateOf(doc), setSongKey(keys, 9, 'aeolian'));
    });

    it('refuses a scale that cannot build chords, naming it', () => {
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setSongKey(keys, 0, 'majorPentatonic'))).toMatch(/Major Pentatonic/);
    });

    it('refuses a scale it does not know, and a tonic that is not a pitch class', () => {
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setSongKey(keys, 0, 'nonsense'))).toMatch(/nonsense/);
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setSongKey(keys, 1.5, 'ionian'))).toMatch(/tonic/i);
    });

    it('wraps a tonic past B round to a pitch class', () => {
      expect(songMetaOf(run(stateOf(doc), setSongKey(keys, 14, 'ionian')).doc).key.tonic).toBe(2);
    });

    it('changes nothing when the key is the one the song is in', () => {
      expect(setSongKey(keys, 0, 'ionian')(stateOf(doc)).kind).toBe('unchanged');
    });
  });

  describe('transposeSong', () => {
    const one = chord(0);
    const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(one, 'Wondering')));

    it('moves the tonic a semitone, chords and all, spelling the new key from its signature', () => {
      const up = run(stateOf(doc), transposeSong(keys, 1)).doc;
      const down = run(stateOf(doc), transposeSong(keys, -1)).doc;

      expect(songMetaOf(up).key).toEqual({ tonic: 1, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: false });
      expect(songMetaOf(down).key).toEqual({ tonic: 11, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true });
      expect(pitchClassesOf(onlyChord(up))).toEqual([1, 5, 8]);
      expect(onlyChord(up).harmony).toEqual(one.attrs['harmony']);
    });

    it('refuses in a key whose scale cannot build chords', () => {
      const pentatonic = songSchema.node('doc', { ...META, key: { ...C_MAJOR, scaleId: 'majorPentatonic' } }, [
        section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('Wondering'))
      ]);

      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(pentatonic), transposeSong(keys, 1))).toMatch(/Major Pentatonic/);
    });

    it('is one undo step', () => {
      expectOneUndoStep(stateOf(doc), transposeSong(keys, 1));
    });
  });

  describe('setTempo', () => {
    const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one')));

    it('sets the BPM', () => {
      expect(songMetaOf(run(stateOf(doc), setTempo(72)).doc).tempo).toBe(72);
    });

    it('refuses a tempo outside what the player can play, or no number at all', () => {
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setTempo(10))).toMatch(/20 to 300/);
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setTempo(301))).toMatch(/20 to 300/);
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setTempo(Number.NaN))).toMatch(/20 to 300/);
      expect(setTempo(100)(stateOf(doc)).kind).toBe('unchanged');
    });

    it('is one undo step', () => {
      expectOneUndoStep(stateOf(doc), setTempo(72));
    });
  });

  describe('setTimeSignature', () => {
    const am = chord(5);
    const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(am, 'one')));
    const threeFour = { numerator: 3, denominator: 4, isCommon: false };

    it('sets the meter and leaves every chord the length it was, in beats', () => {
      const after = run(stateOf(doc), setTimeSignature(threeFour)).doc;

      expect(songMetaOf(after).timeSignature).toEqual(threeFour);
      expect(onlyChord(after)).toEqual(am.attrs as ChordAtomAttrs);
    });

    it('refuses a meter a bar cannot have', () => {
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setTimeSignature({ ...threeFour, numerator: 0 }))).toMatch(/time signature/);
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setTimeSignature({ ...threeFour, numerator: 2.5 }))).toMatch(/time signature/);
      expect(reasonOf(stateOf(doc), setTimeSignature({ ...threeFour, denominator: 3 }))).toMatch(/time signature/);
      expect(setTimeSignature({ ...FOUR_FOUR })(stateOf(doc)).kind).toBe('unchanged');
    });

    it('is one undo step', () => {
      expectOneUndoStep(stateOf(doc), setTimeSignature(threeFour));
    });
  });

  describe('setTitle and setArtist', () => {
    const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one')));

    it('set the song\'s title and artist as typed', () => {
      const after = run(run(stateOf(doc), setTitle('First Dance ')), setArtist('Another Band')).doc;

      expect(songMetaOf(after).title).toBe('First Dance ');
      expect(songMetaOf(after).artist).toBe('Another Band');
    });

    it('change nothing when the text is the same', () => {
      expect(setTitle('Last Dance')(stateOf(doc)).kind).toBe('unchanged');
      expect(setArtist('The Band')(stateOf(doc)).kind).toBe('unchanged');
    });

    it('are one undo step each', () => {
      expectOneUndoStep(stateOf(doc), setTitle('First Dance'));
      expectOneUndoStep(stateOf(doc), setArtist('Another Band'));
    });
  });
});

```ts
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { redoDepth, undoDepth } from 'prosemirror-history';
import { EditorState, NodeSelection, Selection, TextSelection, Transaction } from 'prosemirror-state';
import { EditorView } from 'prosemirror-view';
import { createExtensions } from '../models/progression-normalize';
import { ProgressionKey } from '../models/progression.model';
import { SongMeta } from '../models/song.model';
import { chordWithId, commandOf, insertChord, setTitle } from './song-commands';
import { chordSlotOf, sectionsOf } from './song-document';
import {
  ChordFieldRequest,
  SongEditorOptions,
  requestChordField,
  sectionHeadingOf,
  songEditorPlugins
} from './song-editor-plugins';
import { songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * The sheet's plugin list: history, ids, keys, the `[Chorus]` rule and the
 * chord field's hook.
 *
 * Keys and typed text go through a real `EditorView` on a detached element,
 * because that is where ProseMirror routes them (`handleKeyDown`,
 * `handleTextInput`); nothing is attached to the page, and every view is
 * destroyed after its spec. History grouping is asked of a bare state, as the
 * view would apply the same transactions.
 */
const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const FOUR_FOUR = { numerator: 4, denominator: 4, isCommon: true };
const META: SongMeta = { title: 'Last Dance', artist: '', key: C_MAJOR, tempo: 100, timeSignature: FOUR_FOUR };
const MAC = /Mac|iP(hone|[oa]d)/.test(navigator.platform);

function chord(degree: number): Node {
  return songSchema.node(
    'chord',
    chordSlotOf(
      {
        degree,
        alter: 0,
        extent: 3,
        quality: null,
        inversion: 0,
        suspension: 'none',
        extensions: createExtensions(),
        octave: 0
      },
      C_MAJOR,
      [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11],
      FOUR_FOUR
    )
  );
}

function line(...content: (string | Node)[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node(
    'lyricLine',
    null,
    content.map(part => (typeof part === 'string' ? songSchema.text(part) : part))
  );
}

function section(id: string, label: string, ...lines: Node[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node('section', { id, label, kind: 'verse' }, lines);
}

function song(...sections: Node[]): Node {
  return songSchema.node('doc', META, sections);
}

/** The position just before the first `text` in the document. */
function before(doc: Node, text: string): number {
  let found = -1;
  doc.descendants((node, pos) => {
    const at = node.isText && found < 0 ? (node.text ?? '').indexOf(text) : -1;
    if (at >= 0) found = pos + at;
  });
  if (found < 0) throw new Error(`no "${text}" in the document`);
  return found;
}

/** Each section as its label, kind and lines, chords written `*`. */
function outlineOf(doc: Node): string[] {
  return sectionsOf(doc).map(entry => {
    const lines: string[] = [];
    entry.node.forEach(child => {
      let text = '';
      child.forEach(inline => (text += inline.isText ? inline.text : '*'));
      lines.push(text);
    });
    return `${entry.label} (${entry.kind}): ${lines.join(' / ')}`;
  });
}

describe('songEditorPlugins', () => {
  let view: EditorView | null = null;

  afterEach(() => {
    view?.destroy();
    view = null;
  });

  function viewOf(doc: Node, selection?: (doc: Node) => Selection, options: SongEditorOptions = {}): EditorView {
    const state = EditorState.create({ doc, selection: selection?.(doc), plugins: songEditorPlugins(options) });
    view = new EditorView(document.createElement('div'), { state });
    return view;
  }

  function caret(pos: number): (doc: Node) => Selection {
    return doc => TextSelection.create(doc, pos);
  }

  /** Presses a key as the browser would report it; answers whether the editor took it. */
  function press(target: EditorView, key: string, modifiers: { mod?: boolean; shift?: boolean; alt?: boolean } = {}): boolean {
    const event = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {
      key,
      // The keymap falls back to the key code for a shifted letter.
      keyCode: key.length === 1 ? key.toUpperCase().charCodeAt(0) : 0,
      shiftKey: modifiers.shift ?? false,
      altKey: modifiers.alt ?? false,
      ctrlKey: (modifiers.mod ?? false) && !MAC,
      metaKey: (modifiers.mod ?? false) && MAC
    });
    return target.someProp('handleKeyDown', handle => handle(target, event)) ?? false;
  }

  /** Types `text` one character at a time, as input events would: plugins first, else inserted. */
  function type(target: EditorView, text: string): void {
    for (const character of text) {
      const { from, to } = target.state.selection;
      const typed = (): Transaction => target.state.tr.insertText(character, from, to);
      const handled = target.someProp('handleTextInput', handle => handle(target, from, to, character, typed));
      if (!handled) target.dispatch(typed());
    }
  }

  describe('history', () => {
    const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one')));

    function stateOf(): EditorState {
      return EditorState.create({ doc, selection: TextSelection.create(doc, 5), plugins: songEditorPlugins() });
    }

    it('groups typing as ProseMirror does: a run of adjacent letters is one step', () => {
      let state = stateOf();
      state = state.apply(state.tr.insertText('a'));
      state = state.apply(state.tr.insertText('b'));

      expect(undoDepth(state)).toBe(1);
    });

    it('keeps a command its own step, apart from the typing before it and after it', () => {
      let state = stateOf();
      state = state.apply(state.tr.insertText('a'));
      const command = insertChord(chordSlotOf(
        { degree: 0, alter: 0, extent: 3, quality: null, inversion: 0, suspension: 'none', extensions: createExtensions(), octave: 0 },
        C_MAJOR, [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11], FOUR_FOUR
      ))(state);
      if (command.kind !== 'edit') throw new Error('expected the chord to go in');
      state = state.apply(command.tr);
      state = state.apply(state.tr.insertText('b'));

      expect(undoDepth(state)).toBe(3);
    });

    it('keeps two commands in a row two steps', () => {
      let state = stateOf();
      for (const title of ['First', 'Second']) {
        commandOf(setTitle(title))(state, tr => (state = state.apply(tr)));
      }

      expect(undoDepth(state)).toBe(2);
    });

    it('gives a section the editor splits an id in the same step', () => {
      let state = stateOf();
      state = state.apply(state.tr.split(5, 2));

      expect(sectionsOf(state.doc).map(entry => entry.id)).toEqual(['s1', jasmine.stringMatching(/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/)]);
      expect(undoDepth(state)).toBe(1);
    });
  });

  describe('undo and redo keys', () => {
    it('undo with Mod-z, redo with Mod-y and Mod-Shift-z', () => {
      const editor = viewOf(song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one'))), caret(5));
      type(editor, 'x');

      expect(press(editor, 'z', { mod: true })).toBeTrue();
      expect(editor.state.doc.textContent).toBe('one');
      expect(press(editor, 'y', { mod: true })).toBeTrue();

  });

  describe('Enter', () => {
    it('splits a lyric line at the caret, inside its section', () => {

      const editor = viewOf(doc, caret(before(doc, ' two')));

    it('splits after a selected chord, keeping it', () => {

  describe('Backspace and Delete', () => {
    const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one'), line('two')), section('s2', 'Chorus', line('three')));
