```ts
      expect(outlineOf(editor.state.doc)).toEqual(['Verse 1 (verse): one', 'Bridge (bridge):  / two']);
    });

    it('renames the section in place when typed on its first line, keeping its id', () => {
      const fresh = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(), line('one')));
      const editor = viewOf(fresh, caret(2));

      type(editor, '[Intro]');

      expect(outlineOf(editor.state.doc)).toEqual(['Intro (intro):  / one']);
      expect(sectionsOf(editor.state.doc)[0].id).toBe('s1');
    });

    it('leaves the brackets as words on a line that has anything else on it', () => {
      const editor = viewOf(doc, caret(5));

      type(editor, ' [Chorus]');

      expect(outlineOf(editor.state.doc)).toEqual(['Verse 1 (verse): one [Chorus] / ']);
    });

    it('is one undo step, which leaves the heading as it was typed but for its bracket', () => {
      const editor = viewOf(doc, atEnd);
      type(editor, '[Chorus]');
      expect(sectionsOf(editor.state.doc).length).toBe(2);

      press(editor, 'z', { mod: true });

      expect(outlineOf(editor.state.doc)).toEqual(['Verse 1 (verse): one / [Chorus']);
    });

    it('gives the heading back as typed on a Backspace straight after', () => {
      const editor = viewOf(doc, atEnd);
      type(editor, '[Chorus]');
      expect(sectionsOf(editor.state.doc).length).toBe(2);

      press(editor, 'Backspace');

      expect(outlineOf(editor.state.doc)).toEqual(['Verse 1 (verse): one / [Chorus]']);
    });
  });

  describe('sectionHeadingOf', () => {
    it('reads the six section words, in any case, with an optional number, as their kinds', () => {
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('Intro')).toEqual({ kind: 'intro', label: 'Intro' });
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('Verse 2')).toEqual({ kind: 'verse', label: 'Verse 2' });
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('pre-chorus')).toEqual({ kind: 'pre', label: 'pre-chorus' });
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('Pre Chorus')).toEqual({ kind: 'pre', label: 'Pre Chorus' });
      expect(sectionHeadingOf(' CHORUS ')).toEqual({ kind: 'chorus', label: 'CHORUS' });
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('Bridge')).toEqual({ kind: 'bridge', label: 'Bridge' });
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('Outro3')).toEqual({ kind: 'outro', label: 'Outro3' });
    });

    it('reads any other name as a section of kind other, and nothing as no heading', () => {
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('Middle eight')).toEqual({ kind: 'other', label: 'Middle eight' });
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('Verses')).toEqual({ kind: 'other', label: 'Verses' });
      expect(sectionHeadingOf('   ')).toBeNull();
    });
  });

  describe('the chord field', () => {
    const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('Wondering'), line()));
    const coords = { left: 10, right: 10, top: 20, bottom: 36 };
    const fakeView = { coordsAtPos: () => coords };

    function stateAt(pos: number): EditorState {
      return EditorState.create({ doc, selection: TextSelection.create(doc, pos) });
    }

    it('is asked for on a line with words, at the caret, with where the caret is on screen', () => {
      const requests: ChordFieldRequest[] = [];

      expect(requestChordField(stateAt(5), fakeView, request => requests.push(request))).toBeTrue();
      expect(requests).toEqual([{ pos: 5, coords: { left: 10, top: 20, bottom: 36 } }]);
    });

    it('is asked for without coordinates when there is no view to measure', () => {
      const requests: ChordFieldRequest[] = [];
      requestChordField(stateAt(5), undefined, request => requests.push(request));

      expect(requests).toEqual([{ pos: 5, coords: null }]);
    });

    it('is not asked for on an empty line, where [ starts a section heading instead', () => {
      const request = jasmine.createSpy('request');

      expect(requestChordField(stateAt(doc.content.size - 2), fakeView, request)).toBeFalse();
      expect(request).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });

    it('opens on [ typed into a line with words, and the [ is not typed', () => {
      const requests: ChordFieldRequest[] = [];
      const editor = viewOf(doc, caret(5), { onChordFieldRequest: request => requests.push(request) });

      type(editor, '[');

      expect(requests.map(request => request.pos)).toEqual([5]);
      expect(editor.state.doc.eq(doc)).toBeTrue();
    });

    it('lets [ be typed on an empty line, so [Chorus] still makes a section', () => {
      const requests: ChordFieldRequest[] = [];
      const editor = viewOf(doc, d => Selection.atEnd(d), { onChordFieldRequest: request => requests.push(request) });

      type(editor, '[Chorus]');

      expect(requests).toEqual([]);
      expect(outlineOf(editor.state.doc)).toEqual(['Verse 1 (verse): Wondering', 'Chorus (chorus): ']);
    });
  });
});
```

```ts
  /**
   * Moves one slot into a new key: the notes as `regenerate` has always moved
   * them, and - for a slot that owns its pitches - the *label* re-spelled so it

   * leaves `harmony` exactly as it found it. That is right while only the tonic
   * moves - a hand-voiced `I` in C is a hand-voiced `I` in D - and it is wrong
   * the moment the **mode** moves with it. Click the relative minor on the
   * circle and a hand-edited `I` in C major transposes to A, C♯, E and keeps a
   * card reading `i`: a major triad under a minor numeral, sounded by the synth
   * and printed on the strip, with nothing to tell the user the two disagree.
   * A silent mislabel is the one thing this page is built not to do.
   *
   * ## The rule: a key change never changes what an owned chord is
   *
   * So the identity is taken in the key being **left** - `effectiveChord` over
   * the degree as it stood - and written back through `expressInKey` in the key
   * being entered. Nothing is recognised and no notice is raised, because
   * nothing about the chord changed: `I` in C major and `I` in A minor are the
   * same three pitch classes relative to their tonics, and all that moved is
   * which numeral and which pins the new key needs to write them down.
   *
   * That is the same last step the recogniser ends with, called with an
   * identity that was never parsed - which is what `expressInKey` takes an
   * identity rather than a `ParsedChord` for. Nothing here reads a note.
   *
   * **Only a slot that owns its pitches.** One that does not is re-voiced from
   * its degree and so already sounds whatever the new key makes of that degree,
   * which is the behaviour the whole merge exists to give it; re-spelling it
   * would pin a quality onto a slot that was happily leaving the answer to the
   * key. A literal slot is left alone: it has no degree to re-express, and its
   * notes are the truth in every key.
   *

   *
   * `expressInKey` reads the inversion off a bass note and takes an octave,
   * because the recogniser learns both from where the user's notes happen to
   * sit. Here they are already known and neither is part of the identity, so

   * the spelling, not the register - and reading the inversion off the
   * transposed voicing instead would let a chord the user left in root position
   * come back as a second inversion because the anchor put a different note at
   * the bottom.
   *
   * Writing the octave back is a no-op on the degree route, where the stored
   * octave is what went in and `atDegree`'s clamp cannot move a value the store
   * has already bounded. It is load-bearing on the notes route below, which gets
   * its octave from where the bass happens to sit and would otherwise quietly
   * rewrite what the user asked the octave control for - visible the next time
   * Reset to chord regenerates the slot.

   * source of truth is gone the moment that key's scale will not resolve -

   * somewhere is an ordinary thing to do. Keeping the label as it stood is then
```

```ts
    transposeBy: number
  ): ChordSlot {
    const moved = this.regenerate(slot, key, transposeBy);
    if (moved.harmony.kind !== 'degree' || !moved.owned.pitches) return moved;

    const entering = this.keys.chordScaleFor(key);
    if (entering === null) return moved;

    const degree = moved.harmony.degree;
    const written = this.identityInKey(moved, leaving, entering, key, degree);
    if (written === undefined) return moved;
    if (written === null) return { ...moved, harmony: literalHarmony('unrecognised', degree) };

    // The register is kept rather than re-derived, on both routes and for the
    // reason given above: a key change moves the spelling, not where the chord
    // stands. The notes route reads a bass that the anchor may just have moved,
    // which makes overwriting it the more necessary there, not the less.
    return {
      ...moved,
      harmony: {
        kind: 'degree',
        degree: { ...written, inversion: degree.inversion, octave: degree.octave }
      }
    };
  }

  /**
   * What the chord in `slot` is, written as a degree of the key it is entering.
   *
   * Three answers, and the third is why this is a method rather than an
   * expression: `undefined` is "there is nothing to ask", which `rekey` answers
   * by leaving the slot exactly as it found it, and is a different thing from
   * the `null` that means "asked, and this key has no numeral for it".
   *
   * Which source the identity comes from is the whole of the decision. The
   * degree in the key being left is the better one where it exists - it is what
   * the user chose, and reading it needs no interpretation - so it is tried
   * first, and the notes are the fallback for the case where that key's scale
   * will not resolve.
   */
  private identityInKey(
    slot: ChordSlot,
    leaving: readonly number[] | null,
    entering: readonly number[],
    key: ProgressionKey,
    degree: ChordDegree
  ): ChordDegree | null | undefined {
    if (leaving !== null) {
      const identity = effectiveChord(leaving, degree);
      // The root as the bass, so the position `expressInKey` computes is the one
      // `rekey` overwrites. What the chord is does not depend on it either way.
      return expressInKey(identity, entering, degree.octave, identity.root);
    }

    if (slot.notes.length === 0) return undefined;
    return expressNotesInKey(slot.notes, slot.lengthBeats, key, entering);
  }
```

```ts
export function rekeyedSlot(
  slot: ChordSlot,
  leaving: readonly number[] | null,
  entering: readonly number[] | null,
  key: ProgressionKey,
  transposeBy: number
): ChordSlot {
  const moved = regenerateSlot(slot, key, entering, transposeBy);
  if (moved.harmony.kind !== 'degree' || !moved.owned.pitches) return moved;
  if (entering === null) return moved;

  const degree = moved.harmony.degree;
  const written = identityInKey(moved, leaving, entering, key, degree);
  if (written === undefined) return moved;
  if (written === null) return { ...moved, harmony: literalHarmony('unrecognised', degree) };

  // The register is kept rather than re-derived, on both routes and for the
  // reason given above: a key change moves the spelling, not where the chord
  // stands. The notes route reads a bass that the anchor may just have moved,
  // which makes overwriting it the more necessary there, not the less.
  return {
    ...moved,
    harmony: {
      kind: 'degree',
      degree: { ...written, inversion: degree.inversion, octave: degree.octave }
    }
  };
}

/**
 * What the chord in `slot` is, written as a degree of the key it is entering.
 *
 * Three answers, and the third is why this is a function rather than an
 * expression: `undefined` is "there is nothing to ask", which `rekeyedSlot`
 * answers by leaving the slot exactly as it found it, and is a different thing
 * from the `null` that means "asked, and this key has no numeral for it".
 *
 * Which source the identity comes from is the whole of the decision. The
 * degree in the key being left is the better one where it exists - it is what
 * the user chose, and reading it needs no interpretation - so it is tried
 * first, and the notes are the fallback for the case where that key's scale
 * will not resolve.
 */
function identityInKey(
  slot: ChordSlot,
  leaving: readonly number[] | null,
  entering: readonly number[],
  key: ProgressionKey,
  degree: ChordDegree
): ChordDegree | null | undefined {
  if (leaving !== null) {
    const identity = effectiveChord(leaving, degree);
    // The root as the bass, so the position `expressInKey` computes is the one
    // `rekeyedSlot` overwrites. What the chord is does not depend on it either way.
    return expressInKey(identity, entering, degree.octave, identity.root);
  }

  if (slot.notes.length === 0) return undefined;
  return expressNotesInKey(slot.notes, slot.lengthBeats, key, entering);
}
```

```ts
import { closeHistory } from 'prosemirror-history';

import { messageOf } from './error-message';
import { rekeyedSlot } from './progression-degree-editor';
import { keyTransposeInterval, retimeNotes } from './progression-edit';
import type { ProgressionKeyContext } from './progression-key-context';
import { ChordAt, SongSection, atomAttrsOf, createSectionNode, sectionsOf, songMetaOf } from './song-document';
import { songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * Editing a song: every change the sheet makes to a song document other than
 * typing, as an edit that either builds one transaction or says why it will

 *

 * edit's arguments and returning a `SongEdit` - a function of the editor state
 * - and `commandOf` turns one into the ProseMirror `Command` a keymap or a
 * button calls. Nothing here holds state; the document is the state (design
 * Part 1), and an edit reads it, never a copy.
 *
 * ## Refusals: an outcome, not an exception and not a bare `false`
 *
 * A ProseMirror command can only answer true or false, and false means both
 * "not here" and "not allowed". The sheet needs to tell the user which, and
 * why, so each edit returns a `SongEditOutcome` - the composer's rule
 * (`ComposerHistory.commit`: an edit returns a reason, which refuses it and
 * commits nothing) in the shape ProseMirror wants:
 *
 * - `edit` carries the one transaction to dispatch;
 * - `refused` carries a sentence the user can act on, which `commandOf` hands
 *   to its `onRefuse` callback - the page's status line - only when it was
 *   asked to *run*, never when a menu merely asks whether it *could* (a command
 *   called without `dispatch`);
 * - `unchanged` is an edit that would change nothing - a rename to the same
 *   name, a tempo field committed at the tempo it shows. It is not refused,
 *   because nothing is wrong, and not dispatched, because an empty step on the
 *   undo stack is a press of Ctrl+Z that does nothing visible. That is the
 *   progression page's rule too (`editDegree`: "an edit that changes nothing is
 *   not recorded").
 *
 * The outcome is the testable channel: a spec asks an edit what it would do
 * without a dispatch to capture, and the reason is the same string the page
 * shows.
 *
 * ## One edit, one undo step
 *
 * Every transaction an edit builds is marked with `closeHistory`, so the
 * history does not fold it into the typing before it, and with a meta flag
 * (`isSongCommand`) that the editor's plugin list reads to close the step
 * after it as well - so typing straight after a chord goes in does not join
 * the chord's step either (`song-editor-plugins.ts`). The id plugin's repair,
 * appended to the same dispatch, is folded into the step it repairs.
 *
 * ## Positions never leave the document
 *
 * Chords and sections are named by id, and found again in the state the edit
 * is run on (`chordWithId`, `sectionsOf`). A popover holding a chord's id can
 * run an edit after any amount of typing and still reach the right chord - or
 * be told it is gone - where a held position would quietly hit a neighbour.
 * The one position an edit takes is `moveChordTo`'s drop target, which the
 * view computes from the pointer in the same event that runs it.
 */

/** What an edit makes of the state it is run on. See the header. */
export type SongEditOutcome =
  | { kind: 'edit'; tr: Transaction }
  | { kind: 'unchanged' }
  | { kind: 'refused'; reason: string };

/** An edit: a function of the editor state, building one transaction or saying why not. */
export type SongEdit = (state: EditorState) => SongEditOutcome;

/**
 * What the key commands ask of the app's scales: exactly the three questions
 * `ProgressionService.setKey` asks, so the song and the progression page
 * answer a key change by one set of rules.
 *
 * A `ProgressionKeyContext` is one, and the page hands its own over; it is
 * named as a `Pick` so the commands stay pure - they are handed the rules
 * rather than reaching for `MusicTheoryService` - and so a spec can see the
 * whole of what they depend on.
 */
export type SongKeyRules = Pick<ProgressionKeyContext, 'findScale' | 'chordScaleFor' | 'spellingFor'>;

const OUTSIDE_LINE = 'Put the caret in a line of lyrics to add a chord there.';
const GONE_CHORD = 'That chord is no longer in the song.';
const DUPLICATE_CHORD = 'That chord is already in the song; a copy needs an id of its own.';
const NOT_BEATS = "A chord's length must be a number of beats.";
const AT_LINE_START = 'The chord is already at the start of its line.';
const AT_LINE_END = 'The chord is already at the end of its line.';
const DROP_OUTSIDE = 'A chord can only be dropped onto a line of lyrics.';
const GONE_SECTION = 'That section is no longer in the song.';
const BLANK_LABEL = 'A section needs a name.';
const FIRST_SECTION = 'This is already the first section.';
const LAST_SECTION = 'This is already the last section.';
const ONLY_SECTION = 'A song keeps at least one section.';

/** The meta flag `edited` sets; read through `isSongCommand`. */
const SONG_COMMAND = 'songCommand';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The channel
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function refused(reason: string): SongEditOutcome {
  return { kind: 'refused', reason };
}

const UNCHANGED: SongEditOutcome = { kind: 'unchanged' };

/** A transaction as an edit's outcome. */
function edited(tr: Transaction): SongEditOutcome {
  return { kind: 'edit', tr: markSongCommand(tr) };
}

/**
 * Makes `tr` one undo step of its own: closed off from the history before it,
 * and flagged so the editor closes the step after it too (see the header).
 *
 * Every edit here goes through it; it is exported for the one change the
 * sheet makes outside this file that is a command rather than typing - the
 * `[Chorus]` input rule, whose transaction ProseMirror's input-rule plugin
 * builds and dispatches itself.
 */
export function markSongCommand(tr: Transaction): Transaction {
  return closeHistory(tr).setMeta(SONG_COMMAND, true);
}

/**
 * An edit as a ProseMirror `Command`.
 *
 * Follows the command contract: without `dispatch` it only answers whether the
 * edit would run, so a menu can enable or dim an item by asking. With
 * `dispatch`, an edit dispatches its transaction and a refusal is handed to
 * `onRefuse` - once, at the press - before answering false.
 */
export function commandOf(edit: SongEdit, onRefuse?: (reason: string) => void): Command {
  return (state, dispatch) => {
    const outcome = edit(state);
    if (outcome.kind === 'edit') {
      dispatch?.(outcome.tr);
      return true;
    }
    if (outcome.kind === 'refused' && dispatch !== undefined) onRefuse?.(outcome.reason);
    return false;
  };
}

/** Whether a transaction was built by one of the edits here. */
export function isSongCommand(tr: Transaction): boolean {
  return tr.getMeta(SONG_COMMAND) === true;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Finding things
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

function isLyricLine(node: Node): boolean {
  return node.type === songSchema.nodes.lyricLine;
}

function isChord(node: Node | null | undefined): boolean {
  return node?.type === songSchema.nodes.chord;
}

/** Every chord atom in the song, in document order. */
function chordsIn(doc: Node): ChordAt[] {
  const chords: ChordAt[] = [];
  doc.descendants((node, pos) => {
    if (isChord(node)) chords.push({ attrs: node.attrs as ChordAtomAttrs, pos });
    // Nothing nests inside an inline node, so a line's children are the last
    // level worth walking.
    return !node.isInline;
  });
  return chords;
}

/** The chord atom with `id`, and where it is, or null when the song has none. */
export function chordWithId(doc: Node, id: string): ChordAt | null {
  return chordsIn(doc).find(chord => chord.attrs.id === id) ?? null;
}

/**
 * The chord the selection is on, or null.
 *
 * A chord is selected when the selection is a `NodeSelection` of its atom -
 * what clicking its name makes, and what Alt+arrows act on.
 */
export function selectedChordOf(state: EditorState): ChordAt | null {
  const selection = state.selection;
  if (!(selection instanceof NodeSelection) || !isChord(selection.node)) return null;
  return { attrs: selection.node.attrs as ChordAtomAttrs, pos: selection.from };
}

function sectionWithId(doc: Node, id: string): SongSection | null {
  return sectionsOf(doc).find(section => section.id === id) ?? null;
}

/**
 * The index of the section holding the selection's head.
 *
 * At the top level - between sections, where a section's own `NodeSelection`
 * or a select-all ends - that is the section just before the head: the one
 * the user was last in.
 */
function sectionIndexAtHead(state: EditorState): number {
  const $head = state.selection.$head;
  if ($head.depth > 0) return $head.index(0);
  return Math.max(0, $head.index(0) - 1);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Checking and writing attributes
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Two attribute values as the document would store them, compared. */
function sameValue(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  return JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);
}

/**
 * A chord atom built from `attrs` and put through the schema's own checks
 * (`CHORD_CHECKS`, the progression model's rules), or the reason it failed.
 *
 * ProseMirror runs an attribute's `validate` in `Node.check()`, not when a
 * node is created or a step applied, so an edit that brings a chord in from
 * outside the document checks it here, once, rather than trusting the caller.
 */
function checkedChord(attrs: ChordAtomAttrs): Node | string {
  try {
    const node = songSchema.nodes.chord.create({
      id: attrs.id,
      harmony: attrs.harmony,
      lengthBeats: attrs.lengthBeats,
      notes: attrs.notes,
      owned: attrs.owned
    });
    node.check();
    return node;
  } catch (error) {
    return messageOf(error);
  }
}

/**
 * Writes a chord's slot attributes over the atom at `pos`, each only where it
 * changed, leaving its id.
 *
 * Attribute steps rather than a replacement, because an attribute step maps no
 * position: a selected chord stays selected, and the caret beside it stays
 * beside it.
 */
function writeChord(tr: Transaction, pos: number, next: ChordAtomAttrs, current: ChordAtomAttrs): void {
  for (const name of ['harmony', 'lengthBeats', 'notes', 'owned'] as const) {
    if (!sameValue(next[name], current[name])) tr.setNodeAttribute(pos, name, next[name]);
  }
}

/** A chord atom's attributes as a progression slot, for the slot functions. */
function slotOf(attrs: ChordAtomAttrs): ChordSlot {
  // The start is a placeholder: these slots are edited one at a time and
  // never laid out, and an atom's start is derived (`sectionProgressionOf`).
  return { ...attrs, startBeat: 0 };
}

/**
 * Why `value` cannot be the song's `name` attribute, by the schema's own check,
 * or null when it can. One rule for the song's facts, stated in the schema.
 */
function songAttributeProblem(name: keyof SongMeta, value: unknown): string | null {
  const validate = songSchema.topNodeType.spec.attrs?.[name]?.validate;
  if (typeof validate !== 'function') return null;
  try {
    validate(value);
    return null;
  } catch (error) {
    return messageOf(error);
  }
}

/** An edit writing one of the song's facts: checked, and unchanged when it is already so. */
function songAttributeEdit<K extends keyof SongMeta>(name: K, value: SongMeta[K]): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const problem = songAttributeProblem(name, value);
    if (problem !== null) return refused(problem);
    if (sameValue(songMetaOf(state.doc)[name], value)) return UNCHANGED;
    return edited(state.tr.setDocAttribute(name, value));
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Chords
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Puts a chord atom at the caret: before the character the caret is in front
 * of, which is the letter the chord's name will sit over. With a selection it
 * goes at the selection's start and the selected words are left alone - a
 * chord is placed on words, never in place of them.
 *
 * `attrs` comes from `chordSlotOf`, so it is voiced and has a fresh id. A
 * chord the schema refuses, or one whose id the song already holds, is
 * refused rather than repaired: either is a caller's mistake, and repairing it
 * here would hide it.
 */
export function insertChord(attrs: ChordAtomAttrs): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const $from = state.selection.$from;
    if (!isLyricLine($from.parent)) return refused(OUTSIDE_LINE);
    if (chordWithId(state.doc, attrs.id) !== null) return refused(DUPLICATE_CHORD);

    const node = checkedChord(attrs);
    if (typeof node === 'string') return refused(node);
    return edited(state.tr.insert($from.pos, node));
  };
}

/**
 * Writes a different chord over the chord `id`, which keeps its id and its
 * place: the popover's "change chord". Any id on `attrs` is ignored.
 */
export function replaceChord(id: string, attrs: Omit<ChordAtomAttrs, 'id'>): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const found = chordWithId(state.doc, id);
    if (found === null) return refused(GONE_CHORD);

    const node = checkedChord({ ...attrs, id });
    if (typeof node === 'string') return refused(node);
    const next = node.attrs as ChordAtomAttrs;
    if (sameValue(next, found.attrs)) return UNCHANGED;

    const tr = state.tr;
    writeChord(tr, found.pos, next, found.attrs);
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

/**
 * Sets how long the chord `id` plays, in beats (quarter notes).
 *
 * By the progression page's own road (`ProgressionService.setSlotLength`):
 * the length is bounded by `normalizeChordSlot` - under one beat is held at
 * one, `MIN_SLOT_BEATS` - and the voicing is re-timed to it by `retimeNotes`,
 * which leaves alone a slot that owns its timing. Only a length that is not a
 * number at all is refused, since there is nothing to bound.
 */
export function setChordLength(id: string, beats: number): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    if (!Number.isFinite(beats)) return refused(NOT_BEATS);
    const found = chordWithId(state.doc, id);
    if (found === null) return refused(GONE_CHORD);

    const resized = retimeNotes(normalizeChordSlot({ ...slotOf(found.attrs), lengthBeats: beats }));
    if (resized.lengthBeats === found.attrs.lengthBeats) return UNCHANGED;

    const tr = state.tr;
    writeChord(tr, found.pos, atomAttrsOf(resized), found.attrs);
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

/** Takes the chord `id` out of the song. The words it sat over stay. */
export function deleteChord(id: string): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const found = chordWithId(state.doc, id);
    if (found === null) return refused(GONE_CHORD);
    return edited(state.tr.delete(found.pos, found.pos + 1));
  };
}

/**
 * How many positions the character beside `$pos` takes: two for a character
 * written as a UTF-16 surrogate pair (most emoji), one otherwise - so a chord
 * moved one character never lands between the halves of one, and nor does the
 * caret the arrow keys step past a chord (`song-editor-plugins.ts`).
 *
 * `nodeAfter` and `nodeBefore` are cut at the position, so the character next
 * to it is the first of the one and the last of the other.
 */
export function characterWidthAt($pos: ResolvedPos, dir: -1 | 1): number {
  const text = (dir > 0 ? $pos.nodeAfter : $pos.nodeBefore)?.text ?? '';
  const pair = dir > 0 ? text.slice(0, 2) : text.slice(-2);
  return pair.length === 2 && /^[\uD800-\uDBFF][\uDC00-\uDFFF]$/.test(pair) ? 2 : 1;
}

/**
 * Where the chord at `pos` lands moved one character in `dir`, or why it
 * cannot move: past any chords beside it - they take no width in the words -
 * and over one character, landing right beside that character. Never past
 * either end of its line.
 */
function oneCharacterOn(doc: Node, pos: number, dir: -1 | 1): number | string {
  const $chord = doc.resolve(pos);
  if (dir > 0) {
    let at = pos + 1;
    const end = $chord.end();
    while (at < end && isChord(doc.resolve(at).nodeAfter)) at++;
    if (at >= end) return AT_LINE_END;
    return at + characterWidthAt(doc.resolve(at), 1);
  }

  let at = pos;
  const start = $chord.start();
  while (at > start && isChord(doc.resolve(at).nodeBefore)) at--;
  if (at <= start) return AT_LINE_START;
  return at - characterWidthAt(doc.resolve(at), -1);
}

/**
 * Moves the chord atom from `from` to `to` (a position in the same document,
 * before the move) in one transaction: deleted and inserted, which the id
 * plugin reads as a move and so leaves the id alone. `at` is where the atom
 * now is.
 */
function movedChord(state: EditorState, from: number, to: number): { tr: Transaction; at: number } {
  const node = state.doc.nodeAt(from);
  // `from` is a chord atom's position, found in this document by the caller.
  if (node === null) throw new Error(`No chord at ${from}`);
  const tr = state.tr.delete(from, from + 1);
  const at = tr.mapping.map(to);
  tr.insert(at, node);
  return { tr, at };
}

/**
 * Moves the chord `id` one character left (`-1`) or right (`1`) in its line:
 * Alt+arrow. Its length does not change - a chord's timing is its own, and the
 * word only places it (design decision 3).
 *
 * "One character" counts letters, not chords: chords take no width in the
 * words, so a chord moves past any others beside it and over the next letter,
 * landing right beside that letter. A chord can sit after a line's last letter
 * (a chord on a held note), so the right edge is the end of the line. It never
 * crosses into the next line - dragging is how a chord goes further - so at
 * either edge it is refused, with which edge in the reason.
 *
 * A selected chord stays selected, so holding Alt and pressing the arrow
 * again keeps walking it.
 */
export function moveChordBy(id: string, delta: -1 | 1): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const found = chordWithId(state.doc, id);
    if (found === null) return refused(GONE_CHORD);

    const target = oneCharacterOn(state.doc, found.pos, delta);
    if (typeof target === 'string') return refused(target);

    const { tr, at } = movedChord(state, found.pos, target);
    if (selectedChordOf(state)?.attrs.id === id) tr.setSelection(NodeSelection.create(tr.doc, at));
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

/**
 * Moves the chord `id` to `pos` - a drop, with `pos` a position in the current
 * document - anywhere in any line of the song, and selects it there, as
 * ProseMirror's own drop selects what it dropped.
 *
 * A drop outside a line of lyrics (between sections, on a tab block) is
 * refused. A drop where the chord already is - on either side of itself - is
 * unchanged.
 */
export function moveChordTo(id: string, pos: number): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const found = chordWithId(state.doc, id);
    if (found === null) return refused(GONE_CHORD);
    if (!Number.isInteger(pos) || pos < 0 || pos > state.doc.content.size) return refused(DROP_OUTSIDE);
    if (!isLyricLine(state.doc.resolve(pos).parent)) return refused(DROP_OUTSIDE);
    if (pos === found.pos || pos === found.pos + 1) return UNCHANGED;

    const { tr, at } = movedChord(state, found.pos, pos);
    tr.setSelection(NodeSelection.create(tr.doc, at));
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Sections
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** A section's name as stored - trimmed - or the reason it cannot be one. */
function labelProblem(label: string, kind: SectionKind): string | null {
  if (!SECTION_KINDS.includes(kind)) return `A section's kind is one of ${SECTION_KINDS.join(', ')}; got ${kind}.`;
  return label.trim() === '' ? BLANK_LABEL : null;
}

/**
 * Adds a new, empty section of `kind` called `label` right after the section
 * holding the caret, and puts the caret in its first line - "+ Section".
 */
export function addSection(kind: SectionKind, label: string): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const problem = labelProblem(label, kind);
    if (problem !== null) return refused(problem);

    const after = sectionsOf(state.doc)[sectionIndexAtHead(state)];
    const at = after.pos + after.node.nodeSize;
    const tr = state.tr.insert(at, createSectionNode(label.trim(), kind));
    // One into the section, one into its first line.
    tr.setSelection(TextSelection.create(tr.doc, at + 2));
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

/** Renames the section `id`, and changes its kind when `kind` is given. */
export function renameSection(id: string, label: string, kind?: SectionKind): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const section = sectionWithId(state.doc, id);
    if (section === null) return refused(GONE_SECTION);
    const nextKind = kind ?? section.kind;
    const problem = labelProblem(label, nextKind);
    if (problem !== null) return refused(problem);

    const name = label.trim();
    if (name === section.label && nextKind === section.kind) return UNCHANGED;
    const tr = state.tr.setNodeAttribute(section.pos, 'label', name);
    if (nextKind !== section.kind) tr.setNodeAttribute(section.pos, 'kind', nextKind);
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

/**
 * `selection` moved by `shift` positions into `doc`: the caret or chord
 * selection of a section that has just been moved, kept where it was in it.
 */
function shiftedSelection(selection: Selection, shift: number, doc: Node): Selection {
  if (selection instanceof NodeSelection) return NodeSelection.create(doc, selection.from + shift);
  if (selection instanceof TextSelection) {
    return TextSelection.create(doc, selection.anchor + shift, selection.head + shift);
  }
  return Selection.near(doc.resolve(selection.head + shift));
}

/**
 * Moves the section `id` up (`-1`) or down (`1`) past its neighbour. The
 * caret, if it was in the section, goes with it.
 */
export function moveSection(id: string, delta: -1 | 1): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const sections = sectionsOf(state.doc);
    const index = sections.findIndex(section => section.id === id);
    if (index < 0) return refused(GONE_SECTION);
    if (delta < 0 && index === 0) return refused(FIRST_SECTION);
    if (delta > 0 && index === sections.length - 1) return refused(LAST_SECTION);

    const moving = sections[index];
    const neighbour = sections[index + delta];
    const end = moving.pos + moving.node.nodeSize;
    const tr = state.tr.delete(moving.pos, end);
    const at = delta < 0 ? neighbour.pos : tr.mapping.map(neighbour.pos + neighbour.node.nodeSize);
    tr.insert(at, moving.node);

    const selection = state.selection;
    if (selection.from > moving.pos && selection.to < end) {
      tr.setSelection(shiftedSelection(selection, at - moving.pos, tr.doc));
    }
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

/** A label read as a name and a trailing number: "Verse 2" is "Verse " and 2. */
const NUMBERED = /^(.*?)(\d+)$/;

/**
 * The name a copy of the section called `label` gets, in a song whose
 * sections are called `labels`.
 *
 * **A numbered name counts on; any other name is kept.** "Verse 1" copies to
 * "Verse 2" - or past the highest number any section of that name already has,
 * so copying Verse 1 when Verse 2 exists gives "Verse 3", never a second
 * "Verse 2". "Chorus" copies to "Chorus": a repeated chorus is the same
 * chorus, and that is what a chord chart calls it. The number is the user's
 * own, read off the name rather than inferred from the kind, so a section
 * called "Take 5" counts on too and nothing is numbered that the user did not
 * number. The comparison ignores case and the spaces around the name.
 */
export function copyLabelOf(label: string, labels: readonly string[]): string {
  const numbered = NUMBERED.exec(label.trim());
  if (numbered === null) return label;

  const [, stem, digits] = numbered;
  const same = stem.trim().toLowerCase();
  let highest = Number(digits);
  for (const other of labels) {
    const match = NUMBERED.exec(other.trim());
    if (match !== null && match[1].trim().toLowerCase() === same) highest = Math.max(highest, Number(match[2]));
  }
  return `${stem}${highest + 1}`;
}

/** `node` with a fresh id on it and on every node inside that carries one. */
function withFreshIds(node: Node): Node {
  if (node.isText) return node;
  const attrs = 'id' in node.attrs ? { ...node.attrs, id: crypto.randomUUID() } : node.attrs;
  const content: Node[] = [];
  node.forEach(child => content.push(withFreshIds(child)));
  return node.type.create(attrs, content, node.marks);
}

/**
 * Copies the section `id` to right after itself, and puts the caret at the
 * start of the copy.
 *
 * - **The copy is its own** (design decision 8): a fresh id for the section
 *   and for every chord and tab block in it, made here rather than left to the
 *   id plugin, so the edit is whole on its own and the original keeps every id
 *   the hand-off or an open link knows it by.
 * - **Its name** is `copyLabelOf`'s: "Verse 1" → "Verse 2", "Chorus" stays.
 * - **A voice memo is left out.** Its recording lives outside the document,
 *   keyed by the memo's id (design Part 1), so a copied memo would either share
 *   the original's id - which the song refuses - or name a recording that does
 *   not exist. The take belongs to the section it was recorded on. A copy left
 *   with nothing else gets an empty line, since a section is never empty.
 */
export function duplicateSection(id: string): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const sections = sectionsOf(state.doc);
    const section = sections.find(entry => entry.id === id);
    if (section === undefined) return refused(GONE_SECTION);

    const content: Node[] = [];
    section.node.forEach(child => {
      if (child.type !== songSchema.nodes.memo) content.push(withFreshIds(child));
    });
    if (content.length === 0) content.push(songSchema.nodes.lyricLine.create());
    const label = copyLabelOf(section.label, sections.map(entry => entry.label));
    const copy = songSchema.nodes.section.create({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), label, kind: section.kind }, content);

    const at = section.pos + section.node.nodeSize;
    const tr = state.tr.insert(at, copy);
    tr.setSelection(Selection.near(tr.doc.resolve(at + 1)));
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

/** Deletes the section `id` and everything in it. A song keeps at least one section. */
export function deleteSection(id: string): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const section = sectionWithId(state.doc, id);
    if (section === null) return refused(GONE_SECTION);
    if (state.doc.childCount === 1) return refused(ONLY_SECTION);
    return edited(state.tr.delete(section.pos, section.pos + section.node.nodeSize));
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The song
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Puts the song in a new key, and every chord in it, in one transaction - one
 * undo step for the key and all its chords.
 *
 * It means what `ProgressionService.setKey` means, by the same parts:
 *
 * - the tonic is wrapped into 0-11 (`normalizeProgressionKey`), and a tonic
 *   that is not a whole number is refused rather than thrown;
 * - `preferSharps` is the argument when given - the page knows whether the
 *   user picked F♯ or G♭, which a pitch class cannot say - and otherwise
 *   `spellingFor`: the key's signature, then the scale's own preference, then
 *   the spelling already in force;
 * - every chord atom goes through `rekeyedSlot` with the scale being left and
 *   the one being entered and `keyTransposeInterval` between the tonics, so a
 *   chord that leaves its pitches to the key keeps its degree and is voiced in
 *   the new key, and one whose pitches are owned keeps them - moved with the
 *   tonic - and is written as whatever numeral they make there.
 *
 * **One difference: a scale that cannot build chords is refused.** The
 * progression page applies such a key anyway, because its key comes from the
 * circle of fifths and refusing would leave it in a different key from the
 * fretboard behind it. The song owns its key - the circle is hidden on the
 * song pages - so that reason does not apply, and the opposite one does: every
 * chord on a song sheet is a degree, and in a pentatonic key no degree can be
 * written, so the sheet could print no chord name and accept no new chord. The
 * page's scale menu offers only scales that can build chords (decision 4);
 * this is the same rule at the command, for any other caller. An id the app
 * does not know is refused on the same grounds.
 *
 * A key identical to the song's - tonic, scale and spelling - is unchanged.
 */
export function setSongKey(
  keys: SongKeyRules,
  tonic: number,
  scaleId: string,
  preferSharps?: boolean
): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    if (!Number.isInteger(tonic)) return refused(`A key's tonic is a pitch class, a whole number; got ${tonic}.`);
    const scale = keys.findScale(scaleId);
    if (scale === null) return refused(`The app has no scale called "${scaleId}".`);

    const leavingKey = songMetaOf(state.doc).key;
    const bounded = normalizeProgressionKey({ tonic, scaleId, preferSharps: leavingKey.preferSharps });
    const key: ProgressionKey = {
      ...bounded,
      preferSharps: preferSharps ?? keys.spellingFor(bounded.tonic, scaleId, scale, leavingKey.preferSharps)
    };

    const entering = keys.chordScaleFor(key);
    if (entering === null) {
      return refused(
        `${scale.name} can't build chords: a song's chords are stacked in thirds through a seven-note scale. ` +
          'Choose one of those for the song.'
      );
    }
    if (sameValue(key, leavingKey)) return UNCHANGED;

    const leaving = keys.chordScaleFor(leavingKey);
    const transposeBy = keyTransposeInterval(leavingKey.tonic, key.tonic);
    const tr = state.tr.setDocAttribute('key', key);
    // Attribute steps map no positions, so each chord's position from the
    // document before the change is still its position here.
    for (const chord of chordsIn(state.doc)) {
      const moved = rekeyedSlot(slotOf(chord.attrs), leaving, entering, key, transposeBy);
      writeChord(tr, chord.pos, atomAttrsOf(moved), chord.attrs);
    }
    return edited(tr);
  };
}

/**
 * Moves the song a semitone up (`1`) or down (`-1`): Transpose ↑↓. It is
 * `setSongKey` with the tonic stepped and the scale kept, and - as on the
 * progression page - the spelling worked out afresh for the new tonic rather
 * than carried, so C up a semitone is D♭ major, not C♯.
 */
export function transposeSong(keys: SongKeyRules, delta: -1 | 1): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const key = songMetaOf(state.doc).key;
    return setSongKey(keys, (key.tonic + delta + 12) % 12, key.scaleId)(state);
  };
}

/** Sets the song's tempo, in BPM. Refused outside the range the progression page plays. */
export function setTempo(bpm: number): SongEdit {
  return songAttributeEdit('tempo', bpm);
}

/**
 * Sets the song's time signature. **Chord lengths do not change.**
 *
 * A chord's length is in beats - quarter notes, as everywhere in the
 * progression model - not in bars, so it says how long the chord sounds and a
 * new meter does not change that: a four-beat chord in 4/4 is still four beats
 * in 3/4, now running a beat past the bar line. Scaling lengths to keep "one
 * bar" would silently rewrite the song's harmonic rhythm, and would not even
 * be undone by changing back - 4/4 to 3/4 turns 4 beats to 3, and 3/4 to 6/8
 * leaves them, so the round trip loses the fourth beat. What the meter does
 * decide is the length a chord gets when it is *placed* (`chordSlotOf`: one
 * bar), so chords added after the change are a bar of the new meter.
 */
export function setTimeSignature(timeSignature: TimeSignature): SongEdit {
  // Copied field by field, so what is stored and compared is exactly the
  // three fields, in the order the song's other time signatures have them.
  const { numerator, denominator, isCommon } = timeSignature;
  return songAttributeEdit('timeSignature', { numerator, denominator, isCommon });
}

/** Sets the song's title, as typed: a field being typed into is not trimmed under the caret. */
export function setTitle(title: string): SongEdit {
  return songAttributeEdit('title', title);
}

/** Sets the song's artist, as typed. */
export function setArtist(artist: string): SongEdit {
  return songAttributeEdit('artist', artist);
}
```

```ts
import { baseKeymap, splitBlock } from 'prosemirror-commands';
import { closeHistory, history, redo, undo } from 'prosemirror-history';
import { InputRule, inputRules, undoInputRule } from 'prosemirror-inputrules';
import { keymap } from 'prosemirror-keymap';
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { Command, EditorState, NodeSelection, Plugin, Selection, TextSelection, Transaction } from 'prosemirror-state';
import type { EditorView } from 'prosemirror-view';
import { SectionKind } from '../models/song.model';
import {
  characterWidthAt,
  commandOf,
  isSongCommand,
  markSongCommand,
  moveChordBy,
  selectedChordOf
} from './song-commands';
import { createSongIdsPlugin } from './song-document';
import { songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * The song sheet's editor plugins: what a key press, a typed character and
 * the undo history do in a song.
 *
 * `songEditorPlugins` is the whole list, in the order it must run, and the
 * sheet passes it to its `EditorState` unchanged. Pure but for the view the
 * key handlers are given by ProseMirror; nothing here touches Angular or the
 * DOM itself.
 *
 * ## The keys
 *
 * - **Mod-z** undoes; **Mod-y** and **Mod-Shift-z** redo, so both the Windows
 *   and the Mac habit work.
 * - **Enter** splits the lyric line at the caret, inside its section - never
 *   the section itself, which `baseKeymap`'s Enter does on an empty line in
 *   the middle of one (`liftEmptyBlock` splits the parent). With a chord
 *   selected, the line is split just after the chord and the chord is kept:
 *   Enter is not a way to delete a chord.
 * - **Shift-Enter** does exactly what Enter does. A song's line break *is* a
 *   new lyric line - the schema has no soft break inside one, because a line is
 *   the unit the syllable margin counts and a chord sheet prints - and Shift-
 *   Enter is the line break a hand reaches for from chat boxes and word
 *   processors. Making it do nothing, or something else, would punish the
 *   habit.
 * - **Backspace / Delete** are `baseKeymap`'s: they join two lines of one
 *   section. At a section's edge they stop, because sections are `isolating`
 *   in the schema - and they also *take* the key there, doing nothing, so the
 *   browser's own deletion cannot merge the two sections' DOM behind
 *   ProseMirror's back. A Backspace straight after the `[Chorus]` rule gives
 *   the typed heading back instead (`undoInputRule`).
 * - **ArrowLeft / ArrowRight** step over chord atoms as if they took no width,
 *   which on the sheet they do not: a chord's name sits above the letter it is
 *   anchored to. A press beside a chord moves past it *and* the letter beyond,
 *   so every press moves the caret a letter on screen; with nothing but chords
 *   left in the line it goes on to the next line. Left to themselves, the
 *   arrows would select the chord on one press and step off it on the next -
 *   two presses with the caret standing still - and a browser can stall at a
 *   non-editable span. The chord is selected by clicking its name instead.
 * - **Alt-ArrowLeft / Alt-ArrowRight** move a selected chord a letter
 *   (`moveChordBy`). With a chord selected the key is always taken - at an edge
 *   the refusal is reported through `onRefuse` - so a Mac's Alt+arrow word jump
 *   cannot fire instead and drop the selection. With no chord selected they are
 *   left to the browser.
 *
 * ## `[`: a chord on a line with words, a section heading on an empty line
 *
 * Two features want the bracket. Pressing `[` opens the chord field (task 7)
 * where a chord belongs; typing `[Chorus]` on an empty line makes a section.
 * The rule that lets both live is **which line the caret is in**:
 *
 * - on a lyric line with anything on it - words or chords - `[` asks for the
 *   chord field (`onChordFieldRequest`) and is not typed;
 * - on an empty lyric line `[` is typed as a bracket, so the heading rule can
 *   see `[Chorus]` when its `]` arrives.
 *
 * The cost is that `[` cannot open the chord field on an empty line; a chord
 * there comes from the Chords panel, or by typing a word first. That is the
 * smaller loss: an empty line is exactly where a heading goes, and a chord
 * with no word under it has nothing to be anchored to yet.
 *
 * It is a `handleTextInput` hook rather than a keymap entry because it is
 * about the *character*: on many keyboard layouts `[` is AltGr+8 or Option+5,
 * which a keymap would have to list layout by layout, while the text input
 * arrives as `[` whatever produced it.
 *
 * ## The `[Section]` rule
 *
 * `[Name]` typed on an otherwise empty lyric line - no words, no chords, nothing
 * after the caret - turns that line into the start of a new section called
 * `Name`. Intro, Verse, Pre-Chorus, Chorus, Bridge and Outro, in any case and
 * with an optional number ("Verse 2"), give their kind (`sectionHeadingOf`);
 * any other name is a section of kind `other`. The typed text goes; the line
 * stays, empty, with the caret in it, ready for the section's first words.
 *
 * "From that line on": the line and every line after it in its section become
 * the new section, and the lines before it stay where they were. On a section's
 * *first* line there are no lines before it, and splitting would leave an empty
 * section, so the section itself is renamed - it keeps its id, and a new song's
 * "Verse 1" typed over with `[Intro]` simply becomes the Intro.
 *
 * ## Undo
 *
 * Typing groups as ProseMirror's history always groups it: adjacent edits in
 * quick succession are one step. Every command is a step of its own, apart
 * from the typing on either side of it - `song-commands.ts` closes the step
 * before (`closeHistory`), and the last plugin here closes it after, by
 * appending an empty, closing transaction to any dispatch that carried a
 * command. The heading rule is a command by that measure, so Mod-z after it
 * undoes the section and leaves the typing (`[Chorus`, as the closing bracket
 * was never inserted). The id plugin's repairs join the step they repair.
 */

/** Where the caret is on screen, as the view measures it. */
export interface CaretCoords {
  left: number;
  top: number;
  bottom: number;
}

/** What the sheet is asked for when `[` opens the chord field. */
export interface ChordFieldRequest {
  /** Where the chord will go: the selection's start, as `insertChord` puts it. */
  pos: number;
  /** Where to open the field, or null when there is no view to measure (a spec). */
  coords: CaretCoords | null;
}

export interface SongEditorOptions {
  /** Called when `[` asks for the chord field; without it, `[` is typed. */
  onChordFieldRequest?: (request: ChordFieldRequest) => void;
  /** Told why a key's command was refused - an Alt+arrow at the edge of a line. */
  onRefuse?: (reason: string) => void;
}

/** A heading read from `[...]`: the section's kind and its name as typed. */
export interface SectionHeading {
  kind: SectionKind;
  label: string;
}

/** The six section words, and the kind each one names. */
const SECTION_WORDS: readonly { word: RegExp; kind: SectionKind }[] = [
  { word: /^intro$/i, kind: 'intro' },
  { word: /^verse$/i, kind: 'verse' },
  { word: /^pre[- ]?chorus$/i, kind: 'pre' },
  { word: /^chorus$/i, kind: 'chorus' },
  { word: /^bridge$/i, kind: 'bridge' },
  { word: /^outro$/i, kind: 'outro' }
];

/** A heading's name and its optional trailing number. */
const NUMBERED_HEADING = /^(.*?)\s*\d*$/;

/**
 * `[Name]` at the start of a line's text, ending at the bracket just typed.
 * The name holds no brackets and no `￼` - the stand-in the input-rule
 * plugin puts for a chord atom - so a line with a chord on it never matches.
 */
const HEADING_RULE = /^\[([^[\]￼]+)\]$/;

/**
 * The section a heading names: one of the six words, in any case, with an
 * optional number, gives its kind, and anything else is kind `other`. The
 * label is the text as typed, trimmed. Null for a heading with nothing in it.
 */
export function sectionHeadingOf(text: string): SectionHeading | null {
  const label = text.trim();
  if (label === '') return null;
  const word = NUMBERED_HEADING.exec(label)?.[1] ?? label;
  const known = SECTION_WORDS.find(entry => entry.word.test(word));
  return { kind: known?.kind ?? 'other', label };
}

function isLyricLine(node: Node): boolean {
  return node.type === songSchema.nodes.lyricLine;
}

function isChord(node: Node | null | undefined): boolean {
  return node?.type === songSchema.nodes.chord;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The chord field
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Asks for the chord field if `[` should open it here, and answers whether it
 * did: on a lyric line with anything on it (see the header). The position is
 * the selection's start, where `insertChord` will put the chord; the
 * coordinates are the view's measure of it, when there is a view.
 */
export function requestChordField(
  state: EditorState,
  view: Pick<EditorView, 'coordsAtPos'> | undefined,
  onRequest: (request: ChordFieldRequest) => void
): boolean {
  const $from = state.selection.$from;
  if (!isLyricLine($from.parent) || $from.parent.content.size === 0) return false;

  const pos = state.selection.from;
  const rect = view?.coordsAtPos(pos);
  onRequest({ pos, coords: rect === undefined ? null : { left: rect.left, top: rect.top, bottom: rect.bottom } });
  return true;
}

function chordFieldPlugin(options: SongEditorOptions): Plugin {
  return new Plugin({
    props: {
      handleTextInput: (view, _from, _to, text) => {
        const onRequest = options.onChordFieldRequest;
        return text === '[' && onRequest !== undefined && requestChordField(view.state, view, onRequest);
      }
    }
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The [Section] rule
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Turns the empty line holding `pos` into the start of a section (see the
 * header): split off with the lines after it, or - on a section's first line -
 * the section renamed in place.
 *
 * The split is not put to `canSplit` first, which refuses to split any
 * `isolating` node - a rule for the *user's* splits, which is what keeps Enter
 * inside a section. Here the split is the point, and it always fits: it falls
 * between two lines, so both halves keep a line.
 */
function startSection(tr: Transaction, pos: number, heading: SectionHeading): Transaction {
  const $line = tr.doc.resolve(pos);
  const sectionPos = $line.before(1);
  if ($line.index(1) === 0) {
    tr.setNodeAttribute(sectionPos, 'label', heading.label);
    return tr.setNodeAttribute(sectionPos, 'kind', heading.kind);
  }

  const linePos = $line.before(2);
  tr.split(linePos, 1, [{ type: songSchema.nodes.section, attrs: { id: crypto.randomUUID(), ...heading } }]);
  // Past the old section's end and the new one's start, into the line.
  return tr.setSelection(TextSelection.create(tr.doc, linePos + 3));
}

const sectionHeadingRule = new InputRule(HEADING_RULE, (state, match, start, end) => {
  const $start = state.doc.resolve(start);
  const line = $start.parent;
  // Otherwise empty: the heading is the line's whole text - nothing before it,
  // nothing after the caret, no chord anywhere in it.
  if (!isLyricLine(line) || $start.parentOffset !== 0 || end !== $start.end()) return null;
  if (line.textContent.length !== line.content.size) return null;

  const heading = sectionHeadingOf(match[1]);
  if (heading === null) return null;
  return markSongCommand(startSection(state.tr.delete(start, end), start, heading));
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Keys
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Enter: split the lyric line; past a selected chord, keeping it. See the header. */
export const splitLine: Command = (state, dispatch) => {
  const selection = state.selection;
  if (!isLyricLine(selection.$from.parent)) return false;
  if (!(selection instanceof NodeSelection)) return splitBlock(state, dispatch);

  if (dispatch !== undefined) {
    const tr = state.tr.split(selection.to);
    dispatch(tr.setSelection(TextSelection.create(tr.doc, tr.mapping.map(selection.to))).scrollIntoView());
  }
  return true;
};

/**
 * ArrowLeft (`-1`) or ArrowRight (`1`) beside a chord: past every chord there
 * and the letter beyond, or on to the next line when only chords are left (see
 * the header). False - the browser's own move - when no chord is beside the
 * caret, or there is a selection to collapse.
 */
export function stepPastChord(dir: -1 | 1): Command {
  return (state, dispatch) => {
    const selection = state.selection;
    if (!(selection instanceof TextSelection) || !selection.empty) return false;
    const doc = state.doc;
    const beside = (pos: number): Node | null =>
      dir > 0 ? doc.resolve(pos).nodeAfter : doc.resolve(pos).nodeBefore;

    let at = selection.head;
    if (!isLyricLine(selection.$head.parent) || !isChord(beside(at))) return false;
    while (isChord(beside(at))) at += dir;

    const $at = doc.resolve(at);
    let next: Selection;
    if (beside(at) !== null) {
      next = TextSelection.create(doc, at + dir * characterWidthAt($at, dir));
    } else {
      const edge = doc.resolve(dir > 0 ? $at.after() : $at.before());
      next = Selection.findFrom(edge, dir, true) ?? TextSelection.create(doc, at);
    }
    dispatch?.(state.tr.setSelection(next).scrollIntoView());
    return true;
  };
}

/** Alt+arrow: move the selected chord a letter. Taken whenever a chord is selected. */
function moveSelectedChord(delta: -1 | 1, onRefuse: ((reason: string) => void) | undefined): Command {
  return (state, dispatch) => {
    const chord = selectedChordOf(state);
    if (chord === null) return false;
    commandOf(moveChordBy(chord.attrs.id, delta), onRefuse)(state, dispatch);
    return true;
  };
}

/**
 * Whether the caret is at the start (`-1`) or end (`1`) of its section's text,
 * where Backspace or Delete would cross into the next section. Answering true
 * takes the key and does nothing: see the header.
 */
function holdsAtSectionEdge(dir: -1 | 1): Command {
  return state => {
    const selection = state.selection;
    if (!(selection instanceof TextSelection) || !selection.empty) return false;
    const $head = selection.$head;
    if ($head.depth < 2) return false;
    return dir < 0
      ? $head.parentOffset === 0 && $head.index(1) === 0
      : $head.parentOffset === $head.parent.content.size && $head.indexAfter(1) === $head.node(1).childCount;
  };
}

function songKeymap(options: SongEditorOptions): Record<string, Command> {
  return {
    'Mod-z': undo,
    'Mod-y': redo,
    'Mod-Shift-z': redo,
    Enter: splitLine,
    'Shift-Enter': splitLine,
    Backspace: undoInputRule,
    ArrowLeft: stepPastChord(-1),
    ArrowRight: stepPastChord(1),
    'Alt-ArrowLeft': moveSelectedChord(-1, options.onRefuse),
    'Alt-ArrowRight': moveSelectedChord(1, options.onRefuse)
  };
}

/** After `baseKeymap`: the deletions it binds, held at a section's edge. */
const SECTION_EDGE_KEYMAP: Record<string, Command> = {
  Backspace: holdsAtSectionEdge(-1),
  'Mod-Backspace': holdsAtSectionEdge(-1),
  'Shift-Backspace': holdsAtSectionEdge(-1),
  Delete: holdsAtSectionEdge(1),
  'Mod-Delete': holdsAtSectionEdge(1)
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The list
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Closes the undo step after any dispatch that carried a command, so the
 * typing that follows starts a step of its own (see the header). An empty
 * transaction carrying `closeHistory` changes nothing but the history's
 * grouping.
 */
function commandStepPlugin(): Plugin {
  return new Plugin({
    appendTransaction: (transactions, _before, state) =>
      transactions.some(isSongCommand) ? closeHistory(state.tr) : null
  });
}

/**
 * Every plugin the song sheet's editor runs, in order.
 *
 * The order matters in two places. Key handlers run in list order, so the
 * song's keymap comes before `baseKeymap` - its Enter and arrows win - and the
 * section-edge hold after it, so it only answers what `baseKeymap` declined.
 * And appended transactions run in list order too: the id plugin must repair a
 * command's ids *before* the step is closed behind it, or the repair would be
 * an undo step of its own, so `commandStepPlugin` is last.
 */
export function songEditorPlugins(options: SongEditorOptions = {}): Plugin[] {
  return [
    chordFieldPlugin(options),
    inputRules({ rules: [sectionHeadingRule] }),
    keymap(songKeymap(options)),
    keymap(baseKeymap),
    keymap(SECTION_EDGE_KEYMAP),
    history(),
    createSongIdsPlugin(),
    commandStepPlugin()
  ];
}
```

## Phase C: Keeping songs

The song library, and autosave.

### Task C.1: The song library, and autosave

`SongLibraryService` mirrors the composer's library: one `songs` store behind the `SONG_LIBRARY_DB`
token, summaries read by cursor and published only while something shows them, writes that settle on commit. A load
returns the checked document or the reason it is unreadable, never a half-read song; a save is compare-and-swap on the
revision; a duplicate renews every id, since a section's id is its progression's id.

`SongAutosave` is the "persist the latest document" seam of Part 8: debounced, never overlapping, the latest content
only, with a status the page shows and a flush for leaving.

**Files** (under `client/src/app/` unless given in full):
- Create: `services/song-autosave.spec.ts`, `services/song-autosave.ts`, `services/song-library.service.spec.ts`, `services/song-library.service.ts`
- Modify: `services/song-document.ts`

**Step 1: The failing specs.**

`client/src/app/services/song-autosave.spec.ts`, new:

<!-- apply: create client/src/app/services/song-autosave.spec.ts -->
```ts
import {
  AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS,
  AUTOSAVE_MAX_WAIT_MS,
  AutosaveClock,
  SaveStatus,
  SongAutosave
} from './song-autosave';

/**
 * Autosave against a fake clock and a fake store.
 *
 * The clock runs a timer only when a spec moves time on (`tick`), and the store
 * settles a save only when a spec says so (`succeed`, `failWith`), so every
 * spec decides exactly what has happened by each expectation: nothing here
 * waits on real time.
 */
class FakeClock implements AutosaveClock {
  time = 10_000;
  private timers: { handle: number; at: number; callback: () => void }[] = [];
  private nextHandle = 1;

  now(): number {
    return this.time;
  }

  setTimeout(callback: () => void, ms: number): unknown {
    const handle = this.nextHandle++;
    this.timers.push({ handle, at: this.time + ms, callback });
    return handle;
  }

  clearTimeout(handle: unknown): void {
    this.timers = this.timers.filter(timer => timer.handle !== handle);
  }

  /** Moves time on by `ms`, running each timer that falls due at its own moment, and lets what it starts settle. */
  async tick(ms: number): Promise<void> {
    const until = this.time + ms;
    for (;;) {
      const due = this.timers.filter(timer => timer.at <= until).sort((a, b) => a.at - b.at)[0];
      if (due === undefined) break;
      this.timers = this.timers.filter(timer => timer !== due);
      this.time = due.at;
      due.callback();
      await settled();
    }
    this.time = until;
    await settled();
  }
}

/** A store whose saves stay in flight until a spec settles them, oldest first. */
class FakeStore {
  /** What each save was asked to write, in order, whatever became of it. */
  readonly asked: string[] = [];
  /** What the saves that succeeded wrote, in order. */
  readonly written: string[] = [];
  private inFlight: { content: string; resolve: () => void; reject: (error: unknown) => void }[] = [];

  readonly persist = (content: string): Promise<void> => {
    this.asked.push(content);
    return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => this.inFlight.push({ content, resolve, reject }));
  };

  get pending(): number {
    return this.inFlight.length;
  }

  async succeed(): Promise<void> {
    const save = this.next();
    this.written.push(save.content);
    save.resolve();
    await settled();
  }

  async failWith(error: unknown): Promise<void> {
    this.next().reject(error);
    await settled();
  }

  private next() {
    const save = this.inFlight.shift();
    if (save === undefined) throw new Error('No save is in flight');
    return save;
  }
}

/** Lets every promise reaction already queued run. */
function settled(): Promise<void> {
  return new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
}

describe('SongAutosave', () => {
  const SAVED_AT = 5_000;
  let clock: FakeClock;
  let store: FakeStore;
  let autosave: SongAutosave<string>;
  let statuses: SaveStatus[];

  beforeEach(() => {
    clock = new FakeClock();
    store = new FakeStore();
    autosave = new SongAutosave<string>({ persist: store.persist, savedAt: SAVED_AT, clock });
    statuses = [];
    autosave.status$.subscribe(status => statuses.push(status));
  });

  it('starts saved, as of when the song was last written', () => {
    expect(statuses).toEqual([{ kind: 'saved', at: SAVED_AT }]);
    expect(autosave.hasUnsavedChanges()).toBeFalse();
  });

  describe('debounce', () => {
    it('saves a moment after the last change, not after each one', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(500);
      autosave.change('ab');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS - 1);

      expect(store.asked).toEqual([]);

      await clock.tick(1);

      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['ab']);
    });

    it('saves at the latest a few seconds after the first unsaved change, though the changes never pause', async () => {
      for (let elapsed = 0; elapsed < AUTOSAVE_MAX_WAIT_MS; elapsed += 400) {
        autosave.change(`at ${elapsed}`);
        await clock.tick(400);
      }

      expect(store.asked.length).toBe(1);
      expect(clock.time - 10_000).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(AUTOSAVE_MAX_WAIT_MS);
      expect(store.asked[0]).toBe('at 4800');
    });

    it('honours a delay it is given', async () => {
      const quick = new SongAutosave<string>({ persist: store.persist, savedAt: SAVED_AT, clock, delayMs: 100 });

      quick.change('a');
      await clock.tick(100);

      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a']);
    });
  });

  describe('status', () => {
    it('goes unsaved on a change, saving when the write starts, and saved - at when it landed - when it lands', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      autosave.change('ab');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      clock.time += 30;
      await store.succeed();

      expect(statuses).toEqual([
        { kind: 'saved', at: SAVED_AT },
        { kind: 'unsaved' },
        { kind: 'saving' },
        { kind: 'saved', at: 10_000 + AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS + 30 }
      ]);
    });

    it('says the song has unsaved changes from the change until the save of the latest lands', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      expect(autosave.hasUnsavedChanges()).toBeTrue();

      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      expect(autosave.hasUnsavedChanges()).toBeTrue();

      await store.succeed();
      expect(autosave.hasUnsavedChanges()).toBeFalse();
    });
  });

  describe('one save at a time', () => {
    it('never starts a save while another is in flight, and saves a change made meanwhile once it lands', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      autosave.change('ab');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS * 10);

      expect(store.pending).toBe(1);
      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a']);

      await store.succeed();

      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a', 'ab']);
      expect(statuses.slice(-2)).toEqual([{ kind: 'unsaved' }, { kind: 'saving' }]);
    });

    it('waits out the rest of the delay for a change made just before the save in flight lands', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      autosave.change('ab');
      await clock.tick(300);
      await store.succeed();

      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a']);

      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS - 300);

      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a', 'ab']);
    });

    it('writes only the latest of the changes made while a save was in flight', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      autosave.change('ab');
      autosave.change('abc');
      autosave.change('abcd');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      await store.succeed();
      await store.succeed();

      expect(store.written).toEqual(['a', 'abcd']);
      expect(statuses[statuses.length - 1].kind).toBe('saved');
    });
  });

  describe('flush', () => {
    it('saves a pending change now, without waiting out the delay, and resolves with the status it ends in', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');

      const flushed = autosave.flush();
      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a']);
      await store.succeed();

      expect(await flushed).toEqual({ kind: 'saved', at: clock.time });
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS * 2);
      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a']);
    });

    it('writes nothing when nothing is pending', async () => {
      expect(await autosave.flush()).toEqual({ kind: 'saved', at: SAVED_AT });
      expect(store.asked).toEqual([]);
    });

    it('waits for the save in flight, then saves what came after it', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      autosave.change('ab');

      let done = false;
      const flushed = autosave.flush().then(status => {
        done = true;
        return status;
      });
      await settled();
      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a']);

      await store.succeed();
      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a', 'ab']);
      expect(done).toBeFalse();

      await store.succeed();
      expect((await flushed).kind).toBe('saved');
    });

    it('resolves with the failure when its save fails, rather than rejecting', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');

      const flushed = autosave.flush();
      await store.failWith(new Error('The disk is full'));

      expect(await flushed).toEqual({ kind: 'failed', reason: 'The disk is full' });
    });
  });

  describe('failure', () => {
    it('keeps a failed change pending, says why, and does not retry on its own', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      await store.failWith(new Error('The disk is full'));

      expect(statuses[statuses.length - 1]).toEqual({ kind: 'failed', reason: 'The disk is full' });
      expect(autosave.hasUnsavedChanges()).toBeTrue();

      await clock.tick(60_000);

      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a']);
    });

    it('tries again on the next change, writing the latest, and recovers', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      await store.failWith(new Error('The disk is full'));

      autosave.change('ab');
      // The failure stays shown until the next attempt starts: the change is still not saved, and for that reason.
      expect(statuses[statuses.length - 1].kind).toBe('failed');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      await store.succeed();

      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a', 'ab']);
      expect(statuses.slice(-3)).toEqual([
        { kind: 'failed', reason: 'The disk is full' },
        { kind: 'saving' },
        { kind: 'saved', at: clock.time }
      ]);
      expect(autosave.hasUnsavedChanges()).toBeFalse();
    });

    it('tries the failed change again on a flush', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      await store.failWith(new Error('The disk is full'));

      const flushed = autosave.flush();
      await store.succeed();

      expect(store.written).toEqual(['a']);
      expect((await flushed).kind).toBe('saved');
    });

    it('still saves a change made while the failing save was in flight, a moment after it was made', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      autosave.change('ab');
      await store.failWith(new Error('The disk is full'));
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      await store.succeed();

      expect(store.written).toEqual(['ab']);
    });

    it('gives a reason for a failure that is not an Error', async () => {
      autosave.change('a');
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS);
      await store.failWith('quota');

      expect(statuses[statuses.length - 1]).toEqual({ kind: 'failed', reason: 'quota' });
    });
  });

  describe('destroy', () => {
    it('saves what is pending, completes its status, and ignores changes after it', async () => {
      let completed = false;
      autosave.status$.subscribe({ complete: () => (completed = true) });
      autosave.change('a');

      const destroyed = autosave.destroy();
      autosave.change('after');
      await store.succeed();

      expect((await destroyed).kind).toBe('saved');
      expect(completed).toBeTrue();
      await clock.tick(AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS * 2);
      expect(store.asked).toEqual(['a']);
    });
  });
});
```
