```ts
import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { firstValueFrom } from 'rxjs';
import { ProgressionKey, createDegreeSlot } from '../models/progression.model';
import { SongDoc, SongSummary } from '../models/song.model';
import { abortOnSuccess, deletedDatabase } from './indexed-db.spec-helper';
import { regenerateSlot } from './progression-edit';
import { atomAttrsOf, createSongContent } from './song-document';
import { SONG_LIBRARY_DB, SongLibraryService } from './song-library.service';
import { songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * The library of songs, against real IndexedDB under Karma.
 *
 * Each spec opens a database of its own through `SONG_LIBRARY_DB` and deletes it
 * after with `deletedDatabase`, which fails the spec if the service left a
 * connection open: the service must let its database go when asked.
 */
describe('SongLibraryService', () => {
  let dbName: string;
  let library: SongLibraryService;

  const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
  const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];

  /** Two sections holding two chords, a tab block and a memo: one of every node that carries an id. */
  function fullSong(title: string): Node {
    const chord = (degree: number): Node =>
      songSchema.node('chord', atomAttrsOf(regenerateSlot(createDegreeSlot(degree, 0), C_MAJOR, IONIAN)));
    return songSchema.node('doc', { ...createSongContent().attrs, title, artist: 'The Band' }, [
      songSchema.node('section', { id: 'sec-1', label: 'Verse 1', kind: 'verse' }, [
        songSchema.node('lyricLine', null, [chord(0), songSchema.text('Wondering '), chord(4), songSchema.text('where')])
      ]),
      songSchema.node('section', { id: 'sec-2', label: 'Chorus', kind: 'chorus' }, [
        songSchema.node('tabBlock', {
          id: 'tab-1',
          name: 'Riff',
          score: { title: '', subTitle: '', artist: '', album: '', tempo: 100, masterBars: [], tracks: [] }
        }),
        songSchema.node('memo', { id: 'memo-1', name: 'Hum', durationSec: 12.5 })
      ])
    ]);
  }

  /** Every id in `content`, in document order. */
  function idsIn(content: SongDoc['content']): string[] {
    const ids: string[] = [];
    Node.fromJSON(songSchema, content).descendants(node => {
      if (typeof node.attrs['id'] === 'string') ids.push(node.attrs['id']);
    });
    return ids;
  }

  /** `content` with every id blanked, so two songs can be compared for everything but their ids. */
  function withoutIds(content: SongDoc['content']): unknown {
    return JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(content), (key, value) => (key === 'id' ? '' : value));
  }

  /**
   * Writes `record` straight into the store, past the service: how a corrupt record gets there. The service lists the
   * library first, so the database and its store exist before this opens it.
   */
  async function putRaw(record: unknown): Promise<void> {
    await library.refresh();
    return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      const request = indexedDB.open(dbName, 1);
      request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      request.onsuccess = () => {
        const db = request.result;
        const transaction = db.transaction('songs', 'readwrite');
        transaction.objectStore('songs').put(record);
        transaction.oncomplete = () => {
          db.close();
          resolve();
        };
        transaction.onabort = () => {
          db.close();
          reject(transaction.error);
        };
      };
    });
  }

  /** Waits until the clock has moved on, so two writes get different `updatedAt`s. */
  async function nextMillisecond(): Promise<void> {
    const start = Date.now();
    while (Date.now() === start) await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1));
  }

  beforeEach(() => {
    dbName = `song-library-spec-${crypto.randomUUID()}`;
    TestBed.configureTestingModule({ providers: [{ provide: SONG_LIBRARY_DB, useValue: dbName }] });
    library = TestBed.inject(SongLibraryService);
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    await deletedDatabase(dbName);
  });

  describe('createSong', () => {
    it('stores a new song at revision 1 with the default facts and one empty verse, and returns it', async () => {
      const song = await library.createSong();

      expect(song.revision).toBe(1);
      expect(song.createdAt).toBe(song.updatedAt);
      const loaded = await library.loadSong(song.id);
      expect(loaded?.kind).toBe('song');
      if (loaded?.kind !== 'song') return;
      expect(loaded.doc).toEqual(song);
      expect(loaded.node.attrs['title']).toBe('');
      expect(loaded.node.childCount).toBe(1);
      expect(loaded.node.child(0).attrs['label']).toBe('Verse 1');
    });

    it('starts the song with the facts it is given', async () => {
      const song = await library.createSong({ title: 'Last Dance', tempo: 84 });

      const summary = (await library.refresh()).find(entry => entry.id === song.id);
      expect(summary?.title).toBe('Last Dance');
      expect(song.content['attrs']).toEqual(jasmine.objectContaining({ title: 'Last Dance', tempo: 84 }));
    });

    it('gives each song an id of its own', async () => {
      const first = await library.createSong();
      const second = await library.createSong();

      expect(first.id).not.toBe(second.id);
    });

    it('refuses a create whose transaction aborts after its write succeeded, and keeps nothing', async () => {
      abortOnSuccess('add');

      const failure = library.createSong({ title: 'Lost' });

      await expectAsync(failure).toBeRejectedWithError(/song/i);
      expect(await library.refresh()).toEqual([]);
    });
  });

  describe('loadSong', () => {
    it('gives null for an id that is not in the library', async () => {
      expect(await library.loadSong('nobody')).toBeNull();
    });

    it('reads back the song as stored, as a record and as a checked document', async () => {
      const created = await library.createSong();
      const content = fullSong('Last Dance');
      const saved = await library.saveSong({ ...created, content: content.toJSON() });

      const loaded = await library.loadSong(created.id);

    it('refuses a record whose content is not a song, with the reason, rather than throwing', async () => {

      const loaded = await library.loadSong(created.id);

      expect(loaded?.kind).toBe('unreadable');
      if (loaded?.kind !== 'unreadable') return;
      expect(loaded.reason).toMatch(/nonsense/);
    });

    it('refuses a record that is not even a song record, with the reason', async () => {
      await putRaw({ id: 'odd', revision: 'seven', content: null });

      const loaded = await library.loadSong('odd');

      expect(loaded?.kind).toBe('unreadable');
      if (loaded?.kind !== 'unreadable') return;
      expect(loaded.reason).toMatch(/revision/);

  describe('saveSong', () => {
    it('writes the content, bumps the revision and the time it was updated, and keeps when it was made', async () => {
      const created = await library.createSong();
      await nextMillisecond();

      const saved = await library.saveSong({ ...created, content: fullSong('Second').toJSON() });

      expect(saved.revision).toBe(2);
      expect(saved.createdAt).toBe(created.createdAt);
      expect(saved.updatedAt).toBeGreaterThan(created.updatedAt);

    it('does not read the list after a write while nothing watches it, and reads it afresh when asked', async () => {
      const listed = spyOn(library, 'refresh').and.callThrough();

      const song = await library.createSong({ title: 'Unwatched' });
      await library.saveSong({ ...song, content: fullSong('Edited unwatched').toJSON() });
      await library.duplicateSong(song.id);
      await library.deleteSong(song.id);

      expect(listed).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
      expect((await library.refresh()).map(summary => summary.title)).toEqual(['Edited unwatched (copy)']);
    });

    it('summarises each song from its content - key, section count - and holds no content', async () => {
      const song = await library.saveSong({ ...(await library.createSong()), content: fullSong('Last Dance').toJSON() });

      await library.refresh();
      const [summary] = await firstValueFrom(library.getSummaries());

      expect(summary).toEqual({
        id: song.id,
        title: 'Last Dance',
        artist: 'The Band',
        key: C_MAJOR,
        sectionCount: 2,
        updatedAt: song.updatedAt,
        unreadable: null
      });
      expect(Object.keys(summary)).not.toContain('content');
    });

    it('lists a corrupt record as unreadable, with the reason and the title it still has, rather than dropping it', async () => {
      await library.createSong({ title: 'Fine' });
      await putRaw({ id: 'broken', revision: 1, createdAt: 1, updatedAt: 1, content: { type: 'doc', attrs: { title: 'Broken' } } });
      await putRaw({ id: 'odd', content: 'not a song' });

      const summaries = await library.refresh();

      expect(summaries.map(summary => [summary.title, summary.unreadable === null])).toEqual([
        ['Fine', true],
        ['Broken', false],
        ['', false]
      ]);
      expect(summaries[1].key).toBeNull();
      expect(summaries[2].id).toBe('odd');
      expect(summaries[2].unreadable).toMatch(/revision/);
    });
  });

  describe('its database', () => {
    it('lets its database go when it is deleted, and opens it afresh on the next call', async () => {
      await library.createSong({ title: 'Gone' });

      await deletedDatabase(dbName);

      await library.createSong({ title: 'New' });
      expect((await library.refresh()).map(summary => summary.title)).toEqual(['New']);
    });

    it('opens again after an open that failed, rather than failing for good', async () => {
      // A database already at a later version refuses the service's open (VersionError).
      await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
        const request = indexedDB.open(dbName, 99);
        request.onsuccess = () => {
          request.result.close();
          resolve();
        };
        request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      });

      await expectAsync(library.refresh()).toBeRejectedWithError(/song library could not be opened/);
      await deletedDatabase(dbName);

      expect(await library.refresh()).toEqual([]);
    });
  });
});
```

```ts
import { BehaviorSubject, Observable } from 'rxjs';
import { messageOf } from './error-message';

/**
 * Where a song's saving stands, for the title bar (design decision 9): "Saved · just now", "Saving…", "Unsaved", or
 * "Not saved: <reason>".
 *
 * - `saved`: everything changed has been written; `at` is when the last write landed (epoch ms), or when the song was
 *   last written before it was opened.
 * - `saving`: a write is in flight.
 * - `unsaved`: there is a change no write has started on yet - waiting out the delay.
 * - `failed`: the last write was refused or failed, and `reason` says why. The change it carried is still pending.
 */
export type SaveStatus =
  | { kind: 'saved'; at: number }
  | { kind: 'saving' }
  | { kind: 'unsaved' }
  | { kind: 'failed'; reason: string };

/** Time, as autosave needs it: injected so specs move it by hand. */
export interface AutosaveClock {
  now(): number;
  setTimeout(callback: () => void, ms: number): unknown;
  clearTimeout(handle: unknown): void;
}

/**
 * How long after the last change a save starts.
 *
 * Long enough that a run of typing - keys land 100 to 300 ms apart - is one write, not one a keystroke: each write
 * bumps the song's revision and re-reads the library list, and a status flickering "Saving…" under every letter is
 * noise. Short enough that the status catches up as soon as the writer pauses: under a second still reads as "just
 * now", and a tab closed in that second is caught by the page's flush on `pagehide`. The write itself costs a few
 * milliseconds for a song of a few hundred nodes, so it is the flicker, not the cost, that sets the floor.
 */
export const AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS = 800;

/**
 * The longest a change waits, however long the changes keep coming.
 *
 * A pure debounce never saves while someone types without an 800 ms pause - a fast typist pasting and editing for a
 * minute - and a crash then loses the whole minute. This bounds that loss to a few seconds of typing, while still
 * being rare enough that a writer in full flow sees "Saving…" only now and then.
 */
export const AUTOSAVE_MAX_WAIT_MS = 5000;

/** What an autosave is built with. */
export interface SongAutosaveOptions<T> {
  /**
   * Writes `content`, resolving once it is kept and rejecting with why not. Never called while an earlier call is in
   * flight, so a persist that carries the song's revision forward from one save to the next (`saveSong`) sees its own
   * last result.
   */
  persist: (content: T) => Promise<unknown>;
  /** When the song was last written (its record's `updatedAt`): the starting "Saved · …". */
  savedAt: number;
  clock?: AutosaveClock;
  delayMs?: number;
  maxWaitMs?: number;
}

/** The browser's own timers and clock. */
const BROWSER_CLOCK: AutosaveClock = {
  now: () => Date.now(),
  setTimeout: (callback, ms) => setTimeout(callback, ms),
  clearTimeout: handle => clearTimeout(handle as ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>)
};

/**
 * Saves the latest version of a song a moment after it changes, one write at a time, and says how that is going.
 *
 * Design Part 8's "persist the latest document" seam, from the page's side: the page hands every new document to
 * `change`, and this decides when `persist` writes one. Nothing here knows what a song is - `T` is whatever `persist`
 * takes - so a sync provider can replace `persist` later and keep this.
 *
 * A plain class, not an injectable: it is made per song, when the page has loaded one, and is bound to that song's
 * `persist` and last save time, which do not exist before then. The page makes one per opened song and destroys it
 * with the page.
 *
 * **The rules:**
 * - **Debounced** (`AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS` after the last change), **bounded** (`AUTOSAVE_MAX_WAIT_MS` after the first
 *   unsaved one).
 * - **Never two writes at once.** A change made while one is in flight waits for it, then for the rest of its own delay,
 *   counted from when it was made - so one that came long before the write landed goes at once.
 * - **Only the latest is written.** Changes replace one another while they wait; a write is always of the newest.
 * - **A failure keeps the change pending and does not retry on a timer.** The failures IndexedDB gives are not ones
 *   that pass by themselves - storage full, a song saved or deleted in another tab, a browser refusing storage - so a
 *   retry loop would repeat the same failure under a status that already says why. It retries on the next change, on
 *   `flush` (which the page's Retry, route leave and `pagehide` call), and on `destroy`. The failure stays shown while
 *   changes come in, until the next write starts: the work is still not saved, and for that reason.
 * - **`flush` saves now** and resolves once everything changed before it is saved or a save has failed, with the status
 *   it ends in. It never rejects: a failure is a status, not an exception.
 *
 * **What the page wires** (S1 task 6): `change` on every document change; `flush` on `visibilitychange` to hidden and on
 * `pagehide` (best effort - the browser may stop the page before an IndexedDB write commits); `hasUnsavedChanges` in
 * `beforeunload`, to ask before leaving with work pending; and `destroy` in `ngOnDestroy`.
 */
export class SongAutosave<T> {
  readonly status$: Observable<SaveStatus>;

  private readonly statusSubject: BehaviorSubject<SaveStatus>;
  private readonly persist: (content: T) => Promise<unknown>;
  private readonly clock: AutosaveClock;
  private readonly delayMs: number;
  private readonly maxWaitMs: number;

  /** The newest change no write has taken yet, boxed so a change of `undefined` is still a change. */
  private pending: { content: T } | null = null;
  /** When the pending change was made, and when the oldest change not yet saved was: the delay and its bound. */
  private lastChangeAt = 0;
  private firstUnsavedAt: number | null = null;
  /** The write in flight; it settles - never rejects - once the write has landed or failed. */
  private inFlight: Promise<void> | null = null;
  private timer: unknown = null;
  private destroyed = false;

  constructor(options: SongAutosaveOptions<T>) {
    this.persist = options.persist;
    this.clock = options.clock ?? BROWSER_CLOCK;
    this.delayMs = options.delayMs ?? AUTOSAVE_DELAY_MS;
    this.maxWaitMs = options.maxWaitMs ?? AUTOSAVE_MAX_WAIT_MS;
    this.statusSubject = new BehaviorSubject<SaveStatus>({ kind: 'saved', at: options.savedAt });
    this.status$ = this.statusSubject.asObservable();
  }

  /** The status now; `status$` emits each one. */
  get status(): SaveStatus {
    return this.statusSubject.getValue();
  }

  /** Whether some change is not yet saved: pending, in flight, or failed. */
  hasUnsavedChanges(): boolean {
    return this.pending !== null || this.inFlight !== null;
  }

  /** Takes `content` as the song's latest version, to be saved a moment from now. Ignored once destroyed. */
  change(content: T): void {
    if (this.destroyed) return;
    const now = this.clock.now();
    this.pending = { content };
    this.lastChangeAt = now;
    this.firstUnsavedAt ??= now;
    // "Saving…" stays while a write is in flight, and a failure stays shown until the next write starts.
    if (this.status.kind === 'saved') this.setStatus({ kind: 'unsaved' });
    this.schedule();
  }

  /**
   * Saves whatever is pending now, after the write in flight if there is one, and resolves with the status that ends
   * in: `saved` when everything changed before the call is written, `failed` when a write fails. One failed write ends
   * it - a flush tries once, it does not loop.
   */
  async flush(): Promise<SaveStatus> {
    this.cancelTimer();
    for (;;) {
      if (this.inFlight !== null) {
        await this.inFlight;
        // Landing, the write may have set a timer for what came after it; this flush takes that over.
        this.cancelTimer();
        continue;
      }
      if (this.pending === null) return this.status;
      await this.write();
      if (this.status.kind === 'failed') return this.status;
    }
  }

  /**
   * Flushes, then stops: no further change is taken and `status$` completes once the flush settles. For the page's
   * `ngOnDestroy`, which cannot wait for it - the write goes on after the page has gone, and lands.
   */
  async destroy(): Promise<SaveStatus> {
    this.destroyed = true;
    try {
      return await this.flush();
    } finally {
      this.cancelTimer();
      this.statusSubject.complete();
    }
  }

  /**
   * Sets the timer for the pending change: its delay from when it was made, cut short by the bound from the first
   * unsaved change. Due already - a change that waited out a write longer than its delay - it starts now.
   */
  private schedule(): void {
    this.cancelTimer();
    if (this.pending === null || this.inFlight !== null) return;

    const due = Math.min(this.lastChangeAt + this.delayMs, (this.firstUnsavedAt ?? this.lastChangeAt) + this.maxWaitMs);
    const wait = due - this.clock.now();
    if (wait <= 0) {
      void this.write();
      return;
    }
    this.timer = this.clock.setTimeout(() => {
      this.timer = null;
      // A write that started since - a flush - has the change, or will schedule it when it lands.
      if (this.inFlight === null) void this.write();
    }, wait);
  }

  /**
   * Writes the pending change, and settles once the write has landed or failed. Called only with no write in flight,
   * and synchronously up to `persist`, so two callers cannot both find none and start two.
   */
  private write(): Promise<void> {
    const pending = this.pending;
    if (pending === null) return Promise.resolve();
    this.cancelTimer();
    this.pending = null;
    this.firstUnsavedAt = null;
    this.setStatus({ kind: 'saving' });

    const started = this.clock.now();
    const writing = this.persistSafely(pending.content).then(
      () => {
        this.inFlight = null;
        if (this.pending === null) {
          this.setStatus({ kind: 'saved', at: this.clock.now() });
          return;
        }
        // Changed while the write was in flight: still not saved, and its save is due a moment after it was made.
        this.setStatus({ kind: 'unsaved' });
        this.schedule();
      },
      (error: unknown) => {
        this.inFlight = null;
        const newer = this.pending !== null;
        // A newer change replaces the failed one; otherwise the failed one waits, for the next change or a flush, and
        // has been unsaved since its write started - the bound on the next change's wait counts from then.
        if (!newer) {
          this.pending = pending;
          this.firstUnsavedAt = started;
        }
        this.setStatus({ kind: 'failed', reason: messageOf(error) });
        // A change made during the failed write is the next change it retries on.
        if (newer) this.schedule();
      }
    );
    this.inFlight = writing;
    return writing;
  }

  /** `persist(content)`, with a synchronous throw turned into a rejection, so it fails the same way as one that rejects. */
  private persistSafely(content: T): Promise<unknown> {
    try {
      return this.persist(content);
    } catch (error) {
      return Promise.reject(error);
    }
  }

  private cancelTimer(): void {
    if (this.timer === null) return;
    this.clock.clearTimeout(this.timer);
    this.timer = null;
  }

  /** Emits `next`, except a repeat of `saving` or `unsaved`, which would tell a subscriber nothing new. */
  private setStatus(next: SaveStatus): void {
    if ((next.kind === 'saving' || next.kind === 'unsaved') && next.kind === this.status.kind) return;
    this.statusSubject.next(next);
  }
}
```

```ts
import { Injectable, InjectionToken, NgZone, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { Transform } from 'prosemirror-transform';
import { BehaviorSubject, Observable } from 'rxjs';
import { SongDoc, SongMeta, SongSummary } from '../models/song.model';
import { messageOf } from './error-message';
import { committed } from './indexed-db';
import { UNTITLED_SONG, createSongContent, songNodeOf, songSummaryOf } from './song-document';

/**
 * The IndexedDB database songs are kept in: `song-library`. A token, as `GP_LIBRARY_DB` is, so each spec opens a
 * database of its own and deletes it after, rather than share - or wipe - the one a developer's browser holds.
 */
export const SONG_LIBRARY_DB = new InjectionToken<string>('SONG_LIBRARY_DB', {
  providedIn: 'root',
  factory: () => 'song-library'
});

/**
 * Version 1 holds the `songs` store alone. Memos arrive in S4 with a store of their own and a bump to 2, whose upgrade
 * adds it: creating it now would be a store nothing writes, whose shape S4 would be bound to before designing it.
 */
const DB_VERSION = 1;
const STORE_NAME = 'songs';

/**
 * What opening a song found.
 *
 * - **`song`**: the record, and its content as a document `songNodeOf` has checked - the editor's starting state, so
 *   the page never parses the content a second time, nor holds a record it has not checked.
 * - **`unreadable`**: the record is there but cannot be opened, and why. Not thrown: a corrupt song is a fact the page
 *   shows - "This song cannot be opened: <reason>" with the way back to the library, where its card offers Delete - not
 *   a failure of the library. Its record is not handed back, so nothing can edit, and then save over, a song it could
 *   not read.
 *
 * `null` - no such song - is outside the union, as `ComposerLibraryService.get` and `GpLibraryService.getEntry` give
 * it: not being there is not a property of a record, and the page answers it differently (back to the library, which
 * no longer lists it). A storage failure rejects, as every other call here does.
 */
export type SongLoad = { kind: 'song'; doc: SongDoc; node: Node } | { kind: 'unreadable'; reason: string };

/** What a save of a song another tab or window has saved since is refused with. */
const SAVED_ELSEWHERE =
  'This song was changed in another tab or window after it was opened here, so the changes here were not saved. ' +
  'Reload it to see that version.';

/**
 * Why a write or read failed when IndexedDB gives no reason: an abort with no failed request, which is the commit's
 * own failure (`committed`).
 */
const ABANDONED = 'The browser abandoned the change.';
const ABANDONED_READ = 'The browser abandoned the read.';

/** What a write to a song that is no longer stored is refused with. */
const NOT_IN_LIBRARY = 'This song is no longer in the library - it may have been deleted in another tab or window.';

/**
 * The library of songs: IndexedDB, the `/songs` list's source, and where the sheet loads from and autosaves to.
 *
 * Built as `ComposerLibraryService` and `GpLibraryService` are: one database promise (`database`), let go on a
 * `versionchange` so another tab's upgrade or a spec's delete is not held up, and every write settled on its commit
 * (`committed`), never on its request. Two differences, both deliberate:
 *
 * - **Records are checked on the way out.** `content` is a ProseMirror document as JSON, which a bug or a hand-edited
 *   import can leave unreadable, so nothing read here is trusted: `loadSong` and the list both go through `songNodeOf`,
 *   and a record that fails is reported, never thrown or dropped.
 * - **A save is compare-and-swap on `revision`** (`saveSong`), because a song can be open in two tabs and both
 *   autosave: the slower must not silently overwrite the faster.
 *
 * Every failure rejects with an `Error` whose message a page can show as it is.
 */
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class SongLibraryService {
  private readonly dbName: string = inject(SONG_LIBRARY_DB);
  private readonly ngZone = inject(NgZone);
  private readonly summariesSubject = new BehaviorSubject<SongSummary[]>([]);
  private readyPromise: Promise<IDBDatabase> | null = null;
  /** The newest list read started, so an older read finishing after it cannot replace its result (`refresh`). */
  private refreshes = 0;

  /**
   * Every song's card, newest first; read again after each write this service makes while anything subscribes
   * (`refreshAfterWrite`).
   *
   * Starts empty and is not read until something calls `refresh`, as the composer's library is not: the list page
   * calls it when it opens, so a song another tab wrote since is there and a list left stale while nobody watched it is
   * put right, and a page that only opens a song never reads the list at all.
   */
  getSummaries(): Observable<SongSummary[]> {
    return this.summariesSubject.asObservable();
  }

  /**
   * Reads every song's card, newest first by `updatedAt` (then by id, so equal times keep one order), publishes the
   * list and returns it.
   *
   * Read through a cursor, as `GpLibraryService` lists its files: each record is summarised as it is read and let go,
   * so the list never holds more than one song's content at once, and none once read. A card is derived from the
   * content (`songSummaryOf`) rather than stored beside it, so it cannot disagree with the sheet it opens - which is
   * why the content is read at all. A record that cannot be read is listed with its reason (`unreadable`), never
   * dropped, so the user can see it and delete it.
   */
  async refresh(): Promise<SongSummary[]> {
    const ticket = ++this.refreshes;
    const summaries: SongSummary[] = [];
    try {
      const transaction = (await this.database()).transaction(STORE_NAME, 'readonly');
      const cursor = transaction.objectStore(STORE_NAME).openCursor();
      cursor.onsuccess = () => {
        const at = cursor.result;
        if (!at) return;
        summaries.push(cardOf(at.value));
        at.continue();
      };
      await committed(transaction, ABANDONED_READ);
    } catch (error) {
      throw failure('The song library could not be read', error);
    }

    summaries.sort((a, b) => b.updatedAt - a.updatedAt || (a.id < b.id ? -1 : a.id > b.id ? 1 : 0));
    // Two reads can overlap - a save's and the list page's - and finish in either order; only the one started last
    // has seen every write before it. IndexedDB callbacks run outside Angular's zone.
    if (ticket === this.refreshes) this.ngZone.run(() => this.summariesSubject.next(summaries));
    return summaries;
  }

  /**
   * Makes a new song - the defaults of `createSongContent` under whatever `meta` says - stores it, and returns its
   * record at revision 1: it has been written once.
   */
  async createSong(meta: Partial<SongMeta> = {}): Promise<SongDoc> {
    const now = Date.now();
    const song: SongDoc = {
      id: crypto.randomUUID(),
      revision: 1,
      createdAt: now,
      updatedAt: now,
      content: createSongContent(meta).toJSON()
    };
    await this.write(song, 'The song could not be created');
    return song;
  }

  /** The song `id` as `SongLoad` says, or null when there is none. Never throws over what the record holds. */
  async loadSong(id: string): Promise<SongLoad | null> {
    const stored = await this.read(id);
    if (stored === undefined) return null;

    const record = songRecordOf(stored);
    if (typeof record === 'string') return { kind: 'unreadable', reason: record };
    const reading = songNodeOf(record.content);
    return reading.kind === 'song'
      ? { kind: 'song', doc: record, node: reading.doc }
      : { kind: 'unreadable', reason: reading.reason };
  }

  /**
   * Writes `song`'s content over the stored record and returns the record as written: its revision one more than
   * before, its `updatedAt` now, its `createdAt` the stored one. Hand the returned record to the next save.
   *
   * This is the "persist the latest document" seam (design Part 8): autosave calls it and nothing else, so a sync
   * provider can take its place later without the sheet knowing.
   *
   * **Refused, with a reason, when:**
   * - **the stored revision is not `song.revision`.** Someone else - another tab, another window - saved since this
   *   copy was read, and writing over theirs would lose their changes without a word. Last-writer-wins would be quieter
   *   and would lose work; merging two ProseMirror documents is collaboration's job (design Part 8), not a library's.
   *   So the save is refused and the page says so; reloading shows the other version. Compared for equality, not
   *   "older than", so a copy claiming a revision the store never reached is refused too: it did not come from here.
   * - **the song is no longer stored.** It was deleted - most likely in another tab - and writing it back would undo
   *   that delete behind the user's back.
   * - **its content could not be read back** (`songNodeOf`). A song is never written in a form that would open as
   *   unreadable; the editor only makes valid documents, so this guards against a bug, not the user.
   *
   * The check and the write are one readwrite transaction, so no other tab's save can land between them: IndexedDB runs
   * readwrite transactions on one store one at a time.
   */
  async saveSong(song: SongDoc): Promise<SongDoc> {
    const reading = songNodeOf(song.content);
    if (reading.kind === 'refused') {
      throw new SongLibraryError(`This song was not saved, because it could not be read back: ${reading.reason}`);
    }

    // Set inside the read's callback, so held in an object: a `let` assigned in a callback is invisible to the
    // narrowing after it.
    const outcome: { written?: SongDoc; refusal?: string } = {};
    try {
      const transaction = (await this.database()).transaction(STORE_NAME, 'readwrite');
      const store = transaction.objectStore(STORE_NAME);
      const read = store.get(song.id);
      read.onsuccess = () => {
        if (read.result === undefined) {
          outcome.refusal = NOT_IN_LIBRARY;
          return;
        }
        // A stored record that cannot be read has no revision to compare: the copy here cannot have come from it.
        const stored = songRecordOf(read.result);
        if (typeof stored === 'string' || stored.revision !== song.revision) {
          outcome.refusal = SAVED_ELSEWHERE;
          return;
        }
        // Listed rather than spread, so whatever else a caller hung on the record is not stored with it.
        outcome.written = {
          id: stored.id,
          revision: stored.revision + 1,
          createdAt: stored.createdAt,
          updatedAt: Date.now(),
          content: song.content
        };
        store.put(outcome.written);
      };
      await committed(transaction, ABANDONED);
    } catch (error) {
      throw failure('The song could not be saved', error);
    }

    if (outcome.refusal !== undefined) throw new SongLibraryError(outcome.refusal);
    // Committed with neither a refusal nor a write: the read's callback never ran, which a commit rules out.
    if (outcome.written === undefined) throw new SongLibraryError(`The song could not be saved: ${ABANDONED}`);
    await this.refreshAfterWrite();
    return outcome.written;
  }

  /**
   * Copies the song `id` into a new song titled "<title> (copy)" ("Untitled song (copy)" when it has none), at
   * revision 1, and returns the copy's id. Refuses a song that is not there or cannot be read: a copy of what could not
   * be read would be a second unreadable song.
   *
   * **Every section, chord, tab block and memo is given a fresh id.** A section's id is also the id of its derived
   * progression (`sectionProgressionOf`), and a chord's is its slot's, so a copy sharing them would be taken for the
   * original by anything that matches on them - Open in Progression's hand-off, a generated track's origin (S2). Fresh
   * ids make the copy a song of its own from the start. A memo's id is also the key of its audio, which has a store of
   * its own from S4; nothing is stored under a memo id before then, so renewing one loses nothing now.
   */
  async duplicateSong(id: string): Promise<string> {
    const loaded = await this.loadSong(id);
    if (loaded === null) throw new SongLibraryError(NOT_IN_LIBRARY);
    if (loaded.kind === 'unreadable') {
      throw new SongLibraryError(`This song cannot be read, so it cannot be copied: ${loaded.reason}`);
    }

    const title: string = loaded.node.attrs['title'];
    const copy = withFreshIdsOf(loaded.node);
    copy.setDocAttribute('title', `${title.trim() === '' ? UNTITLED_SONG : title} (copy)`);

    const now = Date.now();
    const song: SongDoc = { id: crypto.randomUUID(), revision: 1, createdAt: now, updatedAt: now, content: copy.doc.toJSON() };
    await this.write(song, 'The song could not be copied');
    return song.id;
  }

  /**
   * Deletes the song `id`, resolving once the delete has committed. An id that is not there resolves too - IndexedDB
   * counts it a success - so deleting a song twice, from two tabs, is harmless.
   */
  async deleteSong(id: string): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const transaction = (await this.database()).transaction(STORE_NAME, 'readwrite');
      transaction.objectStore(STORE_NAME).delete(id);
      await committed(transaction, ABANDONED);
    } catch (error) {
      throw failure('The song could not be deleted', error);
    }
    await this.refreshAfterWrite();
  }

  /** Adds a new record, settled on its commit. `add`, not `put`: a new song never writes over one already stored. */
  private async write(song: SongDoc, what: string): Promise<void> {
    try {
      const transaction = (await this.database()).transaction(STORE_NAME, 'readwrite');
      transaction.objectStore(STORE_NAME).add(song);
      await committed(transaction, ABANDONED);
    } catch (error) {
      throw failure(what, error);
    }
    await this.refreshAfterWrite();
  }

  /** The stored record under `id`, unchecked, or undefined when there is none. */
  private async read(id: string): Promise<unknown> {
    try {
      const db = await this.database();
      return await new Promise<unknown>((resolve, reject) => {
        const request = db.transaction(STORE_NAME, 'readonly').objectStore(STORE_NAME).get(id);
        request.onsuccess = () => resolve(request.result);
        request.onerror = () => reject(request.error ?? new Error(ABANDONED_READ));
      });
    } catch (error) {
      throw failure('The song could not be read', error);
    }
  }

  /**
   * Lists the library again after a write, while anything is watching the list.
   *
   * **Only while watched**, because reading the list reads and checks every song (`refresh`), and the sheet - where
   * autosave writes, a moment after every pause in typing - does not show it. Re-reading the whole library under each
   * autosave would be work nobody sees, growing with the library. A list nobody watches goes stale instead, and is
   * read afresh by the list page when it opens (`getSummaries`).
   *
   * **Its failure is logged, not thrown:** the write landed, and a caller told it failed would say so - autosave showing
   * "Not saved" over a song that is saved.
   */
  private async refreshAfterWrite(): Promise<void> {
    if (!this.summariesSubject.observed) return;
    await this.refresh().catch(error => console.error('Failed to list the song library after a write:', error));
  }

  /**
   * Opens the database once; later calls await the same promise - until the open fails, or the connection is let go,
   * and the next call opens it again. A failed open kept would fail every call after it for as long as the page is
   * open.
   */
  private database(): Promise<IDBDatabase> {
    if (this.readyPromise) return this.readyPromise;

    const opening = new Promise<IDBDatabase>((resolve, reject) => {
      const request = indexedDB.open(this.dbName, DB_VERSION);

      request.onupgradeneeded = () => {
        const db = request.result;
        // No indexes: the list is read whole through a cursor and sorted in memory - a songwriter's library is tens of
        // songs, not thousands - and an index on a field inside `content` is not possible anyway.
        if (!db.objectStoreNames.contains(STORE_NAME)) db.createObjectStore(STORE_NAME, { keyPath: 'id' });
      };

      request.onsuccess = () => {
        const db = request.result;
        const letGo = (): void => {
          if (this.readyPromise === opening) this.readyPromise = null;
        };
        // A delete of the database, or an upgrade to a later version from another tab, waits until every connection to
        // it closes. Held open, this one would hold them up for as long as the page is open.
        db.onversionchange = () => {
          db.close();
          letGo();
        };
        // The browser closed it - storage cleared, the disk gone - so the next call opens it again rather than failing
        // on a dead connection.
        db.onclose = letGo;
        resolve(db);
      };

      request.onerror = () => {
        if (this.readyPromise === opening) this.readyPromise = null;
        reject(request.error ?? new Error('The browser refused to open it.'));
      };
    }).catch(error => {
      throw failure('The song library could not be opened', error);
    });

    this.readyPromise = opening;
    return opening;
  }
}

/**
 * `doc` with a fresh UUID on every node that carries an id, as a transform whose `doc` is the copy - so the caller can
 * add its own steps (the copy's title) before reading it.
 *
 * `setNodeAttribute` replaces no content, so every position found before the first step is still right after the last.
 */
function withFreshIdsOf(doc: Node): Transform {
  const transform = new Transform(doc);
  doc.descendants((node, pos) => {
    if (typeof node.attrs['id'] === 'string') transform.setNodeAttribute(pos, 'id', crypto.randomUUID());
  });
  return transform;
}

/**
 * A stored value as a `SongDoc`, or the reason it is not one.
 *
 * Checks the record's own fields, which `songNodeOf` - checking only `content` - cannot: a record without a revision
 * could never be saved over (`saveSong` compares it), and one whose content is not an object would throw in
 * `songSummaryOf`.
 */
function songRecordOf(value: unknown): SongDoc | string {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null) return 'The stored song is not a record.';
  const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  if (typeof record['id'] !== 'string') return 'The stored song has no id.';
  const revision = record['revision'];
  if (typeof revision !== 'number' || !Number.isInteger(revision) || revision < 0) {
    return 'The stored song has no revision.';
  }
  for (const field of ['createdAt', 'updatedAt']) {
    if (typeof record[field] !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(record[field])) return `The stored song has no ${field}.`;
  }
  const content = record['content'];
  if (typeof content !== 'object' || content === null || Array.isArray(content)) return 'The stored song has no content.';
  return record as unknown as SongDoc;
}

/**
 * A stored value's library card: `songSummaryOf` for a record, and for anything else a card that says why it cannot be
 * opened, under whatever id it is stored at and with an `updatedAt` of 0 if it has none, so it sorts last.
 */
function cardOf(value: unknown): SongSummary {
  const record = songRecordOf(value);
  if (typeof record !== 'string') return songSummaryOf(record);

  const fields = typeof value === 'object' && value !== null ? (value as Record<string, unknown>) : {};
  const updatedAt = fields['updatedAt'];
  return {
    id: String(fields['id']),
    title: '',
    artist: '',
    key: null,
    sectionCount: 0,
    updatedAt: typeof updatedAt === 'number' && Number.isFinite(updatedAt) ? updatedAt : 0,
    unreadable: record
  };
}

/** An error this service has already worded for a page: passed on as it is, never wrapped a second time. */
class SongLibraryError extends Error {}

/**
 * An Error for a page to show: what could not be done, then why.
 *
 * IndexedDB's own errors are `DOMException`s whose message describes the transaction ("The transaction was aborted"),
 * not the song, so the message leads with what the user tried. One of this service's own - an open that failed, seen
 * by the read that needed it - is already worded, and is passed on unchanged.
 */
function failure(what: string, error: unknown): Error {
  return error instanceof SongLibraryError ? error : new SongLibraryError(`${what}: ${messageOf(error)}`);
}
```

```ts
import { ComponentFixture, TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { Router, provideRouter } from '@angular/router';

import { SongLibraryPageComponent } from './song-library-page.component';
import { abortOnSuccess, deletedDatabase } from '../../../services/indexed-db.spec-helper';
import { SONG_LIBRARY_DB, SongLibraryService } from '../../../services/song-library.service';

/**
 * The Songs library (design Part 6): its cards, its search, New song, Duplicate, Delete, the card a corrupt song gets,
 * and where it says what went wrong. Against a library of its own in real IndexedDB, deleted after each spec.

describe('SongLibraryPageComponent', () => {
  let fixture: ComponentFixture<SongLibraryPageComponent>;
  let library: SongLibraryService;
  let dbName: string;
  let host: HTMLElement;

  beforeEach(async () => {
    dbName = `song-library-page-spec-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}`;
    await TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      imports: [SongLibraryPageComponent],
      providers: [provideRouter([]), { provide: SONG_LIBRARY_DB, useValue: dbName }]
    }).compileComponents();
    library = TestBed.inject(SongLibraryService);
  });

  afterEach(async () => {
    fixture?.destroy();
    await deletedDatabase(dbName);
  });

  /** Creates the page, which lists the library as it opens, and waits for that first list to be on screen. */
  async function open(): Promise<void> {
    fixture = TestBed.createComponent(SongLibraryPageComponent);
    host = fixture.nativeElement;
    fixture.detectChanges();
    await until(() => host.querySelector('.library-body')?.getAttribute('aria-busy') === 'false');
  }

  /** Resolves once `done` holds, checking every few milliseconds for up to two seconds: IndexedDB answers outside the zone. */
  async function until(done: () => boolean): Promise<void> {
    for (let waited = 0; waited < 2000; waited += 10) {
      fixture.detectChanges();
      if (done()) return;
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 10));
    }
    fixture.detectChanges();
  }

  const cards = (): HTMLElement[] => Array.from(host.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>('.song-card'));
  const titles = (): string[] => cards().map(card => card.querySelector('.card-title')?.textContent?.trim() ?? '');
  const text = (selector: string): string => host.querySelector(selector)?.textContent?.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() ?? '';
  const status = (): string => text('.library-status');

  function search(query: string): void {
    const input = host.querySelector<HTMLInputElement>('input[type="search"]');
    if (!input) throw new Error('No search box');
    input.value = query;
    input.dispatchEvent(new Event('input'));
    fixture.detectChanges();
  }

  /** Opens `card`'s menu and presses the item `selector` names in it. */
  function choose(card: HTMLElement, selector: string): void {
    card.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.card-menu-toggle')?.click();
    fixture.detectChanges();
    const item = card.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>(selector);
    if (!item) throw new Error(`No ${selector} in the card's menu`);
    item.click();
  }

  /** Writes `record` straight into the store, past the service: how a corrupt record gets there. */
  async function putRaw(record: unknown): Promise<void> {
    await library.refresh();
    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      const request = indexedDB.open(dbName, 1);
      request.onerror = () => reject(request.error);
      request.onsuccess = () => {
        const db = request.result;
        const transaction = db.transaction('songs', 'readwrite');
        transaction.objectStore('songs').put(record);
        transaction.oncomplete = () => {
          db.close();
          resolve();
        };
        transaction.onabort = () => {
          db.close();
          reject(transaction.error);
        };
      };
    });
  }

      host.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.new-song')?.click();
      await until(() => navigate.calls.count() > 0);

      const summaries = await library.refresh();
      expect(summaries.length).toBe(1);
      expect(navigate).toHaveBeenCalledWith(['/songs', summaries[0].id]);
    });

    it('says why in the live region when the song could not be created, and goes nowhere', async () => {
      await open();
      const navigate = spyOn(TestBed.inject(Router), 'navigate').and.resolveTo(true);
      abortOnSuccess('add');

      host.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.new-song')?.click();
      await until(() => status() !== '');

      expect(status()).toMatch(/^The song could not be created: /);
      expect(host.querySelector('.library-status [role="status"]')).not.toBeNull();
      expect(navigate).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    });
  });

  describe("a card's menu", () => {
    beforeEach(async () => {
      await library.createSong({ title: 'Menu' });
      await open();
    });

    const toggle = (): HTMLButtonElement => {
      const button = cards()[0].querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.card-menu-toggle');
      if (!button) throw new Error('No menu toggle');
      return button;
    };

    it('opens on its button, and stays open: the click that opened it is not a click outside it', () => {
      toggle().click();
      fixture.detectChanges();

      expect(toggle().getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('true');
      expect(getComputedStyle(cards()[0].querySelector('.menu-panel') as Element).display).not.toBe('none');
    });

    it('closes on a click outside it', () => {
      toggle().click();
      fixture.detectChanges();

      document.body.click();
      fixture.detectChanges();

      expect(toggle().getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('false');
    });

    it('closes on Escape, giving the focus back to its button', () => {
      toggle().click();
      fixture.detectChanges();
      const duplicate = cards()[0].querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.card-duplicate');
      duplicate?.focus();

      duplicate?.dispatchEvent(new KeyboardEvent('keydown', { key: 'Escape', bubbles: true }));
      fixture.detectChanges();

      expect(toggle().getAttribute('aria-expanded')).toBe('false');

  describe('Duplicate', () => {

      choose(cards()[0], '.card-duplicate');

      expect(status()).toBe('Duplicated "Original"');
    });

  describe('Delete', () => {

      await open();

      choose(cards()[0], '.card-delete');
      await until(() => cards().length === 0);

      expect(confirm).toHaveBeenCalledOnceWith('Delete "Doomed"? This cannot be undone.');
```

```ts
import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { provideRouter } from '@angular/router';
import { RouterTestingHarness } from '@angular/router/testing';

import { SongEditorComponent } from './song-editor/song-editor.component';
import { SongLibraryPageComponent } from './song-library-page/song-library-page.component';
import { SONG_ROUTES } from './songs.routes';
import { deletedDatabase } from '../../services/indexed-db.spec-helper';
import { SONG_LIBRARY_DB } from '../../services/song-library.service';

/**
 * The two song routes `main.ts` registers, resolved through the router as the app resolves them - lazily - so a typo in
 * an import path or an export name fails here rather than on the first click in the nav.
 */
describe('SONG_ROUTES', () => {
  let harness: RouterTestingHarness;
```

```ts
import { relativeTimeOf } from './relative-time';

/**
 * How long ago something happened, as the library's cards say it ("Edited 5 minutes ago") and the sheet's save status
 * will ("Saved · just now"). Fixed instants on both sides, so nothing here depends on when it runs.
 */
describe('relativeTimeOf', () => {
  const NOW = Date.UTC(2026, 9, 1, 12, 0, 0);
  const SECOND = 1000;
  const MINUTE = 60 * SECOND;
  const HOUR = 60 * MINUTE;
  const DAY = 24 * HOUR;

  it('says "just now" for anything under a minute ago', () => {
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW, NOW)).toBe('just now');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 59 * SECOND, NOW)).toBe('just now');
  });

  it('says "just now" for a time ahead of the clock, rather than "in 3 minutes"', () => {
    // Another tab's clock, or this one corrected since the write: the thing has happened, so it happened just now.
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW + 3 * MINUTE, NOW)).toBe('just now');
  });

  it('counts minutes, then hours, then days, rounding down', () => {
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - MINUTE, NOW)).toBe('1 minute ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 59 * MINUTE - 59 * SECOND, NOW)).toBe('59 minutes ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - HOUR, NOW)).toBe('1 hour ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 23 * HOUR, NOW)).toBe('23 hours ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - DAY, NOW)).toBe('1 day ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 6 * DAY, NOW)).toBe('6 days ago');
  });

  it('counts weeks under a month, months under a year, and years after that', () => {
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 7 * DAY, NOW)).toBe('1 week ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 29 * DAY, NOW)).toBe('4 weeks ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 30 * DAY, NOW)).toBe('1 month ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 364 * DAY, NOW)).toBe('12 months ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 365 * DAY, NOW)).toBe('1 year ago');
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 3 * 365 * DAY, NOW)).toBe('3 years ago');
  });

  it('never says "yesterday": 30 hours ago at one in the morning was the day before that', () => {
    expect(relativeTimeOf(NOW - 30 * HOUR, NOW)).toBe('1 day ago');
  });
});
```

```ts
describe('keyNameOf', () => {
  const musicTheory = new MusicTheoryService();
  const ionian = { name: 'Ionian (Major)' };
  const dorian = { name: 'Dorian' };

  it('names a key as the progression page does: the tonic, then the scale as the catalogue calls it', () => {
    expect(keyNameOf(C_MAJOR, ionian)).toBe('C Ionian (Major)');
    expect(keyNameOf(B_FLAT_MAJOR, ionian)).toBe('Bb Ionian (Major)');
    expect(keyNameOf({ tonic: 6, scaleId: 'dorian', preferSharps: true }, dorian)).toBe('F# Dorian');
  });

  it("spells the tonic by the key's own preference", () => {
    expect(keyNameOf({ tonic: 1, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true }, ionian)).toBe('C# Ionian (Major)');
    expect(keyNameOf({ tonic: 1, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: false }, ionian)).toBe('Db Ionian (Major)');
  });

  it('names the tonic alone when the scale is not one the app knows, rather than printing "C undefined"', () => {
    expect(keyNameOf({ tonic: 0, scaleId: 'gone', preferSharps: true }, null)).toBe('C');
  });

  it("agrees with the progression page's key line for every tonic, both spellings, and every scale", () => {
    let checked = 0;
    for (const category of musicTheory.getScaleCategories()) {
      for (const scale of category.scales) {
        for (let tonic = 0; tonic < 12; tonic++) {
          for (const preferSharps of [true, false]) {
            const key: ProgressionKey = { tonic, scaleId: scale.id, preferSharps };
            expect(keyNameOf(key, scale)).toBe(`${musicTheory.spellNote(tonic, preferSharps)} ${scale.name}`);
            checked++;
          }
        }
      }
    }
    expect(checked).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { ChangeDetectionStrategy, Component } from '@angular/core';
import { RouterLink } from '@angular/router';

/**
 * A song's sheet, at `/songs/:id` (design Part 2): the page the library's cards open.
 *
 * So far it is the page's frame alone - the way back to the library, and the line it shows while the song is read -
 * so the route, the library's links and the nav can be built and checked against the component that will hold the
 * editor, under the name and in the folder it keeps. The editor itself, its toolbar and its side panel grow in this
 * file.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-song-editor',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [RouterLink],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  templateUrl: './song-editor.component.html',
  styleUrls: ['./song-editor.component.scss']
})
export class SongEditorComponent {}
```

```html
<div class="song-library">
  <header class="library-header">
    <!-- Focusable from script only: where the focus goes when a deleted song's card takes its button away. -->
    <h1 #heading tabindex="-1">Songs</h1>

    <div class="header-actions">
      <label class="search">
        <span class="search-label">Search songs</span>
        <input
          #searchBox
          type="search"
          placeholder="Search title or artist"
          autocomplete="off"
          [value]="query"
          (input)="setQuery(searchBox.value)"
        />
      </label>
      <button type="button" class="tool new-song" (click)="createSong()">
        <svg aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
          <line x1="12" y1="5" x2="12" y2="19" />
          <line x1="5" y1="12" x2="19" y2="12" />
        </svg>
        New song
      </button>
    </div>
  </header>

  <!--
    What the page did, or why it could not. Always on the page and only its words change: a region inserted with its
    message already in it is the case screen readers miss. Two halves that swap, so a repeated message is a change
    (`SongLibraryPageComponent.messages`). Polite: nothing here interrupts what is being read.
  -->
  <p class="library-status" [class.is-error]="messageIsError">
    <span role="status">{{ messages[0] }}</span><span role="status">{{ messages[1] }}</span>
  </p>

  <section class="library-body" [attr.aria-busy]="listing === 'reading'">
    <p class="empty-state" *ngIf="listing === 'read' && visibleCards.length === 0 && query.trim() === ''">
      No songs yet — <button type="button" class="tool" (click)="createSong()">New song</button>
    </p>
    <p class="empty-state" *ngIf="visibleCards.length === 0 && query.trim() !== ''">No songs match "{{ query.trim() }}"</p>

    <ul class="song-grid" *ngIf="visibleCards.length > 0">
      <li
        *ngFor="let card of visibleCards; trackBy: trackById"
        class="song-card"
        [class.unreadable]="card.unreadable !== null"
        [class.menu-open]="openMenuId === card.id"
      >
        <!-- A song that can be opened: the title is the link, stretched over the card by its ::after. -->
        <ng-container *ngIf="card.unreadable === null; else unreadableCard">
          <h2 class="card-title">
            <a class="card-link" [routerLink]="['/songs', card.id]">{{ card.title }}</a>
          </h2>
          <p class="card-artist" *ngIf="card.artist">{{ card.artist }}</p>
          <p class="card-meta">
            <span class="card-key">{{ card.keyName }}</span>
            <span class="card-sections">{{ card.sections }}</span>
          </p>
          <p class="card-edited" *ngIf="card.edited">
            Edited <time [attr.datetime]="card.editedAt" [title]="card.editedOn">{{ card.edited }}</time>
          </p>

          <div class="card-menu" [class.open]="openMenuId === card.id" (keydown.escape)="closeMenu(toggle, $event)">
            <button
              #toggle
              type="button"
              class="tool card-menu-toggle"
              [class.on]="openMenuId === card.id"
              [attr.aria-label]="'More for ' + card.title"
              [attr.aria-expanded]="openMenuId === card.id"
              [attr.aria-controls]="'song-menu-' + card.id"
              (click)="toggleMenu(card.id)"
            >
              <svg aria-hidden="true" width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="currentColor">
                <circle cx="5" cy="12" r="2" />
                <circle cx="12" cy="12" r="2" />
                <circle cx="19" cy="12" r="2" />
              </svg>
            </button>
            <!-- Hidden with CSS rather than removed, so aria-controls always points at something. -->
            <div class="menu-panel" role="group" [id]="'song-menu-' + card.id" [attr.aria-label]="card.title">
              <button type="button" class="tool card-duplicate" (click)="duplicateSong(card, toggle)">Duplicate</button>
              <button type="button" class="tool card-delete" (click)="deleteSong(card, toggle)">Delete</button>
            </div>
          </div>
        </ng-container>

        <ng-template #unreadableCard>
          <h2 class="card-title">{{ card.title }}</h2>
          <p class="card-reason">{{ card.unreadable }}</p>
          <p class="card-edited" *ngIf="card.edited">
            Edited <time [attr.datetime]="card.editedAt" [title]="card.editedOn">{{ card.edited }}</time>
          </p>
          <button
            #remove
            type="button"
            class="tool card-delete"
            [attr.aria-label]="'Delete ' + card.title"
            (click)="deleteSong(card, remove)"
          >Delete</button>
        </ng-template>
      </li>
    </ul>
  </section>
</div>
```

```scss
@use '../../../styles/a11y';

// The app's dark scheme, named once for the page: the GP library's surfaces and card, the progression page's dim
// grey (#adbcc8, 4.8:1 on the card where the meta line sits) and its error pink (6:1 on these surfaces). The one blue
// marks the one thing selected - a card whose menu is open - as the flat tool palettes do.
:host {
  --songs-surface: #1a252f;
  --songs-bar: #2c3e50;
  --songs-card: #34495e;
  --songs-border: #465666;
  --songs-text: #ecf0f1;
  --songs-text-dim: #adbcc8;
  --songs-accent: #3498db;
  --songs-error: #f1948a;

  display: block;
}

// Fills the window under the shell's header and scrolls itself: the shell's `main` hides its overflow, so a page
// taller than the window would otherwise be cut off. The composer's measure, header height and all.
.song-library {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  height: calc(100vh - var(--app-header-height, 57px));
  height: calc(100dvh - var(--app-header-height, 57px));
  background-color: var(--songs-surface);
  color: var(--songs-text);
}

.library-header {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  justify-content: space-between;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 1rem;
  padding: 1rem 1.5rem;
  background-color: var(--songs-bar);
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--songs-border);

  h1 {
    margin: 0;
    font-size: 1.5rem;
    font-weight: 600;

    &:focus {
      outline: none;
    }
  }
}

.header-actions {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.75rem;
}

.search-label {
  @extend %sr-only;
}

.search input {
  width: 16rem;
  max-width: 100%;
  padding: 0.45rem 0.75rem;
  background-color: var(--songs-surface);
  border: 1px solid var(--songs-border);
  border-radius: 4px;
  color: var(--songs-text);
  font: inherit;
  font-size: 0.9rem;

  &::placeholder {
    color: var(--songs-text-dim);
  }

  &:focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid var(--songs-text);
    outline-offset: -1px;
  }
}

// The flat tool style (composer palette): no chrome until hovered, colour only on the selected one (`.on`).
.tool {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.4rem;
  padding: 0.45rem 0.75rem;
  background: transparent;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 3px;
  color: var(--songs-text);
  font: inherit;
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color 90ms ease-out;

  &:hover:not(.on) {
    background-color: rgb(255 255 255 / 10%);
  }

  &:active {
    background-color: rgb(255 255 255 / 16%);
  }

  &.on {
    background-color: var(--songs-accent);
    color: #fff;
  }

  &:focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid var(--songs-text);
    outline-offset: -2px;
  }
}

// Collapses to nothing while it has nothing to say; never removed (see the template).
.library-status {
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0 1.5rem;
  color: var(--songs-text-dim);
  font-size: 0.9rem;

  span:not(:empty) {
    display: block;
    padding: 0.6rem 0;
  }

  &.is-error {
    color: var(--songs-error);
  }
}

.library-body {
  flex: 1;
  overflow-y: auto;
  padding: 1.5rem;
}

.empty-state {
  margin: 3rem 0 0;
  text-align: center;
  color: var(--songs-text-dim);
  font-size: 1rem;

  .tool {
    padding: 0.25rem 0.5rem;
    text-decoration: underline;
  }
}

.song-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(260px, 1fr));
  gap: 1rem;
  margin: 0;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}

// The GP library's card: raised surface, rounded, lifting a little under the pointer.
.song-card {
  position: relative;
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 0.25rem;
  min-height: 8rem;
  padding: 1rem;
  background-color: var(--songs-card);
  border-radius: 8px;
  transition: transform 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s;

  &:not(.unreadable):hover {
    transform: translateY(-2px);
    box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgb(0 0 0 / 30%);
  }

  // Above its neighbours while its menu is open, so the menu is not drawn under the next card.
  &.menu-open {
    z-index: 2;
  }

  p {
    margin: 0;
  }
}

.card-title {
  margin: 0 2.25rem 0 0;
  font-size: 1rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

.card-link {
  color: inherit;
  text-decoration: none;

  // Stretched over the whole card, so anywhere on it opens the song while the link's name stays the title.
  &::after {
    content: '';
    position: absolute;
    inset: 0;
    border-radius: 8px;
  }

  &:focus-visible {
    outline: none;

    &::after {
      outline: 2px solid var(--songs-text);
      outline-offset: 2px;
    }
  }
}

.card-artist {
  color: var(--songs-text-dim);
  font-size: 0.9rem;
  white-space: nowrap;
  overflow: hidden;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}

// Pinned to the foot of the card, so the meta lines of a row of cards line up whatever their titles' lengths.
.song-card .card-meta {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 0 0.75rem;
  margin-top: auto;
  padding-top: 0.75rem;
  border-top: 1px solid var(--songs-border);
  color: var(--songs-text-dim);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
}

.card-edited {
  color: var(--songs-text-dim);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
}

.card-reason {
  color: var(--songs-error);
  font-size: 0.85rem;
}

.song-card.unreadable .card-delete {
  align-self: flex-start;
  margin-top: auto;
  margin-left: -0.75rem;
}

// Above the stretched link, so the button is pressed rather than the card followed.
.card-menu {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0.5rem;
  right: 0.5rem;
  z-index: 1;
}

.card-menu-toggle {
  padding: 0.35rem;
}

.menu-panel {
  display: none;
  position: absolute;
  top: calc(100% + 0.25rem);
  right: 0;
  min-width: 9rem;
  padding: 0.25rem;
  flex-direction: column;
  background-color: var(--songs-bar);
  border: 1px solid var(--songs-border);
  border-radius: 6px;
  box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgb(0 0 0 / 40%);

  .tool {
    justify-content: flex-start;
    width: 100%;
  }
}

.card-menu.open .menu-panel {
  display: flex;
}

@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .library-header {
    flex-direction: column;
    align-items: stretch;
  }

  .header-actions {
    justify-content: space-between;
  }

  .search {
    flex: 1;

    input {
      width: 100%;
    }
  }

  .library-body {
    padding: 1rem;
  }
}
```

```ts
import { CommonModule } from '@angular/common';
import {
  ChangeDetectionStrategy,
  ChangeDetectorRef,
  Component,
  ElementRef,
  HostListener,
  OnDestroy,
  OnInit,
  ViewChild,
  inject
} from '@angular/core';
import { Router, RouterLink } from '@angular/router';
import { Subject, interval } from 'rxjs';
import { takeUntil } from 'rxjs/operators';
import type { SongSummary } from '../../../models/song.model';
import { messageOf } from '../../../services/error-message';
import { MusicTheoryService } from '../../../services/music-theory.service';
import { ProgressionKeyContext } from '../../../services/progression-key-context';
import { relativeTimeOf } from '../../../services/relative-time';
import { keyNameOf } from '../../../services/song-chord-names';
import { UNTITLED_SONG } from '../../../services/song-document';
import { SongLibraryService } from '../../../services/song-library.service';

/**
 * One song's card, everything it prints worked out once per render rather than in the template: a library re-renders
 * each minute (`relativeTimeOf` moves on), and a card's key name needs a scale lookup.
 */
export interface SongCard {
  id: string;
  /** The song's title, or "Untitled song" when it has none: also the name Delete's question uses. */
  title: string;
  artist: string;
  /** `keyNameOf`: "C Ionian (Major)". Null on a card for a song that cannot be read. */
  keyName: string | null;
  /** "1 section", "4 sections". */
  sections: string;
  /** "5 minutes ago", or null for a record with no usable time (a corrupt one, sorted last as time 0). */
  edited: string | null;
  /** The same moment for `<time datetime>` and, in the reader's own locale, for its tooltip. */
  editedAt: string | null;
  editedOn: string | null;
  /** "This song cannot be opened: <reason>", or null for a song that can be. */
  unreadable: string | null;
  /** The title and artist folded for search (`foldedOf`), so a keystroke compares strings and nothing else. */
  searchText: string;
}

/** How far the first read of the library has got: the empty state waits for `read`, so it never flashes up first. */
type Listing = 'reading' | 'read' | 'failed';

/**
 * The Songs library, at `/songs` (design Part 6): a card for every song, newest first, with search, New song, and on
 * each card Duplicate and Delete.
 *
 * - **A card is a real link** to `/songs/<id>`, stretched over the card by the title's `::after`, so the whole card
 *   opens the song while the link's name is just the title - not the title, artist, key, count and date read out as one
 *   name. The menu button sits above the stretched area, outside the link: a button inside a link is invalid HTML and
 *   a click on it would follow the link.
 * - **A song that cannot be read** gets a card that says why, with Delete as its only action - no link, since opening
 *   it can only say again that it cannot be opened, and no Duplicate, since a copy of it would be a second one
 *   (`SongLibraryService.duplicateSong` refuses it anyway).
 * - **Delete asks first**, through `window.confirm`, naming the song, as the composer's library and the GP library
 *   ask: a song is a writer's work, there is no undo for a delete, and a dialog of the app's own would be the first.
 * - **What the page did, or why it could not**, goes to one polite live region that is always on the page (`say`).
 *
 * The list is the library service's (`getSummaries`); this page holds only what it shows of it - the search, which
 * menu is open, its last message - which is view state, not application state.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-song-library-page',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [CommonModule, RouterLink],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  templateUrl: './song-library-page.component.html',
  styleUrls: ['./song-library-page.component.scss']
})
export class SongLibraryPageComponent implements OnInit, OnDestroy {
  private readonly library = inject(SongLibraryService);
  private readonly router = inject(Router);
  private readonly changes = inject(ChangeDetectorRef);
  private readonly keys = new ProgressionKeyContext(inject(MusicTheoryService));
  private readonly destroy$ = new Subject<void>();

  @ViewChild('heading', { static: true }) private heading?: ElementRef<HTMLElement>;

  private summaries: readonly SongSummary[] = [];
  private cards: SongCard[] = [];

  /** The cards the search lets through, in the library's order. */
  visibleCards: SongCard[] = [];
  /** The search as typed; matched trimmed and folded (`foldedOf`). */
  query = '';
  listing: Listing = 'reading';
  /** The id of the card whose menu is open; one at a time, as menus are. */
  openMenuId: string | null = null;

  /**
   * The live region's two halves, one holding the message and the other empty, swapped on every message (`say`): the
   * same failure twice is then a change in both, and announced again, where one region set to the text it already
   * holds says nothing - `ProgressionComponent.alerts`' pattern.
   */
  messages: readonly [string, string] = ['', ''];
  /** Whether the message showing is a failure, for its colour; the words say it either way. */
  messageIsError = false;

  /** A New song under way: a second press would make a second song. */
  private creating = false;

  ngOnInit(): void {
    this.library
      .getSummaries()
      .pipe(takeUntil(this.destroy$))
      .subscribe(summaries => {
        this.summaries = summaries;
        // A list published after a failed first read came from a read that worked - a write's - so the library can
        // now be said to be empty if it is.
        if (this.listing === 'failed') this.listing = 'read';
        this.render();
      });

    // "Edited 5 minutes ago" goes stale on a page left open, so the cards are worded again each minute.
    interval(60_000)
      .pipe(takeUntil(this.destroy$))
      .subscribe(() => this.render());

    // Read on arrival, because the list nobody watched is stale: another tab may have written since
    // (`SongLibraryService.getSummaries`).
    this.library.refresh().then(
      () => this.settleListing('read'),
      error => {
        this.settleListing('failed');
        this.say(messageOf(error), true);
      }
    );
  }

  ngOnDestroy(): void {
    this.destroy$.next();
    this.destroy$.complete();
  }

  trackById(_index: number, card: SongCard): string {
    return card.id;
  }

  setQuery(query: string): void {
    this.query = query;
    this.filter();
  }

  /** Makes a song and opens it. Its card is there when the user comes back. */
  async createSong(): Promise<void> {
    if (this.creating) return;
    this.creating = true;
    try {
      const song = await this.library.createSong();
      await this.router.navigate(['/songs', song.id]);
    } catch (error) {
      this.say(messageOf(error), true);
    } finally {
      this.creating = false;
    }
  }

  toggleMenu(id: string): void {
    this.openMenuId = this.openMenuId === id ? null : id;
  }

  /** Escape closes the open menu and gives the focus back to its button, since the item focused is hidden with it. */
  closeMenu(toggle: HTMLElement, event: Event): void {
    if (this.openMenuId === null) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    this.openMenuId = null;
    toggle.focus();
  }

  /**
   * A click anywhere outside the cards' menus closes the open one, as a menu is expected to.
   *
   * Any card's menu, not only the open one: this runs in the same dispatch as the toggle's own click, before the view
   * has caught up with it, so the menu just opened is not yet marked open - asking for `.open` here would close every
   * menu the moment it opened. A click on another card's button is that button's to answer (`toggleMenu`).
   */
  @HostListener('document:click', ['$event'])
  onDocumentClick(event: MouseEvent): void {
    if (this.openMenuId === null) return;
    const target = event.target;
    if (target instanceof Element && target.closest('.card-menu') !== null) return;
    this.openMenuId = null;
    this.changes.markForCheck();
  }

  /** Copies the song; the copy's card arrives with the list the copy's write publishes. */
  async duplicateSong(card: SongCard, toggle: HTMLElement): Promise<void> {
    this.openMenuId = null;
    toggle.focus();
    try {
      await this.library.duplicateSong(card.id);
      this.say(`Duplicated "${card.title}"`);
    } catch (error) {
      this.say(messageOf(error), true);
    }
  }

  /**
   * Deletes the song once the user has said yes. The card goes, and its button with it, so the focus goes to the page's
   * heading rather than being dropped on the page's body; on a no it goes back to where it was.
   */
  async deleteSong(card: SongCard, returnTo: HTMLElement): Promise<void> {
    this.openMenuId = null;
    returnTo.focus();
    if (!window.confirm(`Delete "${card.title}"? This cannot be undone.`)) return;

    try {
      await this.library.deleteSong(card.id);
      this.say(`Deleted "${card.title}"`);
      this.heading?.nativeElement.focus();
    } catch (error) {
      this.say(messageOf(error), true);
    }
  }

  /** Puts `message` in the live region, in the half that is empty (see `messages`). */
  private say(message: string, isError = false): void {
    this.messages = this.messages[0] === '' ? [message, ''] : ['', message];
    this.messageIsError = isError;
    this.changes.markForCheck();
  }

  private settleListing(listing: Listing): void {
    this.listing = listing;
    this.changes.markForCheck();
  }

  /** Words every card again from the last list, at the current time, and filters them. */
  private render(): void {
    const now = Date.now();
    this.cards = this.summaries.map(summary => this.cardOf(summary, now));
    this.filter();
  }

  private filter(): void {
    const query = foldedOf(this.query.trim());
    this.visibleCards = query === '' ? this.cards : this.cards.filter(card => card.searchText.includes(query));
    this.changes.markForCheck();
  }

  private cardOf(summary: SongSummary, now: number): SongCard {
    const title = summary.title.trim() === '' ? UNTITLED_SONG : summary.title;
    const at = summary.updatedAt > 0 ? new Date(summary.updatedAt) : null;
    return {
      id: summary.id,
      title,
      artist: summary.artist,
      keyName: summary.key === null ? null : keyNameOf(summary.key, this.keys.findScale(summary.key.scaleId)),
      sections: `${summary.sectionCount} section${summary.sectionCount === 1 ? '' : 's'}`,
      edited: at === null ? null : relativeTimeOf(summary.updatedAt, now),
      editedAt: at?.toISOString() ?? null,
      editedOn: at?.toLocaleString() ?? null,
      unreadable: summary.unreadable === null ? null : `This song cannot be opened: ${summary.unreadable}`,
      // The title as shown, so "untitled" finds the songs the page calls that.
      searchText: foldedOf(`${title}\n${summary.artist}`)
    };
  }
}

/**
 * `text` as search compares it: lower case, with accents taken off, so "cafe" finds "Café" and "ANGSTROM" finds
 * "Ångström". NFD splits a letter from its marks and the marks are dropped; a letter with no decomposition (ø, ß)
 * stays as it is, which is the cheap end of accent-insensitive and enough for titles.
 */
function foldedOf(text: string): string {
  return text.normalize('NFD').replace(/\p{M}/gu, '').toLocaleLowerCase('en');
}
```

```ts
import { Routes } from '@angular/router';

/**
 * The songwriting pages: the library at `/songs` and a song's sheet at `/songs/:id` (design Part 6). `main.ts` spreads
 * these into the app's routes.
 *
 * **In a file of their own** so their spec resolves the very routes the app registers, rather than a copy of them that
 * could drift: `main.ts` bootstraps on import and cannot be imported by a spec.
 *
 * **Both lazy, and this file must stay free of value imports from the pages**, for the reason the other lazy routes in
 * `main.ts` give: what `main.ts` imports statically is in `main`. The library and the sheet both reach ProseMirror -
 * the library through `SongLibraryService`, which reads every song's document to make its card - and the sheet will
 * reach Tone for its audition, so a `component:` here would carry both into the bundle every visitor downloads. Only a
 * dynamic `import()` keeps them in the songs chunks.
 *
 * Two routes rather than a parent with children: the pages share no layout, so a parent would be a component that only
 * hosts an outlet.
 */
export const SONG_ROUTES: Routes = [
  {
    path: 'songs',
    loadComponent: () => import('./song-library-page/song-library-page.component')
      .then(m => m.SongLibraryPageComponent)
  },
  {
    path: 'songs/:id',
    loadComponent: () => import('./song-editor/song-editor.component')
      .then(m => m.SongEditorComponent)
  }
];
```
