```ts
import { CommonModule } from '@angular/common';
import {
  ChangeDetectionStrategy,
  Component,
  ElementRef,
  EventEmitter,
  HostListener,
  Input,
  OnChanges,
  Output,
  ViewChild,
  inject
} from '@angular/core';
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import type { TimeSignature } from '../../../models/composer.model';
import { MIN_SLOT_BEATS } from '../../../models/progression-normalize';
import type { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../../../models/progression.model';
import { ModalFocus } from '../../../services/modal-focus';
import { barBeats } from '../../../services/progression-score';
import {
  SongEdit,
  SongKeyRules,
  changeChord,
  chordWithId,
  deleteChord,
  setChordLength
} from '../../../services/song-commands';
import { numeralOf } from '../../../services/song-chord-names';
import { songMetaOf } from '../../../services/song-document';
import { ChordNaming, chordLabelOf } from '../song-sheet/chord-view';
import { SongChordFieldComponent } from '../song-chord-field/song-chord-field.component';

/** One of the length presets: a share of a bar of the song's meter. */
export interface LengthPreset {
  label: string;
  beats: number;
}

/** Everything the popover shows, worked out from the document once per change rather than in the template. */
interface PopoverModel {
  key: ProgressionKey;
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[] | null;
  /** The chord as the sheet names it, for the field to start from: `Am`, or empty for a chord with no name. */
  name: string;
  /** The heading: `Am · vi`, or the name alone when the chord has no numeral. */
  title: string;
  lengthBeats: number;
  lengthText: string;
  presets: readonly LengthPreset[];
}

/**
 * The length presets for a meter: half a bar, a bar and two bars, in beats (quarter notes, `barBeats`) - leaving out
 * any shorter than the shortest a chord can be (`MIN_SLOT_BEATS`), which a press could only round up to something
 * the label does not say. A bar of 4/4 is 4 beats, of 3/4 is 3, of 6/8 is 3.
 */
export function lengthPresetsOf(timeSignature: TimeSignature): LengthPreset[] {
  const bar = barBeats(timeSignature);
  return [
    { label: '½ bar', beats: bar / 2 },
    { label: '1 bar', beats: bar },
    { label: '2 bars', beats: bar * 2 }
  ].filter(preset => preset.beats >= MIN_SLOT_BEATS);
}

/** Gives each popover's heading a distinct id for `aria-labelledby`. */
let popoverCount = 0;

/** A length as the stepper shows it: "1 beat", "4 beats", "1.5 beats". */
function lengthTextOf(beats: number): string {
  const shown = Number(beats.toFixed(2));
  return `${shown} ${shown === 1 ? 'beat' : 'beats'}`;
}

/**
 * The popover a chord on the sheet opens when its name is clicked, or Enter is pressed on it (design Part 2): change
 * the chord, change its length, delete it.
 *
 * **Everything it does is a song command**, handed to the page on `edit` and run on the sheet, so each press is one
 * step in the song's undo history and the popover keeps no copy of the chord: it is given the document after every
 * change and finds its chord again by id. A document without it - the chord undone away - shows nothing, and the page
 * closes the popover.
 *
 * - **Chord**: the chord field, starting from the chord's lead-sheet name. Enter runs `changeChord` - the same chord
 *   id and length, the new degree, re-voiced (see `changeChord` for why owned pitches are handed back, as on the
 *   progression page).
 * - **Length**: a stepper that moves to the next whole beat either way, and presets of half a bar, a bar and two bars
 *   of the song's meter, the one the chord is now marked pressed (`setChordLength`).
 * - **Delete** (`deleteChord`), which closes the popover.
 *
 * Hearing the chord is task 9's: the popover has no button for it until there is a sound behind it.
 *
 * **Focus.** A non-modal dialog: nothing behind it is made inert, and a press outside it closes it, leaving the focus
 * where the press put it. While it is open the focus is in it - on the chord field first - and Tab goes round its
 * controls rather than out into the page, by the composer's `ModalFocus.trapTab`; the rest of `ModalFocus`, which
 * moves the focus to a heading and back on an `open` input, does not fit a popover the page creates and destroys, so
 * the page gives the focus back instead (`closed` says whether it should). Escape anywhere in it closes it and gives
 * the focus back to the sheet, with the chord still selected.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-song-chord-popover',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [CommonModule, SongChordFieldComponent],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  templateUrl: './song-chord-popover.component.html',
  styleUrls: ['./song-chord-popover.component.scss']
})
export class SongChordPopoverComponent implements OnChanges {
  /** The song now. */
  @Input() doc: Node | null = null;
  /** The chord this popover is for. */
  @Input() chordId = '';
  @Input() keys: Pick<SongKeyRules, 'chordScaleFor'> | null = null;

  /** A change to the song, for the page to run on the sheet. */
  @Output() readonly edit = new EventEmitter<SongEdit>();
  /**
   * The popover is done: true when the focus should go back to the sheet, false when a press outside has already put
   * it somewhere else.
   */
  @Output() readonly closed = new EventEmitter<boolean>();

  @ViewChild('dialog') private dialog?: ElementRef<HTMLElement>;

  private readonly host: HTMLElement = inject(ElementRef).nativeElement;
  private readonly focus = new ModalFocus();

  readonly titleId = `song-chord-popover-title-${++popoverCount}`;
  model: PopoverModel | null = null;

  ngOnChanges(): void {
    this.model = this.modelOf();
  }

  /** Escape from anywhere inside closes it. The chord field's own Escape is the same request, and stops there. */
  @HostListener('keydown', ['$event'])
  onKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent): void {
    if (event.key === 'Escape') {
      event.preventDefault();
      event.stopPropagation();
      this.closed.emit(true);
      return;
    }
    this.focus.trapTab(event, this.model !== null, this.dialog?.nativeElement);
  }

  /** A press anywhere outside closes it, leaving the focus to the press. */
  @HostListener('document:pointerdown', ['$event'])
  onDocumentPointerDown(event: PointerEvent): void {
    const target = event.target;
    if (target instanceof globalThis.Node && this.host.contains(target)) return;
    this.closed.emit(false);
  }

  changeChord(degree: ChordDegree): void {
    if (this.keys !== null) this.edit.emit(changeChord(this.keys, this.chordId, degree));
  }

  /** One step to the next whole beat in `dir`: 4 to 5 or 3, and 1.5 to 2 or 1. */
  step(dir: -1 | 1): void {
    const length = this.model?.lengthBeats;
    if (length === undefined) return;
    const next = dir > 0 ? Math.floor(length) + 1 : Math.ceil(length) - 1;
    this.edit.emit(setChordLength(this.chordId, next));
  }

  setLength(beats: number): void {
    this.edit.emit(setChordLength(this.chordId, beats));
  }

  remove(): void {
    this.edit.emit(deleteChord(this.chordId));
    this.closed.emit(true);
  }

  cancel(): void {
    this.closed.emit(true);
  }

  /** Whether the shorter step is at the shortest a chord can be, where a press changes nothing. */
  atShortest(): boolean {
    return (this.model?.lengthBeats ?? MIN_SLOT_BEATS) <= MIN_SLOT_BEATS;
  }

  trackByLabel(_index: number, preset: LengthPreset): string {
    return preset.label;
  }

  private modelOf(): PopoverModel | null {
    const doc = this.doc;
    const found = doc === null ? null : chordWithId(doc, this.chordId);
    if (doc === null || found === null) return null;

    const { key, timeSignature } = songMetaOf(doc);
    const scaleIntervals = this.keys?.chordScaleFor(key) ?? null;
    const naming: ChordNaming = { key, scaleIntervals, numerals: false };
    const label = chordLabelOf(found.attrs, naming);
    const harmony = found.attrs.harmony;
    const lengthBeats = found.attrs.lengthBeats;
    // A chord with no name - one detached from its degree, or in a key no chord can be named in - is headed `?`, as
    // the sheet prints it, and the field starts empty rather than from a `?` it would refuse.
    const numeral =
      harmony.kind === 'degree' && scaleIntervals !== null ? numeralOf(harmony.degree, scaleIntervals) : null;

    return {
      key,
      scaleIntervals,
      name: numeral === null ? '' : label.text,
      title: numeral === null ? label.text : `${label.text} · ${numeral}`,
      lengthBeats,
      lengthText: lengthTextOf(lengthBeats),
      presets: lengthPresetsOf(timeSignature)
    };
  }
}
```

```ts
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // The chord field and the chord popover
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  // Every opening and closing below is rendered at once (`detectChanges`) rather than on the next frame, which is when
  // this zoneless app would otherwise render a `markForCheck`. Typing outruns frames. A field opened by `[` must hold
  // the focus before the next key arrives, or `[Am]` typed in one go - the ChordPro way - puts its `Am` into the
  // lyrics; and a field closed by Enter must be gone before the next `[`, or that `[` finds the old field still on the
  // page, and `*ngIf` keeps it - with its old text, and without taking the focus again.

  /** `[` in the lyrics: the field opens under the caret, remembering where the chord goes. */
  openChordField(request: ChordFieldRequest): void {
    this.chordPopover = null;
    this.chordField = { pos: request.pos, ...this.anchorFor(request.coords) };
    this.changes.detectChanges();
  }

  /**
   * The field read a chord: it goes where `[` was pressed, voiced and a bar long, and the focus goes back after it. A

   */
  placeChord(degree: ChordDegree): void {
    const field = this.chordField;
    const doc = this.doc;
    if (field === null || doc === null) return;
    const { key, timeSignature } = songMetaOf(doc);
    this.chordField = null;
    this.sheet?.placeChord(field.pos, chordSlotOf(degree, key, this.keys.chordScaleFor(key), timeSignature));
    this.changes.detectChanges();
  }

  /** Escape in the field: nothing placed, and the focus back in the lyrics at the caret. */
  cancelChordField(): void {
    this.chordField = null;
    this.focusSheet();
    this.changes.detectChanges();
  }

   */
  onChordFieldFocusOut(event: FocusEvent, anchor: HTMLElement): void {
    const next = event.relatedTarget;
    if (next instanceof globalThis.Node && anchor.contains(next)) return;
    if (this.chordField === null) return;
    this.chordField = null;
    if (next === null) this.focusSheet();
    this.changes.detectChanges();
  }

  /** A chord's name clicked, or Enter on it: its popover, under the name. */
  openChordPopover(opening: ChordOpening): void {
    this.chordField = null;
    this.chordPopover = { id: opening.id, ...this.anchorFor(opening.anchor) };
    this.changes.detectChanges();
  }

  /** The popover is done; `giveFocusBack` when it closed by its own keys or buttons rather than a press elsewhere. */
  closeChordPopover(giveFocusBack: boolean): void {
    this.chordPopover = null;
    if (giveFocusBack) this.focusSheet();
    this.changes.detectChanges();
```

```ts
/**
 * What a chord's view asks of the sheet it is on: how to name it, where to list itself, and what to do when its name
 * is clicked or dragged.
 */
export interface ChordViewHost {
  /** The key, scale and names/numerals toggle a chord's name is worked out from, as they are now. */
  naming(): ChordNaming;
  /** Every chord view now on the sheet, so a key or toggle change can re-render them all. */
  readonly views: Set<ChordView>;
  /** The name was clicked - the chord is selected - and its popover is wanted, under `name`. */
  open(id: string, name: HTMLElement): void;
  /** A drag would drop the chord at `pos` now: show where, or nothing for null. */
  showDropCaret(pos: number | null): void;
  /** The chord `id` was dropped at `pos`, or where the sheet has no position (null). */
  drop(id: string, pos: number | null): void;
}

/** How far, in CSS pixels, a press on a name must move before it is a drag rather than a click. */
export const DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX = 4;

 * click and drag, and every pointer event. Not a drop of something else onto it, which is ProseMirror's to place in
 * the line.
 */
const OWN_EVENTS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  'mousedown',
  'mouseup',
  'click',
  'dblclick',
  'dragstart',
  'touchstart',
  'touchmove'
]);

  pointerId: number;
  x: number;
  y: number;
  /** Past the threshold: a drag. Short of it at `pointerup`: a click, which the `click` event that follows handles. */
  dragging: boolean;
}

 * names/numerals toggle - lives outside the atom: ProseMirror calls `update` only when the atom itself changes, so
 * the sheet calls `render` on every live view (`views`) when the key or the toggle does.

 * and Delete act on - and asks the host to open its popover. A **drag** - a press that moves `DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX` or more

 * chord there (`moveChordTo`). Its timing does not change: the word only places it (design decision 3).

 * the name even when the pointer leaves it or the window, and one code path serves a mouse, a pen and a finger. Where
 * it lands is the letter just under the moved name's left edge, which is where a name sits over its letter - so what
```

```ts

  destroy(): void {
    if (this.press?.dragging) this.host.showDropCaret(null);
    this.press = null;
    this.dom.removeEventListener('mousedown', this.onMouseDown);
    this.dom.removeEventListener('dragstart', this.onDragStart);
    this.dom.removeEventListener('click', this.onClick);
    this.name.removeEventListener('pointerdown', this.onPointerDown);
    this.name.removeEventListener('pointermove', this.onPointerMove);
    this.name.removeEventListener('pointerup', this.onPointerUp);
    this.name.removeEventListener('pointercancel', this.onPointerCancel);
    this.host.views.delete(this);
  }

  /** Cancelled, so neither the browser nor ProseMirror acts on a press that is the chord's (see the class comment). */
  private readonly onMouseDown = (event: MouseEvent): void => {
    event.preventDefault();
  };

  /** Cancelled: a chord moves by its own drag, never by the browser's (see the class comment). */
  private readonly onDragStart = (event: DragEvent): void => {
    event.preventDefault();
  };

  /** A click that was not the end of a drag: select the chord, put the focus in the sheet, and ask for its popover. */
  private readonly onClick = (): void => {
    if (this.swallowClick) {
      this.swallowClick = false;
      return;
    }
    const pos = this.getPos();
    if (pos === undefined) return;
    this.view.dispatch(this.view.state.tr.setSelection(NodeSelection.create(this.view.state.doc, pos)));
    this.view.focus();
    this.host.open(this.node.attrs['id'], this.name);
  };

  private readonly onPointerDown = (event: PointerEvent): void => {
    if (event.button !== 0 || !event.isPrimary) return;
    this.swallowClick = false;
    this.press = { pointerId: event.pointerId, x: event.clientX, y: event.clientY, dragging: false };
    this.name.setPointerCapture(event.pointerId);
  };

  private readonly onPointerMove = (event: PointerEvent): void => {
    const press = this.press;
    if (press === null || event.pointerId !== press.pointerId) return;
    const dx = event.clientX - press.x;
    const dy = event.clientY - press.y;
    if (!press.dragging) {
      if (Math.hypot(dx, dy) < DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX) return;
      press.dragging = true;
      this.dom.classList.add('is-dragging');
    }
    this.name.style.transform = `translate(${dx}px, ${dy}px)`;
    this.host.showDropCaret(this.dropPos());
  };

  /** The end of a press: a drag drops the chord; anything shorter is left to the `click` that follows. */
  private readonly onPointerUp = (event: PointerEvent): void => {
    const press = this.press;
    if (press === null || event.pointerId !== press.pointerId) return;
    this.press = null;
    if (!press.dragging) return;

    const pos = this.dropPos();
    this.endDrag();
    this.swallowClick = true;
    this.host.drop(this.node.attrs['id'], pos);
  };

  /** The browser took the pointer back - a touch turned into a scroll, a system gesture: the chord stays where it was. */
  private readonly onPointerCancel = (event: PointerEvent): void => {
    if (this.press === null || event.pointerId !== this.press.pointerId) return;
    const wasDragging = this.press.dragging;
    this.press = null;
    if (wasDragging) this.endDrag();
  };

  private endDrag(): void {
    this.name.style.transform = '';
    this.dom.classList.remove('is-dragging');
    this.host.showDropCaret(null);
  }

  /**
   * Where the chord would land now: the position at the letter under the moved name's left edge, half a name's height
   * below it - in the line of words the name sits over - or null where the sheet has no position at all.
   */
  private dropPos(): number | null {
    const box = this.name.getBoundingClientRect();
    return this.view.posAtCoords({ left: box.left + 1, top: box.bottom + box.height / 2 })?.pos ?? null;
  }
}
```

```ts
  private chordHost(view: EditorView): ChordViewHost {

      naming: () => this.naming,

  /** Enter on a selected chord: its popover, hung under its name - or under its place in the line, if no name is drawn. */
  private openChordAt(chord: ChordAt): void {
    const view = this.view;
    if (view === null) return;
    const dom = view.nodeDOM(chord.pos);
    const name = dom instanceof HTMLElement ? dom.querySelector('.song-chord-name') : null;
    const anchor = name === null ? view.coordsAtPos(chord.pos) : name.getBoundingClientRect();
    this.zone.run(() => this.chordOpened.emit({ id: chord.attrs.id, anchor: anchorOf(anchor) }));
  }

  /**
   * Shows the drop caret at `pos` while a chord is dragged, or hides it - and hides it too where the chord could not be
   * dropped, so the caret appears only where letting go would move the chord.
   *
   * Written to the element's style directly rather than bound: this runs on every pointer move, outside Angular's
   * zone, and a change detection pass per move would be all cost - the same reason the editor itself runs outside it.
   */
  private showDropCaret(view: EditorView, pos: number | null): void {
    const caret = this.dropCaret?.nativeElement;
    if (caret === undefined) return;
    const doc = view.state.doc;
    if (pos === null || pos > doc.content.size || doc.resolve(pos).parent.type.name !== 'lyricLine') {
      caret.hidden = true;
      return;
    }
    // The caret is positioned in the sheet's own box, which scrolls with the lyrics.
    const frame = caret.parentElement?.getBoundingClientRect();
    const at = view.coordsAtPos(pos);
    caret.style.left = `${at.left - (frame?.left ?? 0)}px`;
    caret.style.top = `${at.top - (frame?.top ?? 0)}px`;
    caret.style.height = `${at.bottom - at.top}px`;
    caret.hidden = false;
  }
```

```ts
/**
 * Makes the chord `id` a different chord - `degree`, in the song's key - and
 * voices it: the popover's chord field. Its id, its place and its length stay.
 *
 * It means what the progression page's `setSlotChord` means, by the same
 * parts (`ProgressionDegreeEditor.editDegree`), so a chord's ownership reads
 * the same on both pages:
 *
 * - **the pitches are handed back** (`reclaimPitches`) and the chord re-voiced
 *   from its new degree (`regenerateSlot`). A slot that owns its pitches - a
 *   voicing written in the progression page's roll and brought back by Open in
 *   Progression - keeps them through a key change, but a chord change restates
 *   the chord, and keeping them would leave the sheet printing the new name
 *   over the old chord's sound. Undo puts the owned voicing back.
 * - **a rhythm or a dynamic the slot owns is kept**: changing the chord says
 *   nothing about either.
 * - **the same degree is unchanged**, owned pitches and all: retyping a
 *   chord's own name in the field must not quietly throw away its voicing.
 *
 * A key whose scale cannot build chords is refused, since no degree can be
 * voiced in it; the field refuses every name there first.
 */
export function changeChord(keys: Pick<SongKeyRules, 'chordScaleFor'>, id: string, degree: ChordDegree): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const found = chordWithId(state.doc, id);
    if (found === null) return refused(GONE_CHORD);
    const key = songMetaOf(state.doc).key;
    const scaleIntervals = keys.chordScaleFor(key);
    if (scaleIntervals === null) return refused(NO_CHORDS_KEY);

    const harmony = found.attrs.harmony;
    if (harmony.kind === 'degree' && sameDegree(harmony.degree, degree)) return UNCHANGED;

    let slot: ChordSlot;
    try {
      const restated = normalizeChordSlot({ ...slotOf(found.attrs), harmony: { kind: 'degree', degree } });
      slot = regenerateSlot(reclaimPitches(restated), key, scaleIntervals);
    } catch (error) {
      return refused(messageOf(error));
    }
    return replaceChord(id, atomAttrsOf(slot))(state);
  };
}
```

```ts
}

const sectionHeadingRule = new InputRule(HEADING_RULE, (state, match, start, end) => {
  const $start = state.doc.resolve(start);
  const line = $start.parent;
  // Otherwise empty: the heading is the line's whole text - nothing before it,
  // nothing after the caret, no chord anywhere in it.
  if (!isLyricLine(line) || $start.parentOffset !== 0 || end !== $start.end()) return null;
  if (line.textContent.length !== line.content.size) return null;

  const heading = sectionHeadingOf(match[1]);
  if (heading === null) return null;
  return markSongCommand(startSection(state.tr.delete(start, end), start, heading));
});
```

```ts
}

/**
 * The chord atom `text` names in the song's key - as `[Am]` would place it - or
 * null when it names none there, or there are no rules to read it by. The key
 * and the meter are the document's, as the bracket closes.
 */
function bracketChordOf(text: string, doc: Node, keys: SongEditorOptions['keys']): ChordAtomAttrs | null {
  if (keys === undefined) return null;
  const { key, timeSignature } = songMetaOf(doc);
  const scaleIntervals = keys.chordScaleFor(key);
  const reading = chordFromText(text, key, scaleIntervals);
  return reading.kind === 'chord' ? chordSlotOf(reading.degree, key, scaleIntervals, timeSignature) : null;
}

/** `[Am]` or `[Chorus]` typed on an empty line: a chord at its start, or a section from it on. See the header. */
function bracketRule(keys: SongEditorOptions['keys']): InputRule {
  return new InputRule(HEADING_RULE, (state, match, start, end) => {
    const $start = state.doc.resolve(start);
    const line = $start.parent;
    // Otherwise empty: the text is the line's whole text - nothing before it,
    // nothing after the caret, no chord anywhere in it.
    if (!isLyricLine(line) || $start.parentOffset !== 0 || end !== $start.end()) return null;
    if (line.textContent.length !== line.content.size) return null;

    const chord = bracketChordOf(match[1], state.doc, keys);
    if (chord !== null) {
      const tr = state.tr.delete(start, end).insert(start, songSchema.nodes.chord.create(chord));
      return markSongCommand(tr.setSelection(TextSelection.create(tr.doc, start + 1)));
    }

    const heading = sectionHeadingOf(match[1]);
    if (heading === null) return null;
    return markSongCommand(startSection(state.tr.delete(start, end), start, heading));
  });
}
```

### Task E.1: The Chords tab

The side panel of Part 2, with its one tab: the key's triads and sevenths side by side, borrowed chords
and secondary dominants below, each with its name and numeral. A click places the chord at the sheet's caret - the
editor state's own selection, which survives the panel taking focus - or replaces the selected chord. The diatonic rows
come from `diatonicChordsOf`, extracted from the progression palette, so the two pages build the same chords.

```ts
import { ComponentFixture, TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { EditorState } from 'prosemirror-state';
import { createExtensions } from '../../../models/progression-normalize';
import type { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../../../models/progression.model';
import type { ChordAtomAttrs } from '../../../models/song.model';
import { MusicTheoryService } from '../../../services/music-theory.service';
import { ProgressionKeyContext } from '../../../services/progression-key-context';
import { SongEdit } from '../../../services/song-commands';

import { SongChordPanelComponent } from './song-chord-panel.component';

const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];
const FOUR_FOUR = { numerator: 4, denominator: 4, isCommon: true };

function degreeAt(degree: number, extent: 3 | 7 = 3): ChordDegree {
  return {
    degree,
    alter: 0,
    extent,
    quality: null,
    inversion: 0,
    suspension: 'none',
    extensions: createExtensions(),
    octave: 0
  };
}

    fixture.componentRef.setInput('doc', doc);
    fixture.componentRef.setInput('keys', keys);
    if (inputs.numerals !== undefined) fixture.componentRef.setInput('numerals', inputs.numerals);

  }

  /** A chord atom's attributes for `degree`, as the sheet hands over the selected one. */

  it('shows the song’s key between its transpose arrows', () => {

    expect(lines('secondary', 'role')).toEqual(['V/ii', 'V/iii', 'V/IV', 'V/V', 'V/vi']);
    expect(cells('triads')[5].getAttribute('aria-label')).toBe('A minor');

  it('puts numerals first when the sheet shows numerals', () => {

    host.querySelector<HTMLButtonElement>('.panel-transpose-down')?.click();

    const state = EditorState.create({ doc });
    const tonicAfter = (edit: SongEdit): number | null => {
      const outcome = edit(state);
      return outcome.kind === 'edit' ? songMetaOf(outcome.tr.doc).key.tonic : null;
    };
    expect(edits.map(tonicAfter)).toEqual([1, 11]);
  });

  it('follows the song into a new key', () => {
    show(createSongContent({ key: C_MAJOR }));
    fixture.componentRef.setInput('doc', createSongContent({ key: { tonic: 9, scaleId: 'aeolian', preferSharps: true } }));
    fixture.detectChanges();

    expect(text(host.querySelector('.panel-key-name'))).toBe('A Aeolian (Natural Minor)');
    expect(lines('triads', 'primary')).toEqual(['Am', 'B°', 'C', 'Dm', 'Em', 'F', 'G']);
  });

  it('marks the cell of the chord selected on the sheet, and says a click will replace it', () => {
    show(createSongContent({ key: C_MAJOR }));
    expect(text(host.querySelector('.panel-hint'))).toBe('Click a chord to place it at the caret.');
    expect(host.querySelectorAll('.cell.on').length).toBe(0);

    fixture.componentRef.setInput('selected', selectedAtom(degreeAt(5)));
    fixture.detectChanges();

    const marked = Array.from(host.querySelectorAll('.cell.on'));
    expect(marked).toEqual([cells('triads')[5]]);
    expect(cells('triads')[5].getAttribute('aria-current')).toBe('true');
    expect(cells('triads')[4].hasAttribute('aria-current')).toBeFalse();
    expect(text(host.querySelector('.panel-hint'))).toBe('Click a chord to replace the one selected on the sheet.');
  });

  it('says why a key that cannot build chords has none, in place of the grid', () => {
    show(createSongContent({ key: { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'majorPentatonic', preferSharps: true } }));
    expect(text(host.querySelector('.panel-refusal'))).toBe(
      "This key's scale can't build chords; choose a seven-note scale for the song."
    );
    expect(host.querySelectorAll('.cell').length).toBe(0);
  });
});
```

```ts
import { Component } from '@angular/core';

import { RouterTestingHarness } from '@angular/router/testing';
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { EditorState, NodeSelection, TextSelection } from 'prosemirror-state';
import { createExtensions } from '../../../models/progression-normalize';
import { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../../../models/progression.model';
import { SongDoc } from '../../../models/song.model';
import { deletedDatabase } from '../../../services/indexed-db.spec-helper';
import { AutosaveClock } from '../../../services/song-autosave';
import { chordSlotOf } from '../../../services/song-document';
import { SONG_LIBRARY_DB, SongLibraryService } from '../../../services/song-library.service';
import { songSchema } from '../../../services/song-schema';
import { SONG_PREFERENCES_STORAGE, SongSheetPreferencesService } from '../../../services/song-sheet-preferences.service';
import { SongSheetComponent } from '../song-sheet/song-sheet.component';
import { SONG_AUTOSAVE_CLOCK, SongEditorComponent } from './song-editor.component';

const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];
const FOUR_FOUR = { numerator: 4, denominator: 4, isCommon: true };

function chord(degree: number): Node {
  const at: ChordDegree = {
    degree,
    alter: 0,
    extent: 3,
    quality: null,
    inversion: 0,
    suspension: 'none',
    extensions: createExtensions(),
    octave: 0
  };
  return songSchema.node('chord', chordSlotOf(at, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, FOUR_FOUR));
}

/** "Last Dance" in C major: C over "Got" and Am over "thinking". */
function lastDance(): Node {
  return songSchema.node(
    'doc',
    { title: 'Last Dance', artist: 'The Band', key: C_MAJOR, tempo: 100, timeSignature: FOUR_FOUR },
    [
      songSchema.node('section', { id: crypto.randomUUID(), label: 'Verse 1', kind: 'verse' }, [
        songSchema.node('lyricLine', null, [chord(0), songSchema.text('Got me '), chord(5), songSchema.text('thinking')])
      ])
    ]
  );
}

/** A clock whose timers never come due: nothing autosaves behind a spec's back, and the page's destroy still saves. */
class StoppedClock implements AutosaveClock {
  now(): number {
    return Date.now();
  }
  setTimeout(): unknown {
    return 0;
  }
  clearTimeout(): void {
    return;
  }
}

@Component({ standalone: true, template: '<p class="library-stand-in">Library</p>' })

      press(cell('triads', 1));

      expect(names()).toEqual(['C', 'Dm']);
      const selection = editorState().selection;
      expect(selection instanceof NodeSelection && selection.from).toBe(10);
      expect(document.activeElement).toBe(editor());
      expect(Array.from(host().querySelectorAll('.cell.on'))).toEqual([cell('triads', 1)]);
    });

    it('says why nothing was placed when the lyrics have not had a caret yet', async () => {
      await openLastDance();

      press(cell('triads', 3));

      expect(names()).toEqual(['C', 'Am']);
      expect(messages()).toBe('Put the caret in a line of lyrics to add a chord there.');
      expect(document.activeElement).not.toBe(editor());
    });
  });
});
```

```ts
import { EditorState } from 'prosemirror-state';
import { chordLabelOf } from '../components/songs/song-sheet/chord-view';
import { createExtensions } from '../models/progression-normalize';
import type { ChordAtomAttrs } from '../models/song.model';
import type { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../models/progression.model';
import { MusicTheoryService } from './music-theory.service';
import { ProgressionKeyContext } from './progression-key-context';
import { chordVocabulary } from './progression-vocabulary';
import { chordFromText } from './song-chord-parse';
import { insertChord } from './song-commands';
import { chordSlotOf, createSongContent } from './song-document';
import { SongPaletteOption, SongPaletteRows, isSameChord, songPaletteOf } from './song-palette';

const IONIAN = [0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11];
const AEOLIAN = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10];
const DORIAN = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 10];
const HARMONIC_MINOR = [0, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 11];
const MAJOR_PENTATONIC = [0, 2, 4, 7, 9];
const FOUR_FOUR = { numerator: 4, denominator: 4, isCommon: true };

const C_MAJOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 0, scaleId: 'ionian', preferSharps: true };
const A_MINOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 9, scaleId: 'aeolian', preferSharps: true };
const D_DORIAN: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 2, scaleId: 'dorian', preferSharps: false };
const A_HARMONIC_MINOR: ProgressionKey = { tonic: 9, scaleId: 'harmonicMinor', preferSharps: true };

/** The four rows of a key that can build chords; a refusal fails the spec. */
function rowsOf(key: ProgressionKey, scaleIntervals: readonly number[]): SongPaletteRows {
  const palette = songPaletteOf(key, scaleIntervals);
  if (palette.kind !== 'rows') throw new Error(`Refused: ${palette.reason}`);
  return palette.rows;
}

const names = (options: readonly SongPaletteOption[]): string[] => options.map(option => option.name);
const numerals = (options: readonly SongPaletteOption[]): string[] => options.map(option => option.numeral);

function degreeOf(degree: number, extent: 3 | 7 = 3, inversion = 0): ChordDegree {
  return {
    degree,
    alter: 0,
    extent,
    quality: null,
    inversion,
    suspension: 'none',
    extensions: createExtensions(),
    octave: 0
  };
}

/**
 * The Chords tab's four rows: the key's own triads and sevenths, built here, and the borrowed chords and secondary
 * dominants the progression palette's vocabulary offers - every one written as the sheet writes it.
 */
describe('songPaletteOf', () => {
  describe('the diatonic rows', () => {
    it('gives C ionian its seven triads and seven sevenths', () => {
      const rows = rowsOf(C_MAJOR, IONIAN);

      expect(numerals(rows.triads)).toEqual(['I', 'ii', 'iii', 'IV', 'V', 'vi', 'vii°']);
      expect(names(rows.triads)).toEqual(['C', 'Dm', 'Em', 'F', 'G', 'Am', 'B°']);
      expect(numerals(rows.sevenths)).toEqual(['Imaj7', 'ii7', 'iii7', 'IVmaj7', 'V7', 'vi7', 'viiø7']);
      expect(names(rows.sevenths)).toEqual(['Cmaj7', 'Dm7', 'Em7', 'Fmaj7', 'G7', 'Am7', 'Bø7']);
    });

    it('numbers A aeolian from its own tonic', () => {
      const rows = rowsOf(A_MINOR, AEOLIAN);

      expect(numerals(rows.triads)).toEqual(['i', 'ii°', 'III', 'iv', 'v', 'VI', 'VII']);
      expect(names(rows.triads)).toEqual(['Am', 'B°', 'C', 'Dm', 'Em', 'F', 'G']);
      expect(names(rows.sevenths)).toEqual(['Am7', 'Bø7', 'Cmaj7', 'Dm7', 'Em7', 'Fmaj7', 'G7']);
    });

    it('builds D dorian’s chords from its own scale, not the major scale’s', () => {
      const rows = rowsOf(D_DORIAN, DORIAN);

      expect(numerals(rows.triads)).toEqual(['i', 'ii', 'III', 'IV', 'v', 'vi°', 'VII']);
      expect(names(rows.triads)).toEqual(['Dm', 'Em', 'F', 'G', 'Am', 'B°', 'C']);
      expect(names(rows.sevenths)).toEqual(['Dm7', 'Em7', 'Fmaj7', 'G7', 'Am7', 'Bø7', 'Cmaj7']);
    });

    it('stacks harmonic minor’s raised seventh into its chords: the major V7 and the leading-tone vii°7', () => {
      const rows = rowsOf(A_HARMONIC_MINOR, HARMONIC_MINOR);

      expect(names(rows.triads)).toEqual(['Am', 'B°', 'C+', 'Dm', 'E', 'F', 'G#°']);
      expect(names(rows.sevenths)).toEqual(['AmMaj7', 'Bø7', 'C+maj7', 'Dm7', 'E7', 'Fmaj7', 'G#°7']);
      expect(numerals(rows.sevenths)[4]).toBe('V7');
      expect(numerals(rows.sevenths)[6]).toBe('vii°7');
    });

    it('places each diatonic chord as the key gives it: degree by degree, no override, at its row’s height', () => {
      const rows = rowsOf(C_MAJOR, IONIAN);

      expect(rows.triads.map(option => option.degree)).toEqual([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6].map(degree => degreeOf(degree)));
      expect(rows.sevenths.map(option => option.degree)).toEqual([0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6].map(degree => degreeOf(degree, 7)));
    });

    it('says each chord for assistive technology by its name, not its numeral', () => {
      const rows = rowsOf(C_MAJOR, IONIAN);
      expect(rows.triads[5].spoken).toBe('A minor');
      expect(rows.sevenths[6].spoken).toBe('B half diminished seventh');
    });
  });

  describe('the borrowed and secondary rows', () => {
    it('are the vocabulary’s, chord for chord and in its order', () => {
      for (const [key, scale] of [
        [C_MAJOR, IONIAN],
        [A_MINOR, AEOLIAN],
        [D_DORIAN, DORIAN]
      ] as const) {
        const rows = rowsOf(key, scale);
        const vocabulary = chordVocabulary(key, scale, null);
        const shape = (degree: ChordDegree): unknown => [degree.degree, degree.alter, degree.quality, degree.extent];

        expect(rows.borrowed.map(option => shape(option.degree))).toEqual(
          vocabulary.borrowed.map(option => [option.degree, option.alter, option.quality, option.extent])
        );
        expect(rows.secondary.map(option => shape(option.degree))).toEqual(
          vocabulary.secondary.map(option => [option.degree, option.alter, option.quality, option.extent])
        );
      }
    });

    it('names them the sheet’s way, and keeps the secondary dominants’ slash numerals as their role', () => {
      const rows = rowsOf(C_MAJOR, IONIAN);

      expect(names(rows.borrowed)).toEqual(['Db', 'Eb', 'Fm', 'Ab', 'Bb']);
      expect(numerals(rows.borrowed)).toEqual(['♭II', '♭III', 'iv', '♭VI', '♭VII']);
      expect(rows.borrowed.map(option => option.role)).toEqual([null, null, null, null, null]);

      expect(names(rows.secondary)).toEqual(['A7', 'B7', 'C7', 'D7', 'E7']);
      expect(rows.secondary.map(option => option.role)).toEqual(['V/ii', 'V/iii', 'V/IV', 'V/V', 'V/vi']);
      // The numeral is the one the sheet prints for the chord once placed: its place in the key.
      expect(numerals(rows.secondary)).toEqual(['VI7', 'VII7', 'I7', 'II7', 'III7']);
      expect(rows.secondary[0].spoken).toBe('A dominant seventh, leading to D minor');
    });

    it('offers a minor key its major dominant and leading-tone triad as borrowed chords', () => {
      expect(names(rowsOf(A_MINOR, AEOLIAN).borrowed)).toEqual(['Bb', 'E', 'G#°']);
    });
  });

  it('refuses a key whose scale cannot build chords, with the reason', () => {
    const pentatonic = songPaletteOf({ tonic: 0, scaleId: 'majorPentatonic', preferSharps: true }, MAJOR_PENTATONIC);
    const unknown = songPaletteOf({ tonic: 0, scaleId: 'nothing', preferSharps: true }, null);

    for (const palette of [pentatonic, unknown]) {
      expect(palette).toEqual({
        kind: 'refused',
        reason: "This key's scale can't build chords; choose a seven-note scale for the song."
      });
    }
  });

  it('gives options the sheet places and prints as the panel writes them, in every key a song can be in', () => {
    const keys = new ProgressionKeyContext(new MusicTheoryService());
    const scales = new MusicTheoryService()
      .getScaleCategories()
      .flatMap(category => category.scales)
      .filter(scale => keys.chordScale(scale) !== null);
    expect(scales.length).toBeGreaterThan(10);

    const problems: string[] = [];
    for (const scale of scales) {
      for (const [tonic, preferSharps] of [
        [0, true],
        [3, false],
        [6, true],
        [10, false]
      ] as const) {
        const key: ProgressionKey = { tonic, scaleId: scale.id, preferSharps };
        const rows = rowsOf(key, scale.intervals);
        const state = EditorState.create({ doc: createSongContent({ key }) });

        for (const option of [...rows.triads, ...rows.sevenths, ...rows.borrowed, ...rows.secondary]) {
          const outcome = insertChord(chordSlotOf(option.degree, key, scale.intervals, FOUR_FOUR))(state);
          if (outcome.kind !== 'edit') {
            problems.push(`${scale.id} ${tonic} ${option.name}: ${outcome.kind}`);
            continue;
          }
          // The new song's caret is in its first line, at 2: the atom is there.
          const attrs = outcome.tr.doc.nodeAt(2)?.attrs as ChordAtomAttrs;
          const named = chordLabelOf(attrs, { key, scaleIntervals: scale.intervals, numerals: false });
          const numbered = chordLabelOf(attrs, { key, scaleIntervals: scale.intervals, numerals: true });
          if (named.text !== option.name || numbered.text !== option.numeral) {
            problems.push(`${scale.id} ${tonic}: ${option.name} ${option.numeral} printed ${named.text} ${numbered.text}`);
          }
          if (named.spoken !== `chord ${option.spoken.split(', ')[0]}`) {
            problems.push(`${scale.id} ${tonic}: ${option.spoken} said as ${named.spoken}`);
          }
        }
      }
    }
    expect(problems).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/** Which cell the chord selected on the sheet is: the chord it builds, wherever it came from. */
describe('isSameChord', () => {
  let rows: SongPaletteRows;

  beforeEach(() => {
    rows = rowsOf(C_MAJOR, IONIAN);
  });

  it('finds a placed chord’s own cell, and no other diatonic cell', () => {
    const placed = chordSlotOf(rows.triads[5].degree, C_MAJOR, IONIAN, FOUR_FOUR).harmony;
    if (placed.kind !== 'degree') throw new Error('Placed a literal');
    const cells = [...rows.triads, ...rows.sevenths, ...rows.borrowed, ...rows.secondary];

    expect(cells.filter(option => isSameChord(option.degree, placed.degree, IONIAN)).map(option => option.name)).toEqual([
      'Am'
    ]);
  });

  it('knows a typed chord, and an inverted one, by the chord it builds', () => {
    const typed = chordFromText('Bb', C_MAJOR, IONIAN);
    if (typed.kind !== 'chord') throw new Error(typed.reason);

    expect(isSameChord(rows.borrowed[4].degree, typed.degree, IONIAN)).toBeTrue();
    expect(isSameChord(rows.triads[0].degree, degreeOf(0, 3, 1), IONIAN)).toBeTrue();
  });

  it('tells a triad from its seventh', () => {
    expect(isSameChord(rows.triads[4].degree, degreeOf(4, 7), IONIAN)).toBeFalse();
    expect(isSameChord(rows.sevenths[4].degree, degreeOf(4, 7), IONIAN)).toBeTrue();
  });
});
```

```ts
 * disagreeing with the thing it labelled before the user had touched anything.
 * The complexity control below it is how a chord gets taller, after it is placed.
 *
 * The seven are built by `diatonicChordsOf` at this height - unaltered and with
```

```ts
/**
 * The degree a palette button stands for, as `chordRootName` wants it.
 *
 * It is `createDegreeSlot`'s degree at the palette's own extent - the slot the
 * button appends - so building it here rather than passing the index alone is
 * what makes the label and the appended chord one description. `alter: 0` is
 * copied from that factory rather than assumed: it is the field M2's borrowed
 * chords move, and the day it moves the palette follows through the shared
 * function instead of standing still.
 *
 * `quality: null` is copied from it for the same reason, and it used to be the
 * *derived* label instead - which was the palette writing a name into a field
 * that means "override", one call site over from the `regenerateSlot` that did
 * the same thing everywhere else. The root arithmetic reads neither, so
 * nothing moved; what changed is that the two descriptions now match.
 */
export function paletteDegree(degree: number): ChordDegree {
  return {
    degree,
    alter: 0,
    extent: PALETTE_EXTENT,
    quality: null,
    inversion: 0,
    suspension: 'none',
    extensions: createExtensions(),
    octave: 0
  };
}
```

```ts
  }

  private buildChords(key: ProgressionKey, intervals: readonly number[]): PaletteChord[] {
    return [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6].map(degree => {
      // The whole identity rather than a bare quality, which is what the three
      // renderers take since M3 Task 5 - and it is the same identity the strip
      // card and the fretboard read, so a diatonic button here cannot come to a
      // different conclusion about a chord from the card it will make. At this
      // row's extent nothing composes: a triad with no suspension and no pinned
      // extension renders exactly what `degreeQuality` rendered before.
      const chord = effectiveChord(intervals, paletteDegree(degree));
      // The shared arithmetic rather than a local `(tonic + interval) % 12`,
      // which is what this was and which agrees with it only while `alter` is
      // pinned at zero. The strip card and the fretboard highlight both call
      // this function; a palette doing its own sum is the one label that would
      // not follow when M2 lets a degree be altered - and it would also not
      // fold a negative sum back into range.
      //
      // Spelled on this degree's own letter rather than from the two chromatic
      // tables, which is what makes F locrian's third degree an `Ab` here
      // instead of the `G♯` a six-sharp signature gave it - and what keeps this
      // row agreeing with the borrowed row beside it, where a lowered root now
      // has a letter no preference could have chosen.
      const root = chordRootName(key, intervals, paletteDegree(degree));

      return {
        degree,
        numeral: romanNumeral(degree, PALETTE_ALTER, chord),
        name: chordName(root, chord),
        // The numeral is dropped from the spoken label rather than translated:
        // read aloud it is a string of letters ("vee eye eye") and the one fact
        // it carries beyond the position - the quality - is already in the
        // spoken name. The position is given as the degree instead.
        label: `Add ${spokenChordName(root, chord)}, degree ${degree + 1}`,
        isTonic: degree === 0
      };
    });
  }
```

```ts
  }

  /**
   * The seven buttons: the key's own triads, as `diatonicChordsOf` builds them.
   *
   * Built there rather than here since the song sheet's Chords tab needs the
   * same seven, and its sevenths, so the two cannot disagree about a key's
   * chords. What the vocabulary decides - the root on the degree's own letter
   * through `chordRootName`, the identity the strip card and the fretboard read
   * through `effectiveChord` - is argued there; what is the palette's is the
   * height (`PALETTE_EXTENT`, what `createDegreeSlot` appends) and the label.
   */
  private buildChords(key: ProgressionKey, intervals: readonly number[]): PaletteChord[] {
    return diatonicChordsOf(key, intervals, PALETTE_EXTENT).map(({ degree: { degree }, numeral, name, spoken }) => ({
      degree,
      numeral,
      name,
      // The numeral is dropped from the spoken label rather than translated:
      // read aloud it is a string of letters ("vee eye eye") and the one fact
      // it carries beyond the position - the quality - is already in the
      // spoken name. The position is given as the degree instead.
      label: `Add ${spoken}, degree ${degree + 1}`,
      isTonic: degree === 0
    }));
  }
```

```scss
// The song pages' tokens, each with its own value as the fallback so the panel renders the same outside the page.
:host {
  --panel-text: var(--songs-text, #ecf0f1);
  --panel-text-dim: var(--songs-text-dim, #adbcc8);
  --panel-accent: var(--songs-accent, #3498db);
  --panel-border: var(--songs-border, #465666);

  display: block;
  color: var(--panel-text);
  font-family: system-ui, sans-serif;
}

.chord-panel {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 0.75rem;
  padding: 0.75rem;
}

// ↑ C Ionian (Major) ↓, as the design's sketch has it.
.panel-key {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  gap: 0.5rem;
}

.panel-key-name {
  font-weight: 600;
  text-align: center;
}

.panel-hint,
.panel-refusal {
  margin: 0;
  color: var(--panel-text-dim);
  font-size: 0.8rem;
}

.panel-refusal {
  font-size: 0.9rem;
}

// Triads and sevenths side by side, each a column of seven, so a degree's triad sits beside its seventh.
.diatonic {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr));
  gap: 0.75rem;

  .cells {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);
  }
}

.chromatic {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  gap: 0.75rem;

  .cells {
    grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(3.75rem, 1fr));
  }
}

.chord-group {
  min-width: 0;
}

.group-title {
  margin: 0 0 0.3rem;
  color: var(--panel-text-dim);
  font-size: 0.75rem;
  font-weight: 600;
  letter-spacing: 0.04em;
  text-transform: uppercase;
}

.cells {
  display: grid;
  gap: 0.15rem;
}

// The flat tool style: no chrome until hovered, colour only on the selection (`.on`).
.tool {
  background: transparent;
  border: 0;
  border-radius: 3px;
  color: var(--panel-text);
  font: inherit;
  cursor: pointer;
  transition: background-color 90ms ease-out;

  &:hover:not(.on) {
    background-color: rgb(255 255 255 / 10%);
  }

  &:active {
    background-color: rgb(255 255 255 / 16%);
  }

  &.on {
    background-color: var(--panel-accent);
    color: #fff;
  }

  &:focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid var(--panel-text);
    outline-offset: -2px;
  }
}

.panel-transpose-up,
.panel-transpose-down {
  min-width: 2rem;
  padding: 0.3rem 0.5rem;
}

.cell {
  display: flex;
  flex-direction: column;
  align-items: center;
  min-width: 0;
  padding: 0.3rem 0.25rem;
  line-height: 1.2;
}

.cell-primary {
  font-size: 0.95rem;
  font-weight: 600;
}

.cell-secondary,
.cell-role {
  color: var(--panel-text-dim);
  font-size: 0.75rem;
}

// Numerals are set in the toolbar's I-IV face wherever they appear; the role is always a numeral.
.cell-role {
  font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif;
}

.cell.on .cell-secondary,
.cell.on .cell-role {
  color: rgb(255 255 255 / 85%);
}

// Under the sheet (the page's narrow layout, at the same width): there is room across and little down, so each group
// is a row, triads above sevenths with a degree's two chords in one column.
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .diatonic {
    grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr);

    .cells {
      grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr));
    }
  }

  .cell-primary {
    font-size: 0.85rem;
  }
}
```

```ts
import { CommonModule } from '@angular/common';
import {
  ChangeDetectionStrategy,
  Component,
  EventEmitter,
  Input,
  OnChanges,
  Output,
  SimpleChanges
} from '@angular/core';
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import type { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../../../models/progression.model';
import type { ChordAtomAttrs } from '../../../models/song.model';
import { keyNameOf } from '../../../services/song-chord-names';
import { SongEdit, SongKeyRules, transposeSong } from '../../../services/song-commands';
import { songMetaOf } from '../../../services/song-document';
import { SongPalette, SongPaletteOption, isSameChord, songPaletteOf } from '../../../services/song-palette';

/** The four groups, by the row of the palette each draws. */
export type ChordGroupId = 'triads' | 'sevenths' | 'borrowed' | 'secondary';

/** One cell: the chord it places, its two lines in the order the sheet's toggle asks, and whether it is selected. */
export interface ChordCell {
  readonly option: SongPaletteOption;
  /** What the sheet shows now - the name, or with numerals on, the numeral. */
  readonly primary: string;
  /** The other of the two, smaller, underneath. */
  readonly secondary: string;
  /** The chord selected on the sheet builds this cell's chord. */
  readonly current: boolean;
}

export interface ChordGroup {
  readonly id: ChordGroupId;
  readonly title: string;
  /** The id of its heading, which labels the group. */
  readonly headingId: string;
  readonly cells: readonly ChordCell[];
}

const GROUP_TITLES: Readonly<Record<ChordGroupId, string>> = {
  triads: 'Triads',
  sevenths: 'Sevenths',
  borrowed: 'Borrowed',
  secondary: 'Secondary dominants'
};

const PLACE_HINT = 'Click a chord to place it at the caret.';
const REPLACE_HINT = 'Click a chord to replace the one selected on the sheet.';

/**
 * The Chords tab (design Part 2): the song's key between Transpose ↑↓, and the key's chords in four groups - triads
 * and sevenths side by side, borrowed chords and secondary dominants below - each cell its chord's name and numeral.
 *
 * **It never changes the song itself**, as the toolbar does not: Transpose emits a `SongEdit` (`edit`) the page runs
 * on the sheet, and a cell emits the degree it stands for (`chosen`) and nothing more. Whether that chord is placed
 * at the caret or replaces the selected chord is the page's to decide, since it needs the sheet's caret and selection
 * and this panel is outside the sheet; the panel only says which will happen (`hint`), from the selected chord it is
 * handed.
 *
 * **What the cells say is the sheet's.** The rows are `songPaletteOf`'s, named and numbered by the functions the sheet
 * prints a chord with, so a cell and the chord it places read the same.
 *
 * - **Names or numerals first, per the sheet's I-IV toggle**, with the other underneath, smaller. The first and larger
 *   line is the one the eye scans for, and it should be the token the user is reading over the words: someone in
 *   numerals finds `vi`, not `Am`, and the name is still there under it. The order moves only when the user flips the
 *   toggle, which is a deliberate act, not under the pointer.
 * - **A secondary dominant also shows its role**, `V/ii`, under the two: the sheet numbers it by its place in the key
 *   (`VI7`), because an atom does not store the chord it leads to, and the role is the reason it is in this row.
 *
 * **Colour only on the selection** (the flat tool style): the cell whose chord is selected on the sheet is the one
 * coloured, and carries `aria-current`; nothing else has chrome until hovered.
 *
 * **Plain buttons, one tab stop each, not a roving tabindex.** Every cell is a command of its own, as the progression
 * palette's buttons are, and a native button needs no script to be pressed, found by a screen reader's button list,
 * or reached by voice control. A roving tabindex would save Tab presses, but its arrow keys would have to mean a
 * direction in a grid that reflows - two columns of seven beside the sheet, rows of cells under it on a narrow
 * screen - and an arrow that goes somewhere different at each width is worse than a longer Tab. The panel is the last
 * thing on the page, so its stops come after everything else.
 */
@Component({
  selector: 'app-song-chord-panel',
  standalone: true,
  imports: [CommonModule],
  changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush,
  templateUrl: './song-chord-panel.component.html',
  styleUrls: ['./song-chord-panel.component.scss']
})
export class SongChordPanelComponent implements OnChanges {
  /** The song now: its key decides the chords. */
  @Input() doc: Node | null = null;
  @Input() keys: SongKeyRules | null = null;
  /** Whether the sheet shows numerals, so the cells put them first. */
  @Input() numerals = false;
  /** The chord selected on the sheet, which a click replaces, or null. */
  @Input() selected: ChordAtomAttrs | null = null;

  /** Transpose ↑↓, for the page to run on the sheet. */
  @Output() readonly edit = new EventEmitter<SongEdit>();
  /** A cell was clicked: the chord it places. */
  @Output() readonly chosen = new EventEmitter<ChordDegree>();

  /** `C Ionian (Major)`, as the library's cards and the progression page write a key. */
  keyName = '';
  /** Why the key has no chords to offer, in place of the groups; null when it has. */
  refusal: string | null = null;
  /** Triads and sevenths, side by side when there is room. */
  diatonic: readonly ChordGroup[] = [];
  /** Borrowed chords and secondary dominants, below; a group with nothing to offer is left out. */
  chromatic: readonly ChordGroup[] = [];
  hint = PLACE_HINT;

  private key: ProgressionKey | null = null;
  private scaleIntervals: readonly number[] | null = null;
  private palette: SongPalette | null = null;

  ngOnChanges(changes: SimpleChanges): void {
    const doc = this.doc;
    const keys = this.keys;
    if (doc === null || keys === null) return;

    // The song's document is new on every keystroke; its key is the same object until the key changes.
    const key = songMetaOf(doc).key;
    const rekeyed = key !== this.key || changes['keys'] !== undefined;
    if (rekeyed) {
      this.key = key;
      this.scaleIntervals = keys.chordScaleFor(key);
      this.palette = songPaletteOf(key, this.scaleIntervals);
      this.keyName = keyNameOf(key, keys.findScale(key.scaleId));
    }
    if (rekeyed || changes['numerals'] !== undefined || changes['selected'] !== undefined) this.layOut();
  }

  /** A cell clicked: its chord, for the page to place or put in place of the selected one. */
  choose(cell: ChordCell): void {
    this.chosen.emit(cell.option.degree);
  }

  /** ↑ or ↓: the song a semitone up or down, as the toolbar's Transpose. */
  transpose(delta: -1 | 1): void {
    if (this.keys !== null) this.edit.emit(transposeSong(this.keys, delta));
  }

  trackByGroup(_index: number, group: ChordGroup): ChordGroupId {
    return group.id;
  }

  /** A cell by its chord's name, which no two cells in one group share. */
  trackByCell(_index: number, cell: ChordCell): string {
    return cell.option.name;
  }

  private layOut(): void {
    const palette = this.palette;
    const scaleIntervals = this.scaleIntervals;
    this.hint = this.selected === null ? PLACE_HINT : REPLACE_HINT;
    if (palette === null || palette.kind === 'refused' || scaleIntervals === null) {
      this.refusal = palette?.kind === 'refused' ? palette.reason : null;
      this.diatonic = [];
      this.chromatic = [];
      return;
    }

    const harmony = this.selected?.harmony;
    const selected = harmony?.kind === 'degree' ? harmony.degree : null;
    const group = (id: ChordGroupId, options: readonly SongPaletteOption[]): ChordGroup => ({
      id,
      title: GROUP_TITLES[id],
      headingId: `song-chord-panel-${id}`,
      cells: options.map(option => ({
        option,
        primary: this.numerals ? option.numeral : option.name,
        secondary: this.numerals ? option.name : option.numeral,
        current: selected !== null && isSameChord(option.degree, selected, scaleIntervals)
      }))
    });

    const { triads, sevenths, borrowed, secondary } = palette.rows;
    this.refusal = null;
    this.diatonic = [group('triads', triads), group('sevenths', sevenths)];
    this.chromatic = [group('borrowed', borrowed), group('secondary', secondary)].filter(entry => entry.cells.length > 0);
  }
}
```

```scss
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: 0.25rem;
  padding: 0.3rem 0.5rem;
  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--songs-border);

.panel-tabs {
  display: flex;
  flex: 1;
  gap: 0.25rem;
}

// A selected tab is marked by a line under it rather than a fill: the flat style keeps colour for a selection, and a

.panel-tab {
  font-weight: 600;

  &.selected {
    box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 var(--songs-accent);

.panel-toggle {
  display: inline-flex;

}

// The selected tab's panel scrolls on its own, so the tab strip and the toggle stay in reach.
.panel-body {
  flex: 1;
  min-height: 0;
  overflow-y: auto;
```

```ts
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // The side panel
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  /** Hide panel / Show panel, remembered for this viewer. */
  togglePanel(): void {
    this.preferencesService.setPanelOpen(!this.preferences.panelOpen);
  }

  selectTab(id: PanelTabId): void {
    this.selectedTab = id;
  }

  /**
   * The tab strip's keys, by the ARIA tabs pattern: ←/→ to the previous and next tab, round the ends, and Home and
   * End to the first and last, each selecting the tab it lands on and taking the focus there. With one tab every key
   * lands where it started.
   */
  onTabKeydown(event: KeyboardEvent, index: number): void {
    const count = this.panelTabs.length;
    const moves: Record<string, number> = { ArrowLeft: index - 1, ArrowRight: index + 1, Home: 0, End: count - 1 };
    const target = moves[event.key];
    if (target === undefined) return;
    event.preventDefault();
    const next = (target + count) % count;
    this.selectTab(this.panelTabs[next].id);
    this.panelTabElements?.get(next)?.nativeElement.focus();
  }

  /**
   * A chord clicked in the Chords tab: in place of the chord selected on the sheet, or at the caret the lyrics last had
   * (see the class comment). `changeChord` keeps the selected chord's id, place and length, and leaves it selected, so
   * the cell it now matches is marked and another click swaps it again.
   */
  placePaletteChord(degree: ChordDegree): void {
    const sheet = this.sheet;
    const doc = this.doc;
    if (sheet === undefined || doc === null) return;

    const selected = sheet.selectedChord();
    if (selected !== null) {
      sheet.run(changeChord(this.keys, selected.attrs.id, degree));
      sheet.focus();
      return;
    }

    const { key, timeSignature } = songMetaOf(doc);
    const attrs = chordSlotOf(degree, key, this.keys.chordScaleFor(key), timeSignature);
    // No caret yet is handed on as a place no line can hold, so the refusal and its words are `insertChord`'s.
    if (sheet.run(insertChord(attrs, sheet.lastCaret() ?? Number.NaN))) sheet.focus();
  }
```

```ts
      if (state.doc !== before.doc) this.docChanged.emit(state.doc);
      if (historyMoved) this.historyChanged.emit(history);
      if (selectionMoved) this.selectedChordChanged.emit(selected);
    });
  }

  /**
   * Reads into the editor the caret a click in the words has just put down, as the click ends.
   *
   * The browser moves its caret on the press, but ProseMirror learns of it from `selectionchange`, which Chrome fires
   * a task later - and ignores once the editor has lost the focus. A press on a Chords panel cell straight after the
   * click can take the focus in between, and the chord then goes to the caret before the click. So the browser's
   * caret is read here, at `mouseup`, while the editor still has the focus; ProseMirror's own reading a moment later
   * finds the state already there and changes nothing.
   *
   * At the end of a click and not as the focus leaves: a keystroke's text can be in the browser's DOM before
   * ProseMirror has read it, and a caret read then would be ahead of the document - but a click types nothing. A press
   * on a chord's name never gets here (`ChordView` keeps its own events), and a browser selection anywhere but in a
   * line of words is left alone.
   */
  private catchUpCaret(view: EditorView): void {
    const state = view.state;
    const dom = view.dom.ownerDocument.getSelection();
    if (dom === null) return;
    const { anchorNode, anchorOffset, focusNode, focusOffset } = dom;
    if (anchorNode === null || focusNode === null) return;
    if (!view.dom.contains(anchorNode) || !view.dom.contains(focusNode)) return;

    let anchor: number;
    let head: number;
    try {
      anchor = view.posAtDOM(anchorNode, anchorOffset);
      head = view.posAtDOM(focusNode, focusOffset);
    } catch {
      // A node ProseMirror does not map (a chord name's own text): nothing to read.
      return;
    }
    if (anchor === state.selection.anchor && head === state.selection.head) return;
    const $anchor = state.doc.resolve(anchor);
    const $head = state.doc.resolve(head);
    if (!$anchor.parent.inlineContent || !$head.parent.inlineContent) return;
    this.dispatch(state.tr.setSelection(TextSelection.between($anchor, $head)));
  }
```

```ts
/**
 * One of a key's own chords at a given height: the degree that builds it, and
 * the three ways of writing it that a `ChordOption` carries.
 *
 * The degree is the whole `ChordDegree` a slot would store rather than an
 * index, because it is what a caller places: the progression palette appends
 * its index through `createDegreeSlot`, and the song sheet's Chords tab writes
 * the whole of it into a chord atom (`chordSlotOf`).
 */
export interface DiatonicChord {
  /** `quality: null` - the key's own chord - at the height asked for, unaltered. */
  degree: ChordDegree;
  /** `vi`, `V7`, `viiø7`. */
  numeral: string;
  /** `A min`, `G7` - `chordName` style, as the palette prints. */
  name: string;
  /** `A minor`. */
  spoken: string;
}

/**
 * A key's own seven chords at `extent`: its triads at 3, its sevenths at 7 -
 * each degree's stack of thirds through the scale, which is what `quality:
 * null` builds.
 *
 * **The diatonic row, which the vocabulary above used not to have.** The
 * progression palette built its seven buttons itself, and the song sheet's
 * Chords tab needs the same seven and the same seven again at a seventh's
 * height. Built once here so the two cannot come to different conclusions
 * about a key's chords: the root is `chordRootName`'s - spelled on the degree's
 * own letter, so F locrian's third degree is `Ab` and not the `G#` a six-sharp
 * signature would give - and the chord is `effectiveChord`'s, the identity the
 * strip card and the fretboard read. The name and numeral are written from
 * those two by the functions every other option here uses.
 *
 * **Unaltered and unoverridden.** `alter` 0 and `quality` null are what make
 * them the key's own: the accidental and the shape are what the borrowed row
 * carries, so a diatonic chord written with either would be a borrowed one by
 * another name. The fields a button does not choose are what a fresh slot
 * carries (`optionDegree`).
 *
 * A scale that cannot stack thirds gives none, on the bargain `chordVocabulary`
 * makes: an empty row rather than a throw three layers down.
 */
export function diatonicChordsOf(
  key: ProgressionKey,
  scaleIntervals: readonly number[],
  extent: ChordExtent
): DiatonicChord[] {
  if (!isHeptatonic(scaleIntervals)) return [];

  return scaleIntervals.map((_, index) => {
    const degree = optionDegree(index, 0, null, extent);
    const chord = effectiveChord(scaleIntervals, degree);
    const root = chordRootName(key, scaleIntervals, degree);
    return {
      degree,
      numeral: romanNumeral(index, degree.alter, chord),
      name: chordName(root, chord),
      spoken: spokenChordName(root, chord)
    };
  });
}
```

<!-- apply: create client/src/app/services/song-palette.ts -->
```ts
import type { ChordDegree, ProgressionKey } from '../models/progression.model';
import { ChordExtent, effectiveChord, isHeptatonic } from './progression-harmony';
import { ChordOption, chordVocabulary, diatonicChordsOf, optionDegree } from './progression-vocabulary';
import { leadSheetNameOf, numeralOf } from './song-chord-names';
import { NO_CHORDS_KEY } from './song-commands';

/**
 * The song sheet's Chords tab, as data: four rows of chords a click places at the caret (design Part 2).
 *
 * Pure, with no Angular, on the `progression-vocabulary.ts` precedent, which it sits on. **Nothing here decides which
 * chords a key offers.** The two diatonic rows are `diatonicChordsOf` - the builder the progression palette's own
 * diatonic row uses - at a triad's height and at a seventh's; the borrowed and secondary rows are `chordVocabulary`'s,
 * chord for chord and in its order. What this module adds is how the *sheet* writes them: every option is named by
 * `leadSheetNameOf` and numbered by `numeralOf`, the two functions the sheet prints a chord atom with
 * (`chordLabelOf`), so a cell and the chord it places read the same - `Am` over `vi`, never the palette's `A min`.
 *
 * ## The secondary dominants' two numerals
 *
 * A secondary dominant has two: what it *does*, `V/ii`, and where it *is* in the key, `VI7`. The sheet can only print
 * the second - a chord atom stores a degree, not the chord it leads to, so there is no target to write a slash
 * against - and a cell must number its chord as the sheet will. So `numeral` is the sheet's, and the slash numeral the
 * vocabulary writes is kept beside it as the option's `role`, which the panel shows under the chord: the row is
 * *about* what each chord leads to, and losing that would leave five chords with no reason to be together.
 */

/** One chord a cell places: the degree a chord atom will store, and how the sheet writes it. */
export interface SongPaletteOption {
  /** Placed whole by `chordSlotOf`: its shape, height and accidental, root position, no suspension. */
  readonly degree: ChordDegree;
  /** As the sheet prints it with names showing: `Am`, `Bb`, `Bø7`. */
  readonly name: string;
  /** As the sheet prints it with numerals showing: `vi`, `♭VII`, `viiø7`. */
  readonly numeral: string;
  /** For a label that is heard: `A minor`; a secondary dominant adds what it leads to. */
  readonly spoken: string;
  /** A secondary dominant's function, `V/ii`; null in the other rows. See the header. */
  readonly role: string | null;
}

/** The four rows, in the order the panel lays them out. */
export interface SongPaletteRows {
  readonly triads: readonly SongPaletteOption[];
  readonly sevenths: readonly SongPaletteOption[];
  readonly borrowed: readonly SongPaletteOption[];
  readonly secondary: readonly SongPaletteOption[];
}

/** A key's palette, or why it has none. */
export type SongPalette = { kind: 'rows'; rows: SongPaletteRows } | { kind: 'refused'; reason: string };

const TRIAD: ChordExtent = 3;
const SEVENTH: ChordExtent = 7;

/**
 * Steps up the scale from a secondary dominant's degree to the degree it leads to: a fifth down is four steps down,
 * which in seven is three up. The inverse of the vocabulary's `target + 4` (`secondary` in
 * `progression-vocabulary.ts`).
 */
const STEPS_TO_TARGET = 3;

/**
 * A key's four rows, or a refusal when its scale cannot build chords.
 *
 * `scaleIntervals` is the key's scale as `ProgressionKeyContext.chordScaleFor` gives it, so the page hands that
 * answer straight over: null - an id the app does not know, a scale with no thirds to stack - and a scale that is not
 * heptatonic are both refused, with the sentence the song's commands refuse a chord with (`NO_CHORDS_KEY`), because
 * it is the same fact. The song's key control offers only scales that can build chords, so the refusal is for a song
 * stored by something else.
 */
export function songPaletteOf(key: ProgressionKey, scaleIntervals: readonly number[] | null): SongPalette {
  if (scaleIntervals === null || !isHeptatonic(scaleIntervals)) return { kind: 'refused', reason: NO_CHORDS_KEY };

  const option = (degree: ChordDegree, spoken: string, role: string | null = null): SongPaletteOption => ({
    degree,
    name: leadSheetNameOf(degree, key, scaleIntervals),
    numeral: numeralOf(degree, scaleIntervals),
    spoken,
    role
  });
  const fromVocabulary = (chord: ChordOption): ChordDegree =>
    optionDegree(chord.degree, chord.alter, chord.quality, chord.extent);

  const triads = diatonicChordsOf(key, scaleIntervals, TRIAD);
  const vocabulary = chordVocabulary(key, scaleIntervals, null);

  return {
    kind: 'rows',
    rows: {
      triads: triads.map(chord => option(chord.degree, chord.spoken)),
      sevenths: diatonicChordsOf(key, scaleIntervals, SEVENTH).map(chord => option(chord.degree, chord.spoken)),
      borrowed: vocabulary.borrowed.map(chord => option(fromVocabulary(chord), chord.spoken)),
      // Its target is one of the key's own triads - the vocabulary offers a dominant only for a degree whose triad is
      // major or minor - so the triads row already holds how to say it.
      secondary: vocabulary.secondary.map(chord => {
        const target = triads[(chord.degree + STEPS_TO_TARGET) % triads.length];
        return option(fromVocabulary(chord), `${chord.spoken}, leading to ${target.spoken}`, chord.numeral);
      })
    }
  };
}

/**
 * Whether two degrees build the same chord in a scale: the same root - degree and accidental - and the same stack
 * over it. Which cell the chord selected on the sheet is.
 *
 * **The chord built, not the fields stored.** A chord typed `Bb` and the borrowed `♭VII` cell may differ in whether
 * `quality` is pinned, and a placed triad stores `quality: null` where the vocabulary's options name theirs; both build
 * the same notes and the sheet prints the same name, so they are the same chord. The stack is `effectiveChord`'s - the
 * identity the sheet names a chord from - so height counts (`G` is not `G7`) and the suspension and pinned extensions
 * count, while the inversion and octave do not: `C/E` is still the `C` cell, as it is still `I` on the sheet.
 *
 * `scaleIntervals` must be heptatonic, as for every chord on the sheet.
 */
export function isSameChord(a: ChordDegree, b: ChordDegree, scaleIntervals: readonly number[]): boolean {
  if (a.degree !== b.degree || a.alter !== b.alter) return false;
  const first = effectiveChord(scaleIntervals, a);
  const second = effectiveChord(scaleIntervals, b);
  return (
    first.suspension === second.suspension &&
    first.intervals.length === second.intervals.length &&
    first.intervals.every((interval, index) => interval === second.intervals[index])
  );
}
```

### Task E.2: Chord names on a line that wraps

The panel narrows the sheet, and a line of piled chords that wraps exposed the spacing: padding that
moves a chord to the next row changes which row it is measured on, so the pass oscillated, and wrapped rows had no room
for names. Rows are now spaced for names by the line height, and every measure starts each line from no padding, so it
is idempotent by construction.

```ts
          range.setStart(node, at);
          range.setEnd(node, at + 1);
          const box = range.getBoundingClientRect();
          if (box.width > 0) boxes.push(box);
        }
      }
      return boxes;
    }

    /** Every name that overlaps another name or a printed character, said as "Dm/Em" or "Am over 'h'". */
    function collisions(): string[] {
      const named = chordEls().map(el => ({ text: nameOf(el).textContent ?? '', box: nameOf(el).getBoundingClientRect() }));
      const letters = letterBoxes();
      const found: string[] = [];
      named.forEach((name, index) => {
        for (const other of named.slice(index + 1)) if (overlap(name.box, other.box)) found.push(`${name.text}/${other.text}`);
        if (letters.some(letter => overlap(name.box, letter))) found.push(`${name.text} over a letter`);
      });
      return found;
    }

    /** How many rows the chords sit on: their own boxes are the row of words they are in, letter or no letter after. */
    const chordRows = (): number => new Set(chordEls().map(el => Math.round(el.getBoundingClientRect().top))).size;

    /** Everything the measuring decides, as the padding it wrote and where each name ended up. */
    const layout = (): string[] =>
      chordEls().map(el => {
        const box = nameOf(el).getBoundingClientRect();
        return `${el.style.paddingLeft || '0'} @ ${box.left.toFixed(1)},${box.top.toFixed(1)}`;
      });

    /**
     * Waits for a resize to be measured: the sheet's `ResizeObserver` hears of it in the next frame, after this wait's
     * first frame callback, and measures in the frame after that, after its second - so it is done by the third.
     */
    const afterResize = (): Promise<void> =>
      new Promise(resolve =>
        requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(() => requestAnimationFrame(() => resolve())))
      );

    it('keeps each name over its own letter on every row of a line that wraps', () => {
      open(song(section('v1', 'Verse 1', wrapping())), 360);
      expect(chordRows()).toBeGreaterThan(1);

      for (const el of chordEls()) {
        const name = nameOf(el).getBoundingClientRect();
        const letter = letterAfter(el);
        expect(Math.abs(name.left - letter.left)).withContext(nameOf(el).textContent ?? '').toBeLessThan(1);
        expect(name.bottom).toBeLessThanOrEqual(letter.top + 1);
      }
    });

    it('keeps every name below the row of words above its own', () => {
      open(song(section('v1', 'Verse 1', wrapping(), piled())), 360);
      expect(chordRows()).toBeGreaterThan(2);
      const letters = letterBoxes();

      for (const el of chordEls()) {
        const row = el.getBoundingClientRect();
        // The bottom of the nearest row of characters above this chord's row: its line's row before, or the line or
        // section header above it.
        const above = Math.max(...letters.filter(letter => letter.bottom <= row.top + 1).map(letter => letter.bottom));
        expect(nameOf(el).getBoundingClientRect().top)
          .withContext(nameOf(el).textContent ?? '')
          .toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(above - 0.5);
      }
      expect(collisions()).toEqual([]);
    });

    it('sets chords piled at the end of a line side by side, onto the next row when they run out of room', () => {
      open(song(section('v1', 'Verse 1', piled())), 300);
      expect(chordRows()).toBe(2);
      expect(collisions()).toEqual([]);
    });

    it('measures the same layout every time it measures', () => {
      open(song(section('v1', 'Verse 1', wrapping(), piled())), 300);
      const first = layout();

      spaceChordNames(editor());
      expect(layout()).toEqual(first);
      spaceChordNames(editor());
      expect(layout()).toEqual(first);
      expect(collisions()).toEqual([]);
    });

    it('keeps the names apart through a resize, and lays them out as before when the width comes back', async () => {
      open(song(section('v1', 'Verse 1', wrapping(), piled())), 900);
      const wide = layout();
      expect(collisions()).toEqual([]);

      host.style.width = '300px';
      await afterResize();
      expect(chordRows()).toBeGreaterThan(3);
      expect(collisions()).toEqual([]);

      host.style.width = '900px';
      await afterResize();
      expect(layout()).toEqual(wide);
    });
  });
```

```ts
 * The atom is an empty inline `span` placed just before the letter, so it is zero wide and its left edge is that
 * letter's left edge. The name is absolutely positioned inside it, at its right edge and just above the text, so it
 * starts exactly where the letter starts and takes no room in the line.
 *
 * **A plain inline span, so it wraps with its letter.** An inline span is no place for a line to break: a chord inside
 * a word goes onto the next row with the word, and one at the start of a word goes with that word rather than staying
 * at the end of the row before. An `inline-block` would have been the obvious way to give a name a box of its own, but
 * a line may break on either side of one - `Wonder|ing` - so a chord would split the word it is in.
 *
 * **Every row keeps a band above it for names** - the first row of a line and every row it wraps onto, chords or
 * none - and it is the line's leading that keeps it (the sheet's SCSS), not padding above the line, which only its
 * first row would have. So a name on a wrapped row has the same room as one on a first row, and is never over the row
 * of words before it, with no measuring at all. The cost is height: a wrapped line's rows are spaced as far apart as
 * two lines are, chords on them or not, where the design (Part 2) pictured room only above a line.
 *
 * ## When two names would collide
 *
 * Two chords a letter or two apart would print their names on top of one another. The line widens instead, as the
 * design has it: the later chord's span gets left padding, which pushes it - and the letter after it - right until its
 * name clears the one before it. The name stays at the span's right edge, so it is still over its own letter, and
 * anywhere nothing collides the chords keep taking no width in the words. Chords piled on one letter, or after a
 * line's last word, are no special case: each is a chord whose name must clear the one before it, so their names sit
 * side by side in the order they come. The padding is measured, not computed from character counts, because names are
 * a proportional bold face over a monospace line and the lyric size is the viewer's to change; `chordSpacingPlugin`
 * measures after every update of the view, and the sheet again whenever it is resized or a font arrives.
 *
 * Widening a line can wrap it, which is what makes measuring it subtle: see `spaceChordNames`.
 */
```
