```ts
import { DestroyRef, ErrorHandler, Injectable, InjectionToken, inject } from '@angular/core';
import { takeUntilDestroyed } from '@angular/core/rxjs-interop';
import { Router } from '@angular/router';
import { BehaviorSubject, Observable, combineLatest, map } from 'rxjs';
import type { ProgressionDoc, ProgressionKey, ProgressionState } from '../models/progression.model';
import { SECTION_KINDS, SectionKind } from '../models/song.model';
import { errorOf } from './error-message';
import { requireUniqueSlotIds, settle } from './progression-edit';
import { ProgressionService } from './progression.service';

/**
 * Where an open link is kept across a reload: the tab's session storage, or null where the browser refuses it (a
 * locked-down private window), when the link lives in memory only. A spec hands in a map of its own, so nothing it
 * opens is left in the browser for the next spec to restore.
 */
export const PROGRESSION_HANDOFF_STORAGE = new InjectionToken<Storage | null>('PROGRESSION_HANDOFF_STORAGE', {
  providedIn: 'root',
  factory: () => {
    try {
      return window.sessionStorage;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }
});

/** The key the link is stored under, and the shape's version, so a later shape can tell an old record from its own. */
const STORAGE_KEY = 'progression-handoff';
const STORAGE_VERSION = 1;

/**
 * A section on its way out to the Progression page: what `sectionHandoffOf` (`song-progression-return.ts`) makes of
 * a song. Built on the song's side, so this service - which the Progression page loads - never imports ProseMirror.
 */
export interface SectionHandoff {
  songId: string;
  /** As the banner names it: the song's title, or "Untitled song". */
  songTitle: string;
  sectionId: string;
  sectionLabel: string;
  sectionKind: SectionKind;
  /** The section's derived progression (`sectionProgressionOf`): its id is the section's. */
  progression: ProgressionDoc;
}

/** The one section out on the Progression page, and what to put back when it comes home. */
export interface ProgressionLink {
  songId: string;
  songTitle: string;
  sectionId: string;
  sectionLabel: string;
  sectionKind: SectionKind;
  /**
   * The section's progression as the Progression page's store published it on the way out. Its `revision` is the
   * sent revision - the store re-issues revisions on every commit, so the document open there has moved off it
   * exactly when something was edited - and its slots are the base the song's merge compares against.
   */
  sent: ProgressionDoc;
  /** The user's own progression, set aside to make room for the section, and put back when it comes home. */
  previous: ProgressionDoc;
  /** Whether `previous` had unsaved changes when it was set aside, so it is put back as the user had it. */
  previousDirty: boolean;
  /** Whether the circle of fifths names a key other than the song's, which the banner then explains. */
  keyHeld: boolean;
}

/** A section's progression handed back to its song, waiting for the song's page to take it. */
export interface ProgressionReturn {
  songId: string;
  sectionId: string;
  sectionLabel: string;
  sectionKind: SectionKind;
  sent: ProgressionDoc;
  returned: ProgressionDoc;
}

/** What the Progression page's banner shows, while a link's section is the progression open there. */
export interface HandoffBanner {
  sectionLabel: string;
  songTitle: string;
  /** The song's key, which holds while the section is open (see `declineKey`). */
  key: ProgressionKey;
  /** The scale the key names, as the page's state resolved it, for saying the key in words. */
  scaleName: string | null;
  keyHeld: boolean;
}

/** What is kept in session storage. */
interface StoredHandoff {
  version: number;
  link: ProgressionLink | null;
  /** The latest document the link's progression has been on the Progression page: what a reload puts back there. */
  current: ProgressionDoc | null;
  returns: ProgressionReturn[];
}

/**
 * Open in Progression and back (brief decision 7): the one link between a song's section and the Progression page.
 *
 * **Going out** (`open`): the section's derived progression replaces the one on the Progression page, which is kept
 * to put back; the revision the store gives it is recorded; and the app goes there. The song's page saves itself
 * before it calls this, so the song it opens on return is the stored one.
 *
 * **There**, while the section's progression is the one open (`isLinked`, by id: a section's progression carries the
 * section's id), the page shows a banner (`banner$`) and does not take the circle of fifths' key (`declineKey`): the
 * key is the song's, shared by every section, and set on the song.
 *
 * **Coming back** (`returnToSong`): the edited progression is captured, the user's own put back, and the app goes to
 * the song, whose page takes what came back (`takeReturn`) and applies it as one undo step
 * (`songAfterReturnOf`). With nothing edited there, coming back is a cancel (`cancel`): nothing is handed back, so
 * the song's page has nothing to apply and nothing to say.
 *
 * ## Nothing set aside is ever lost
 *
 * - **The user's own progression.** Kept on the link and put back on the way home - marked unsaved if it was unsaved
 *   when it was set aside, clean if it was clean, as the user had it. Opening a second section while one is out
 *   replaces the link but carries its `previous` over: the progression on the page then is the first section's, not
 *   the user's, and setting *that* aside would put the wrong one back.
 * - **A first section's edits, when a second is opened over them.** They are handed back to the first section's song
 *   as if Back to song had been pressed, and wait for its page to take them. Opening the section already out - edited
 *   or not - goes back to it as it is rather than deriving it afresh over the edits.
 * - **A reload.** The Progression page holds its document in memory only, so a reload would lose both the section's
 *   edits and the user's own progression set aside for them - and the latter would be the hand-off's doing. So the
 *   link, the section's latest progression and any return not yet taken are kept in **session storage** and restored
 *   when the app starts again: the Progression page comes back on the section, edits and all, still linked. Session
 *   rather than local storage, because a link belongs to one tab's trip out and back: a second tab restoring the same
 *   link would bring the same edits back twice.
 *
 * Root, as `ProgressionService` is: the link has to outlive both pages it connects.
 */
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class ProgressionHandoffService {
  private readonly progression = inject(ProgressionService);
  private readonly router = inject(Router);
  private readonly errors = inject(ErrorHandler);
  private readonly storage = inject(PROGRESSION_HANDOFF_STORAGE);
  private readonly linkSubject = new BehaviorSubject<ProgressionLink | null>(null);
  /** Returns handed back and not yet taken by their song's page. */
  private returns: ProgressionReturn[] = [];
  /** The latest document the link's progression has been, for a reload to put back (see the class comment). */
  private current: ProgressionDoc | null = null;
  /** Whether the progression open now has unsaved changes: what `previousDirty` records. */
  private dirty = false;

  /**
   * The banner, while the link's section is the progression open on the Progression page; null otherwise - with no
   * link, and also while the user has undone back past the hand-off to their own progression there.
   */
  readonly banner$: Observable<HandoffBanner | null>;

  constructor() {
    this.restore();

    const state$ = this.progression.getState();
    state$.pipe(takeUntilDestroyed(inject(DestroyRef))).subscribe(state => this.follow(state));
    this.banner$ = combineLatest([this.linkSubject, state$]).pipe(map(([link, state]) => bannerOf(link, state)));
  }

  /** The section out on the Progression page, or null. */
  get link(): ProgressionLink | null {
    return this.linkSubject.getValue();
  }

  /** Whether `doc` is the progression of the section out on the Progression page. */
  isLinked(doc: ProgressionDoc): boolean {
    return this.link?.sent.id === doc.id;
  }

  /**
   * Sends `section` to the Progression page, setting aside the progression there, and goes there. See the class
   * comment for a second open and for opening the section already out.
   */
  open(section: SectionHandoff): void {
    const link = this.link;
    const open = this.progression.doc;
    const linked = link !== null && this.isLinked(open);

    if (linked && link.songId === section.songId && link.sectionId === section.sectionId) {
      void this.go(['/progression']);
      return;
    }
    if (linked && open.revision !== link.sent.revision) this.returns.push(returnOf(link, open));

    const previous = linked ? link.previous : open;
    const previousDirty = linked ? link.previousDirty : this.dirty;
    // Clean: the section's progression is the song's, saved with it, so nothing about it is unsaved yet.
    this.progression.replaceDocument(section.progression, true);
    const sent = this.progression.doc;
    this.current = sent;
    this.linkSubject.next({
      songId: section.songId,
      songTitle: section.songTitle,
      sectionId: section.sectionId,
      sectionLabel: section.sectionLabel,
      sectionKind: section.sectionKind,
      sent,
      previous,
      previousDirty,
      keyHeld: false
    });
    this.save();
    void this.go(['/progression']);
  }

  /**
   * Back to song: hands the section's progression back to its song if anything was edited there, puts the user's own
   * progression back, and goes to the song. False, doing nothing, while the progression open is not the section's.
   */
  returnToSong(): Promise<boolean> {
    return this.close(true);
  }

  /** Goes back to the song without the edits made there, putting the user's own progression back. */
  cancel(): Promise<boolean> {
    return this.close(false);
  }

  /** The returns waiting for the song `songId`, in the order they were handed back; taking them clears them. */
  takeReturn(songId: string): ProgressionReturn[] {
    const taken = this.returns.filter(back => back.songId === songId);
    if (taken.length === 0) return [];
    this.returns = this.returns.filter(back => back.songId !== songId);
    this.save();
    return taken;
  }

  /**
   * The circle of fifths offering `offered` as the key of the progression `open`: declined, answering true, while
   * `open` is a section's progression, whose key is the song's (the caller must then not re-key it). The banner is
   * told whether the circle's key differs from the song's, so it can say why it was not taken. False for any other
   * progression, which takes the circle's key as always.
   */
  declineKey(open: ProgressionDoc, offered: ProgressionKey): boolean {
    const link = this.link;
    if (link === null || !this.isLinked(open)) return false;
    const keyHeld =
      offered.tonic !== open.key.tonic ||
      offered.scaleId !== open.key.scaleId ||
      offered.preferSharps !== open.key.preferSharps;
    if (keyHeld !== link.keyHeld) {
      this.linkSubject.next({ ...link, keyHeld });
      this.save();
    }
    return true;
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // The way home
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  /** Ends the link, handing the section's edits back when `keep` and there are any, and goes to its song. */
  private close(keep: boolean): Promise<boolean> {
    const link = this.link;
    const open = this.progression.doc;
    if (link === null || !this.isLinked(open)) return Promise.resolve(false);

    if (keep && open.revision !== link.sent.revision) this.returns.push(returnOf(link, open));
    // The link goes first, so the publish below is not followed as the section's latest.
    this.linkSubject.next(null);
    this.current = null;
    this.progression.replaceDocument(link.previous, !link.previousDirty);
    this.save();
    return this.go(['/songs', link.songId]);
  }

  /** Navigates, reporting a navigation that throws rather than leaving it unhandled. */
  private go(commands: string[]): Promise<boolean> {
    return this.router.navigate(commands).catch((error: unknown) => {
      this.errors.handleError(errorOf(error));
      return false;
    });
  }

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  // Following the page, and the reload
  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  /** Keeps the section's latest progression for a reload, and whether the page's progression is unsaved. */
  private follow(state: ProgressionState): void {
    this.dirty = state.isDirty;
    if (this.link === null || !this.isLinked(state.doc) || state.doc === this.current) return;
    this.current = state.doc;
    this.save();
  }

  /** Writes the link, the section's latest progression and the waiting returns to storage, or clears it when empty. */
  private save(): void {
    const storage = this.storage;
    if (storage === null) return;
    try {
      if (this.link === null && this.returns.length === 0) {
        storage.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
        return;
      }
      const stored: StoredHandoff = {
        version: STORAGE_VERSION,
        link: this.link,
        current: this.current,
        returns: this.returns
      };
      storage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(stored));
    } catch (error) {
      // A full or refused storage: the link still works in memory, it just would not survive a reload.
      this.errors.handleError(errorOf(error));
    }
  }

  /**
   * Picks up what a reload left in storage: the waiting returns, and the link with its section's latest progression,
   * which goes back on the Progression page as it was.
   *
   * The section's progression is put back only over the store's untouched starting document (revision 0, before any
   * commit). This service is made by the first page that needs it - the Progression page makes it before it can edit
   * anything - so that is always the case after a reload; were it not, the progression there would be the user's own
   * work, which is not to be written over. The section's edits are then handed back to its song instead.
   *
   * A record that cannot be read is reported and dropped: it is this service's own writing, so it is damaged, not
   * the user's, and keeping it would fail the same way on every start.
   */
  private restore(): void {
    const storage = this.storage;
    if (storage === null) return;
    let stored: StoredHandoff | null;
    try {
      stored = storedHandoffOf(storage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY));
    } catch (error) {
      this.errors.handleError(errorOf(error));
      this.removeStored();
      return;
    }
    if (stored === null) return;

    this.returns = stored.returns;
    const link = stored.link;
    if (link !== null) {
      const doc = stored.current ?? link.sent;
      const edited = doc.revision !== link.sent.revision;
      if (this.progression.doc.revision !== 0) {
        if (edited) this.returns.push(returnOf(link, doc));
      } else {
        this.progression.replaceDocument(doc, !edited);
        this.current = this.progression.doc;
        // Re-issued on the way in (`replaceDocument`), so an unedited progression is re-sent at its new revision to
        // keep reading as unedited; an edited one keeps the old sent revision, which it has moved off.
        this.linkSubject.next(edited ? link : { ...link, sent: this.current });
      }
    }
    this.save();
  }

  private removeStored(): void {
    try {
      this.storage?.removeItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    } catch {
      // Nothing more to do: a storage that refuses a remove has nothing this service can clear.
    }
  }
}

/** The link's section, handed back as `returned`. */
function returnOf(link: ProgressionLink, returned: ProgressionDoc): ProgressionReturn {
  return {
    songId: link.songId,
    sectionId: link.sectionId,
    sectionLabel: link.sectionLabel,
    sectionKind: link.sectionKind,
    sent: link.sent,
    returned
  };
}

function bannerOf(link: ProgressionLink | null, state: ProgressionState): HandoffBanner | null {
  if (link === null || link.sent.id !== state.doc.id) return null;
  return {
    sectionLabel: link.sectionLabel,
    songTitle: link.songTitle,
    key: state.doc.key,
    scaleName: state.keyScale?.name ?? null,
    keyHeld: link.keyHeld
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Reading storage
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** The stored hand-off in `text`, null when there is none, or a throw naming what is wrong with it. */
function storedHandoffOf(text: string | null): StoredHandoff | null {
  if (text === null) return null;
  const value = record(JSON.parse(text), 'The stored hand-off');
  if (value['version'] !== STORAGE_VERSION) {
    throw new Error(`The stored hand-off is version ${String(value['version'])}.`);
  }
  const returns = value['returns'];
  if (!Array.isArray(returns)) throw new Error('The stored hand-off has no list of returns.');
  return {
    version: STORAGE_VERSION,
    link: value['link'] === null ? null : linkOf(value['link']),
    current: value['current'] === null ? null : progressionOf(value['current']),
    returns: returns.map(returnFrom)
  };
}

function linkOf(value: unknown): ProgressionLink {
  const link = record(value, 'The stored link');
  if (typeof link['previousDirty'] !== 'boolean' || typeof link['keyHeld'] !== 'boolean') {
    throw new Error('The stored link is missing its flags.');
  }
  return {
    ...sectionFieldsOf(link, 'The stored link'),
    songTitle: text(link, 'songTitle', 'The stored link'),
    sent: progressionOf(link['sent']),
    previous: progressionOf(link['previous']),
    previousDirty: link['previousDirty'],
    keyHeld: link['keyHeld']
  };
}

function returnFrom(value: unknown): ProgressionReturn {
  const back = record(value, 'A stored return');
  return {
    ...sectionFieldsOf(back, 'A stored return'),
    sent: progressionOf(back['sent']),
    returned: progressionOf(back['returned'])
  };
}

function sectionFieldsOf(
  value: Record<string, unknown>,
  subject: string
): Pick<ProgressionLink, 'songId' | 'sectionId' | 'sectionLabel' | 'sectionKind'> {
  const kind = value['sectionKind'];
  if (!SECTION_KINDS.includes(kind as SectionKind)) throw new Error(`${subject} has no section kind.`);
  return {
    songId: text(value, 'songId', subject),
    sectionId: text(value, 'sectionId', subject),
    sectionLabel: text(value, 'sectionLabel', subject),
    sectionKind: kind as SectionKind
  };
}

/** A stored progression, through the store's own checks: settled, with unique slot ids. Throws when it fails them. */
function progressionOf(value: unknown): ProgressionDoc {
  const doc = record(value, 'A stored progression') as unknown as ProgressionDoc;
  if (typeof doc.id !== 'string' || typeof doc.revision !== 'number' || !Array.isArray(doc.slots)) {
    throw new Error('A stored progression is not a progression.');
  }
  return settle(requireUniqueSlotIds(doc));
}

function record(value: unknown, subject: string): Record<string, unknown> {
  if (typeof value !== 'object' || value === null || Array.isArray(value)) {
    throw new Error(`${subject} is not a record.`);
  }
  return value as Record<string, unknown>;
}

function text(value: Record<string, unknown>, name: string, subject: string): string {
  const field = value[name];
  if (typeof field !== 'string') throw new Error(`${subject} has no ${name}.`);
  return field;
}
```

```ts
import { Node } from 'prosemirror-model';
import { TextSelection } from 'prosemirror-state';
import { Step, Transform } from 'prosemirror-transform';
import type { ChordSlot, ProgressionDoc } from '../models/progression.model';
import type { ChordAtomAttrs, SectionKind } from '../models/song.model';
import type { SectionHandoff } from './progression-handoff.service';
import { SongEdit, checkedChord, markSongCommand } from './song-commands';
import {
  ChordAt,
  SongSection,
  UNTITLED_SONG,
  atomAttrsOf,
  chordsOf,
  sectionProgressionOf,
  sectionsOf,
  songMetaOf
} from './song-document';
import { songSchema } from './song-schema';

/**
 * Open in Progression, the song's half (brief decision 7): what goes out to the Progression page, and what the song
 * makes of what comes back.
 *
 * Pure but for the fresh ids `addReturnedSection` draws. The page's half - which progression is open, and the way
 * there and back - is `ProgressionHandoffService`'s; this file is everything that reads or writes a song document,
 * kept here so that service never imports ProseMirror and the Progression page's chunk never loads it.
 *
 * ## Coming back is a three-way merge
 *
 * A section is out on the Progression page for as long as the user likes, and the sheet stays editable meanwhile -
 * the user can go back to the song by the nav, place a chord, change one, and go to the Progression page again. So
 * what comes back is not simply "the section now". Three versions are compared: the progression as it was **sent**
 * (the base), as it was **returned** (the Progression page's edits), and the section's atoms **now** (the sheet's).
 * Only what the Progression page changed is written, and only to what the sheet still has:
 *
 * - **a chord changed there** - its harmony, length, notes or ownership differ from the sent slot - is written over
 *   its atom, found by id. A chord it left as it was is not written at all, so an edit made on the sheet since the
 *   section went out is kept rather than overwritten by the stale copy the Progression page was holding;
 * - **a chord removed there** has its atom deleted, if the sheet still has it; its words stay;
 * - **a chord added there** has no word to sit on, so it goes at the end of the section's last line, in the
 *   progression's order, and a notice says how many - the user drags each onto its word;
 * - **a chord placed on the sheet since** was never sent, so the Progression page cannot have removed it: it stays;
 * - **a chord changed there but taken out of the section here meanwhile** stays out - the sheet's delete is the
 *   later word on it - and a notice says so rather than dropping the change unmentioned;
 * - **a reorder made there** cannot move the words, and the sheet's order is the lyrics' order, so it is not
 *   applied, and a notice says so;
 * - **the key, the tempo and the time signature are the song's**, shared by every section (design Part 1), so one
 *   section's progression cannot change them; a notice says which the Progression page changed and that they were
 *   not brought back.
 *
 * Everything lands as one transaction, so one undo step, built here as steps over the document it was worked out
 * from and applied by `applyReturn`. **Nothing is applied when the revision did not move**: the Progression page's
 * store issues a new revision on every commit, so an unmoved one is proof nothing was edited there.
 */

/** What the song makes of a progression coming back. See the file comment. */
export type SongAfterReturn =
  /**
   * The steps to apply, all over the document `songAfterReturnOf` was given, and what to tell the user. The steps
   * may be empty when there is only something to say (a reorder, a tempo).
   */
  | { kind: 'changes'; steps: readonly Step[]; notices: readonly string[] }
  /** Nothing was edited there, or nothing that differs from the song. */
  | { kind: 'unchanged' }
  /** What came back is not chords the song can hold; none of it is applied. */
  | { kind: 'refused'; reason: string }
  /**
   * The section is no longer in the song - deleted in another tab, or here and saved, while it was out. Nothing is
   * applied, and every chord that came back is handed over, checked, so the page can offer them a new section
   * (`addReturnedSection`) rather than dropping them.
   */
  | { kind: 'sectionGone'; chords: readonly ChordAtomAttrs[] };

const UNCHANGED: SongAfterReturn = { kind: 'unchanged' };
const REFUSED = "The Progression page's chords could not be brought back:";
const STALE_DOC = "The song changed before the Progression page's chords could be brought back.";
const REORDERED = 'The chords were reordered on the Progression page; on the sheet each keeps its place in the words.';

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Going out
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * What Open in Progression sends for the section `sectionId`: its derived progression (`sectionProgressionOf`) and
 * the names the Progression page's banner shows. Null when the song has no such section.
 */
export function sectionHandoffOf(songId: string, doc: Node, sectionId: string): SectionHandoff | null {
  const progression = sectionProgressionOf(doc, sectionId);
  const section = sectionsOf(doc).find(entry => entry.id === sectionId);
  if (progression === null || section === undefined) return null;
  const title = songMetaOf(doc).title.trim();
  return {
    songId,
    songTitle: title === '' ? UNTITLED_SONG : title,
    sectionId,
    sectionLabel: section.label,
    sectionKind: section.kind,
    progression
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Coming back
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * What the song `doc` makes of the progression `returned` for its section `sectionId`, sent as `sent`. See the file
 * comment for the rules.
 *
 * Every returned chord is checked by the schema's own rules (`checkedChord`) before anything is worked out, and one
 * the song could not hold refuses the whole return: a progression with a broken chord in it is not one to apply
 * half of.
 */
export function songAfterReturnOf(
  doc: Node,
  sectionId: string,
  returned: ProgressionDoc,
  sent: ProgressionDoc
): SongAfterReturn {
  if (returned.revision === sent.revision) return UNCHANGED;
  if (returned.id !== sectionId || sent.id !== sectionId) {
    return { kind: 'refused', reason: `${REFUSED} that progression is not this section's.` };
  }

  const checked = checkedChordsOf(returned);
  if (typeof checked === 'string') return { kind: 'refused', reason: `${REFUSED} ${checked}` };

  const section = sectionsOf(doc).find(entry => entry.id === sectionId);
  if (section === undefined) return { kind: 'sectionGone', chords: checked };

  const label = section.label;
  const sentById = new Map(sent.slots.map(slot => [slot.id, atomAttrsOf(slot)]));
  const returnedIds = new Set(checked.map(chord => chord.id));
  const atoms = chordsOf(section.node, section.pos);
  const atomById = new Map(atoms.map(atom => [atom.attrs.id, atom]));
  const tf = new Transform(doc);
  const notices: string[] = [];

  // Changed there: written over the atom, attribute by attribute. Attribute steps map no positions, so every
  // position read from `doc` stays good through them.
  let changed = 0;
  let outOfSection = 0;
  for (const chord of checked) {
    const base = sentById.get(chord.id);
    if (base === undefined || sameChord(chord, base)) continue;
    const atom = atomById.get(chord.id);
    if (atom === undefined) {
      outOfSection++;
    } else if (!sameChord(chord, atom.attrs)) {
      writeChord(tf, atom, chord);
      changed++;
    }
  }

  // Removed there: deleted from the end backwards, so each position is still the one read from `doc`.
  const removed = sent.slots
    .filter(slot => !returnedIds.has(slot.id))
    .map(slot => atomById.get(slot.id))
    .filter((atom): atom is ChordAt => atom !== undefined)
    .sort((a, b) => b.pos - a.pos);
  for (const atom of removed) tf.delete(atom.pos, atom.pos + 1);

  // Added there: at the end of the section's last line, through the deletes' mapping.
  const fresh = checked.filter(chord => !sentById.has(chord.id));
  if (fresh.length > 0) appendChords(tf, section, fresh);

  if (changed > 0 || removed.length > 0) notices.push(summaryOf(label, changed, removed.length));
  if (fresh.length > 0) {
    const one = fresh.length === 1;
    notices.push(
      `${chordsCount(fresh.length)} added on the Progression page ${one ? 'is' : 'are'} at the end of ` +
        `${label}'s last line; drag ${one ? 'it' : 'each'} onto its word.`
    );
  }
  if (outOfSection > 0) {
    notices.push(
      `${chordsCount(outOfSection)} changed on the Progression page had been taken out of ${label} here, so ` +
        `${outOfSection === 1 ? 'it stays' : 'they stay'} out.`
    );
  }
  if (reordered(sent, checked)) notices.push(REORDERED);
  const facts = songFactsChanged(sent, returned);
  if (facts !== null) {
    notices.push(
      `The ${facts} set on the Progression page ${facts.includes(' and ') ? 'were' : 'was'} not brought back: ` +
        "the song's own are set on the song."
    );
  }

  if (tf.steps.length === 0 && notices.length === 0) return UNCHANGED;
  return { kind: 'changes', steps: tf.steps, notices };
}

/**
 * The edit that applies a return's steps as one undo step. `doc` is the document they were worked out from: steps are
 * positions in it, so on any other document - the song changed between working them out and applying them - the edit
 * is refused rather than writing chords into the wrong places.
 */
export function applyReturn(doc: Node, steps: readonly Step[]): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    if (state.doc !== doc) return { kind: 'refused', reason: STALE_DOC };
    const tr = state.tr;
    for (const step of steps) {
      const result = tr.maybeStep(step);
      if (result.failed !== null) return { kind: 'refused', reason: `${REFUSED} ${result.failed}` };
    }
    return tr.docChanged ? { kind: 'edit', tr: markSongCommand(tr) } : { kind: 'unchanged' };
  };
}

/**
 * Puts `chords` - a return whose section had gone (`sectionGone`) - in a new section of `kind` called `label` at the
 * end of the song, on one line with no words, as one undo step, with the caret at the start of that line.
 *
 * **Fresh ids**, because they are copies now: the section they came from may yet come back - an undo in the tab that
 * deleted it - holding the originals under those ids, and the song's ids must stay unique (`songNodeOf`).
 */
export function addReturnedSection(label: string, kind: SectionKind, chords: readonly ChordAtomAttrs[]): SongEdit {
  return state => {
    const nodes: Node[] = [];
    for (const chord of chords) {
      const node = checkedChord({ ...chord, id: crypto.randomUUID() });
      if (typeof node === 'string') return { kind: 'refused', reason: `${REFUSED} ${node}` };
      nodes.push(node);
    }
    const section = songSchema.nodes.section.create({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), label, kind }, [
      songSchema.nodes.lyricLine.create(null, nodes)
    ]);
    const at = state.doc.content.size;
    const tr = state.tr.insert(at, section);
    // One into the section, one into its line.
    tr.setSelection(TextSelection.create(tr.doc, at + 2));
    return { kind: 'edit', tr: markSongCommand(tr) };
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The parts
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Every returned slot as a chord atom's attributes, checked by the schema, or the first reason one fails. */
function checkedChordsOf(returned: ProgressionDoc): ChordAtomAttrs[] | string {
  if (!Array.isArray(returned.slots)) return 'it has no chords.';
  const checked: ChordAtomAttrs[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  for (const slot of returned.slots as readonly ChordSlot[]) {
    let node: Node | string;
    try {
      node = checkedChord(atomAttrsOf(slot));
    } catch (error) {
      node = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
    }
    if (typeof node === 'string') return node;
    const attrs = node.attrs as ChordAtomAttrs;
    if (seen.has(attrs.id)) return `the chord ${attrs.id} is in it twice.`;
    seen.add(attrs.id);
    checked.push(attrs);
  }
  return checked;
}

/** The four attributes that make a chord, written where they differ from `atom`'s. Its id stays. */
function writeChord(tf: Transform, atom: ChordAt, chord: ChordAtomAttrs): void {
  for (const name of ['harmony', 'lengthBeats', 'notes', 'owned'] as const) {
    if (!sameValue(chord[name], atom.attrs[name])) tf.setNodeAttribute(atom.pos, name, chord[name]);
  }
}

/**
 * Puts `chords` at the end of `section`'s last line of lyrics, in order - after its last word, where a chord on a
 * held note already sits. A section with no line (only tab blocks and memos) is given one at its end to hold them.
 * `section`'s position is in the document `tf` started from, and is mapped through the steps already on it.
 */
function appendChords(tf: Transform, section: SongSection, chords: readonly ChordAtomAttrs[]): void {
  const nodes = chords.map(chord => songSchema.nodes.chord.create(chord));
  let lastLineEnd: number | null = null;
  // The section's content starts one past its own position, and a line's content one past the line's.
  let at = section.pos + 1;
  for (let index = 0; index < section.node.childCount; index++) {
    const child = section.node.child(index);
    if (child.type === songSchema.nodes.lyricLine) lastLineEnd = at + 1 + child.content.size;
    at += child.nodeSize;
  }
  if (lastLineEnd !== null) {
    tf.insert(tf.mapping.map(lastLineEnd), nodes);
  } else {
    const sectionEnd = section.pos + section.node.nodeSize - 1;
    tf.insert(tf.mapping.map(sectionEnd), songSchema.nodes.lyricLine.create(null, nodes));
  }
}

/** "Verse 1: 2 chords changed and 1 removed on the Progression page." */
function summaryOf(label: string, changed: number, removed: number): string {
  const parts: string[] = [];
  if (changed > 0) parts.push(`${chordsCount(changed)} changed`);
  if (removed > 0) parts.push(changed > 0 ? `${removed} removed` : `${chordsCount(removed)} removed`);
  return `${label}: ${parts.join(' and ')} on the Progression page.`;
}

function chordsCount(count: number): string {
  return `${count} chord${count === 1 ? '' : 's'}`;
}

/**
 * Whether the chords both sides still have came back in a different order from the one they went out in. Chords
 * added or removed there do not count: only a move does.
 */
function reordered(sent: ProgressionDoc, returned: readonly ChordAtomAttrs[]): boolean {
  const returnedIds = new Set(returned.map(chord => chord.id));
  const sentIds = new Set(sent.slots.map(slot => slot.id));
  const before = sent.slots.map(slot => slot.id).filter(id => returnedIds.has(id));
  const after = returned.map(chord => chord.id).filter(id => sentIds.has(id));
  return before.join('\n') !== after.join('\n');
}

/** "key", "tempo", "key and tempo", "key, tempo and time signature": the song's facts changed there, or null. */
function songFactsChanged(sent: ProgressionDoc, returned: ProgressionDoc): string | null {
  const facts: string[] = [];
  if (!sameValue(sent.key, returned.key)) facts.push('key');
  if (sent.tempo !== returned.tempo) facts.push('tempo');
  if (!sameValue(sent.timeSignature, returned.timeSignature)) facts.push('time signature');
  if (facts.length === 0) return null;
  return facts.length === 1 ? facts[0] : `${facts.slice(0, -1).join(', ')} and ${facts[facts.length - 1]}`;
}

/** Whether two chords are the same chord: harmony, length, notes and ownership. Not their ids. */
function sameChord(a: ChordAtomAttrs, b: ChordAtomAttrs): boolean {
  return sameValue([a.harmony, a.lengthBeats, a.notes, a.owned], [b.harmony, b.lengthBeats, b.notes, b.owned]);
}

/**
 * Two values compared as data, whatever order their keys were written in. A slot normalised by the progression
 * store and the same slot read off an atom can list a degree's fields in different orders; that is not a change.
 */
function sameValue(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  return JSON.stringify(canonical(a)) === JSON.stringify(canonical(b));
}

function canonical(value: unknown): unknown {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) return value.map(canonical);
  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object') return value;
  const record = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  return Object.fromEntries(
    Object.keys(record)
      .sort()
      .map(key => [key, canonical(record[key])])
  );
}
```

## Phase H: The caret

Word, line and selection motions across chords.

### Task H.1: The caret across chords

Beside a chord, ProseMirror took every modified arrow key to select the atom, so a word jump, a Shift
extension or a Mac's Alt jump stuck - and a second Alt+arrow moved the chord. A key handler steps the caret past the
chords first and declines the key, so the browser makes its own motion from there. Home, End and the vertical motions
were already native and are left so.

```ts
  });

  /**
   * Every other way a caret moves, beside chords: word jumps, Shift, Home and End, up and down.
   *
   * These go through ProseMirror's *whole* key handling, not just the plugins' `handleKeyDown`: a keydown event is
   * dispatched on the editor, so the view's own arrow handling runs after the plugins, as it does in the browser - and
   * that is where a chord was being selected. The view is attached to the page, as the sheet's is. A synthetic event
   * makes no native motion, so a key that is not taken (`preventDefault`) leaves the editor's selection where the
   * plugins put it, and the browser's own motion is what would happen next.
   */
  describe('caret motions beside a chord', () => {
    const KEY_CODES: Record<string, number> = {
      ArrowLeft: 37,
      ArrowUp: 38,
      ArrowRight: 39,
      ArrowDown: 40,
      Home: 36,
      End: 35,
      Delete: 46
    };

    interface Held {
      ctrl?: boolean;
      alt?: boolean;
      shift?: boolean;
      /** Ctrl, or Cmd on a Mac. */
      mod?: boolean;
    }

    const c = chord(0);
    const f = chord(3);
    const g = chord(4);
    // A chord at the start of the line, one mid-line, one after its last word.
    const doc = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line('one'), line(c, 'Wondering ', f, 'where', g)));
    const lineStart = before(doc, 'Wondering') - 1;
    const where = before(doc, 'where');
    const lineEnd = where + 'where'.length + 1;

    function attachedViewOf(start: Node, selection: (d: Node) => Selection): EditorView {
      const mount = document.body.appendChild(document.createElement('div'));
      view = new EditorView(mount, { state: EditorState.create({ doc: start, selection: selection(start), plugins: songEditorPlugins() }) });
      return view;
    }

    afterEach(() => view?.dom.parentElement?.remove());

    /** Sends a keydown through ProseMirror's whole key handling (see above); answers whether the key was taken. */
    function keydown(target: EditorView, key: string, held: Held = {}): boolean {
      const event = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {
        key,
        keyCode: KEY_CODES[key] ?? key.toUpperCase().charCodeAt(0),
        ctrlKey: (held.ctrl ?? false) || ((held.mod ?? false) && !MAC),
        metaKey: (held.mod ?? false) && MAC,
        altKey: held.alt ?? false,
        shiftKey: held.shift ?? false,
        bubbles: true,
        cancelable: true
      });
      target.dom.dispatchEvent(event);
      return event.defaultPrevented;
    }

    function textSelection(target: EditorView): { anchor: number; head: number } | string {
      const selection = target.state.selection;
      return selection instanceof TextSelection ? { anchor: selection.anchor, head: selection.head } : selection.toJSON()['type'];
    }

    const WORD_JUMPS: readonly Held[] = [{ ctrl: true }, { alt: true }];

      const jumps: [string, number, number][] = [
        ['ArrowRight', lineStart, lineStart + 1],
        ['ArrowRight', where - 1, where],
        ['ArrowLeft', where, where - 1]
      ];
      for (const held of WORD_JUMPS) {
        for (const [key, from, to] of jumps) {
          const editor = attachedViewOf(doc, caret(from));
          const context = `${JSON.stringify(held)} ${key} from ${from}`;

          expect(keydown(editor, key, held)).withContext(context).toBeFalse();
          expect(textSelection(editor)).withContext(context).toEqual({ anchor: to, head: to });
          editor.dom.parentElement?.remove();
          editor.destroy();
        }
      }
    });

    it('never select the chord on the way, so a second Alt+arrow cannot move it', () => {
      const editor = attachedViewOf(doc, caret(lineStart));

      keydown(editor, 'ArrowRight', { alt: true });

      expect(editor.state.doc.eq(doc)).toBeTrue();
    });

      const piled = song(section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(c, f, 'Wo')));
      const editor = attachedViewOf(piled, caret(2));

      expect(keydown(editor, 'ArrowRight', { ctrl: true })).toBeFalse();
      expect(textSelection(editor)).toEqual({ anchor: 4, head: 4 });

    it('pass the chords after a line\'s last word, leaving the browser to go on to the next line', () => {
      const editor = attachedViewOf(doc, caret(lineEnd - 1));

      expect(keydown(editor, 'ArrowRight', { ctrl: true })).toBeFalse();
      expect(textSelection(editor)).toEqual({ anchor: lineEnd, head: lineEnd });
    });

    it('extend a Shift selection over the chords beside its head, keeping its anchor, for the browser to extend on', () => {
      const extensions: [Held, string, { anchor: number; head: number }, number][] = [
        [{ shift: true }, 'ArrowRight', { anchor: lineStart, head: lineStart }, lineStart + 1],
        [{ shift: true }, 'ArrowLeft', { anchor: where + 3, head: where }, where - 1],
        [{ shift: true, ctrl: true }, 'ArrowRight', { anchor: where - 3, head: where - 1 }, where],
        [{ shift: true, alt: true }, 'ArrowLeft', { anchor: where + 3, head: where }, where - 1]

        expect(textSelection(editor)).withContext(context).toEqual({ anchor, head: to });
        editor.dom.parentElement?.remove();

      expect(keydown(selected, 'ArrowRight', { alt: true })).toBeTrue();

      selected.dom.parentElement?.remove();

            expect(textSelection(editor)).withContext(context).toEqual({ anchor: at, head: at });
            editor.dom.parentElement?.remove();
            editor.destroy();

        }
      }
    });

    it('delete a chord with a selection across it, as the letter under it goes too', () => {
      const editor = attachedViewOf(doc, d => TextSelection.create(d, where - 2, where + 1));

      expect(keydown(editor, 'Delete')).toBeTrue();

      expect(outlineOf(editor.state.doc)).toEqual(['Verse 1 (verse): one / *Wonderinghere*']);
    });

    it('make select all and a typed letter one fresh section holding the letter', () => {
      const twoSections = song(
        section('s1', 'Verse 1', line(c, 'one')),
        section('s2', 'Chorus', line('two ', f, 'three'))
      );
      const editor = attachedViewOf(twoSections, caret(3));

      expect(keydown(editor, 'a', { mod: true })).toBeTrue();
      expect(editor.state.selection).toEqual(jasmine.any(AllSelection));
      // A letter typed over a selection that is not text in one line is ProseMirror's to insert, on keypress.
      const typed = new KeyboardEvent('keypress', { key: 'x', charCode: 'x'.charCodeAt(0), bubbles: true, cancelable: true });
      editor.dom.dispatchEvent(typed);
```

```ts
}

/**
 * The selection a modified left (`-1`) or right (`1`) arrow should start
 * from: its head moved past every chord beside it in that direction - only
 * the head when `extend` (Shift), so the anchor stays; the caret itself
 * otherwise. Null when no chord is there, or for a selection that is not text:
 * a selected chord's keys are its own, and with words selected a word jump
 * collapses the selection, which is the browser's to do.
 */
function selectionPastChordsOf(state: EditorState, dir: -1 | 1, extend: boolean): TextSelection | null {
  const selection = state.selection;
  if (!(selection instanceof TextSelection) || (!extend && !selection.empty)) return null;
  const doc = state.doc;
  const beside = (pos: number): Node | null => (dir > 0 ? doc.resolve(pos).nodeAfter : doc.resolve(pos).nodeBefore);

  let head = selection.head;
  if (!isChord(beside(head))) return null;
  while (isChord(beside(head))) head += dir;
  return TextSelection.create(doc, extend ? selection.anchor : head, head);
}

/**
 * Moves the caret's head past the chords beside it before a modified left or
 * right arrow, and leaves the key itself to ProseMirror and the browser (see
 * the header).
 *
 * A `handleKeyDown` that changes the selection and still answers false, which
 * a keymap command must not do: false is what lets the key go on to
 * ProseMirror's own arrow handling - which, with no atom beside the caret
 * now, declines it - and then to the browser's word jump or extension, made
 * from the selection set here, because the view writes a dispatched
 * selection to the DOM before the key's default action runs. The plain
 * arrows are `stepPastChord`'s, which takes them; any modifier at all comes
 * here, Cmd on a Mac too, whose line-start and line-end jumps lose nothing by
 * starting past a chord.
 */
function passChordsPlugin(): Plugin {
  return new Plugin({
    props: {
      handleKeyDown: (view, event) => {
        const dir = event.key === 'ArrowLeft' ? -1 : event.key === 'ArrowRight' ? 1 : 0;
        if (dir === 0 || !(event.shiftKey || event.ctrlKey || event.altKey || event.metaKey)) return false;
        const next = selectionPastChordsOf(view.state, dir, event.shiftKey);
        if (next !== null) view.dispatch(view.state.tr.setSelection(next));
        return false;
      }
    }
  });
}
```

result in the design doc. **A step that cannot be performed is recorded as not performed, with the reason; it is never
recorded as passed.**
